zajjaj:37-37.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَكَفَّلَها زَكَرِيّا﴾. There is more than one way of reading this. Permissible are: ”وَكَفَّلَها زَكَرِيّاءَ“ with the long vowel (madd), ”كُلَّما دَخَلَ عَلَيْها زَكَرِيّاءُ“; and ”كَفَلَها زَكَرِيّا“ with the short form (qaṣr), ”كُلَّما دَخَلَ عَلَيْها زَكَرِيّا“ with the short form. In ”زَكَرِيّا“ there are three dialectal forms, which are the well-known and recognised ones: ”زَكَرِيّاءُ“ with the long vowel, and ”زَكَرِيّا“ with the short form — without tanwīn (nunation) in both cases — and ”زَكَرِيٌّ“, with the alif dropped, declinable (muʿrab) and with tanwīn. As for its not being declined fully (i.e. being a diptote), that is because at its end there is the alif of the feminine — in the long form the long feminine alif, and in the short form the short feminine alif. Some grammarians said: it is not fully declined because it is foreign (aʿjamī). But whatever contains the feminine alif is the same whether in Arabic or in foreign words, because what is foreign is fully declined when indefinite, whereas it is not permissible for nouns containing the feminine alif to be fully declined, whether definite or indefinite, because they contain the mark of the feminine, and because it is formed together with the noun as one single form; so it differs from the feminine hāʾ (tāʾ marbūṭa). For that reason it is not fully declined even when indefinite.
It is also permissible to read ”كَفَّلَها زَكَرِيّاءَ“, with ”زَكَرِيّاءَ“ in the accusative, and in this position ”زَكَرِيّا“ with the short form is also permissible. Whoever read ”كَفَلَها زَكَرِيّاءُ“ put it in the nominative by its verb (as its fāʿil (agent)); the meaning, according to what Abū ʿUbayda mentioned, is: he guaranteed her (ḍaminahā), and its meaning here is: he undertook responsibility for her affairs. Whoever read ”كَفَّلَها زَكَرِيّاءَ“ in the accusative, the meaning is: "And Allah made Zakariyyā her guardian." As for the third dialectal form, it is not permissible in the Quran, because it contradicts the written text of the Muṣḥaf, though it is frequent in the speech of the Arabs.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿كُلَّما دَخَلَ عَلَيْها زَكَرِيّا المِحْرابَ﴾: the short and long forms in ”زَكَرِيّا“, and reading with both is widespread, as we have described. ”اَلْمِحْرابُ“ is the noblest of sitting places and the foremost among them. It has also been said that their places of worship were called ”اَلْمَحارِيبَ“. ”اَلْمِحْرابُ“ in the language is the high, noble place. The poet said:
رَبَّةُ مِحْرابٍ إذا جِئْتُها ∗∗∗ لَمْ ألْقَها أوْ أرْتَقِي سُلَّما
(The mistress of a lofty chamber: when I come to her, I do not meet her unless I climb a ladder.)
And from this is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَهَلْ أتاكَ نَبَأُ الخَصْمِ إذْ تَسَوَّرُوا المِحْرابَ﴾ [Ṣād: 21]. ”كُلَّما“ is put in the accusative by His saying ”وَجَدَ“, that is: he finds provision with her at every time he enters upon her in the miḥrāb. Thus ”ما“ together with ”دَخَلَ“ is equivalent to "the entering", i.e. "every time of entering".
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قالَ يا مَرْيَمُ أنّى لَكِ هَذا﴾, that is: from where do you have this? ﴿قالَتْ هو مِن عِنْدِ اللَّهِ﴾. Zakariyyā asked only about the provision because he feared that it might come to her from some source other than through him; so it became clear to him that it was from Allah. That is among the signs of Maryam. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿وَجَعَلْناها وابْنَها آيَةً لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 91]. Among her signs: she was the first woman accepted under a vow for the place of worship; among them: Allah brought ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) into being in her from a word which He cast to her; and among them: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, nourished her with provision from Himself which He did not convey by the hand of any of His servants. It has been said in the exegesis that she was never put to a breast. The meaning of ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ﴾ is: without stinting. And in ”حِسابٍ“, if you wish you pronounce the alif with fatḥa and keep it in the fatḥa direction, and if you wish you incline it (imāla) towards kasra because of the kasra of the ḥāʾ; that is frequent in the language of the Arabs.

zajjaj:38-38.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿هُنالِكَ دَعا زَكَرِيّا رَبَّهُ﴾. ”زَكَرِيّا“ with the long vowel and the short form, as we have described. The meaning: at that, Zakariyyā called upon his Lord, i.e. upon what he encountered of Maryam's affair; then he asked Allah to grant him good offspring. ﴿هُنالِكَ﴾ is in the position of the accusative, because it is a ẓarf (adverb) that applies to place and to states — states of time. The meaning is: in that place of time and of state, Zakariyyā called upon his Lord, just as you say: ”مِن هُنا قُلْتُ كَذا وكَذا“ ("from here I said such-and-such") and ”مِن هُنالِكَ قُلْتُ كَذا وكَذا“ ("from there I said such-and-such"), i.e. from that aspect and that direction; and this, in what is not a place, runs as a figure of speech. The kasra of the lām of ”هُنالِكَ“ occurs because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, since ”هُنالِكَ“ is a pointing to a distant place, or to one of the states of time whose relation is to place. He said ”طَيِّبَةً“ (feminine) following the word-form of ”ذُرِّيَّةً“. And ”هُنالِكَ“ need not be declined (made muʿrab) in the nominative or the genitive, because in pointing to place it is like the pointing in ”هَذا“ and ”هَذاكَ“ to all other things; so it resembles the particles that came for a meaning.

zajjaj:39-39.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَنادَتْهُ المَلائِكَةُ﴾, and ”فَناداهُ المَلائِكَةُ“: both ways are permissible, because a group takes the feminine designation, since its meaning is the meaning of "a group (jamāʿa)", and it is also permissible to express it with the masculine wording, just as one says ”جَمْعُ المَلائِكَةِ“ ("the gathering of the angels"). It is permissible to say ”نادَتْهُ المَلائِكَةُ“ ("the angels called him") although only Jibrāʾīl called him, because the meaning is: the call came to him from this genus — just as we say ”رَكِبَ فُلانٌ في السُّفُنِ“ ("so-and-so travelled in the ships") when he travelled in only one ship, meaning by that that his travelling was in this genus.
Permissible are ﴿أنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكَ﴾ and ”إنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكَ“, with ”إنَّ“ pronounced with fatḥa and with kasra. Whoever reads it with fatḥa, the meaning is: she called him with "that Allah gives you glad tidings", i.e. she called him with the glad tidings. Whoever reads it with kasra intends: the angels said: "Indeed Allah gives you glad tidings"; and ”إنَّ“ after (a verb of) saying is always with kasra.
In ”يُبَشِّرُكَ“ there are three dialectal forms: ”إنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكَ“ with fatḥa on the bāʾ and a doubled shīn, which is a very widespread reading; ”يَبْشُرُكَ“ with the bāʾ quiescent and ḍamma on the shīn; and Ḥumayd alone read ”يُبْشِرُكَ“ with ḍamma on the yāʾ, the bāʾ quiescent and kasra on the shīn. The meaning of ”يُبَشِّرُكَ“ and ”يَبْشُرُكَ“ is the giving of glad tidings, and the meaning of ”يُبْشِرُكَ“ is: He delights you and gladdens you. One says ”بَشَّرْتُ الرَّجُلَ، أُبَشِّرُهُ، وأبْشُرُهُ“ when you gladden him, and one says ”بَشُرَ الرَّجُلُ يَبْشُرُ“. Al-Akhfash, al-Kisāʾī and a group of grammarians recited:
وَإذا لَقِيتَ الباهِشِينَ إلى النَّدا ∗∗∗ غُبْرًا أكُفُّهُمُ بِقاعٍ مُمْحِلِ
فَأعِنْهم وابْشُرْ بِما بَشُرُوا بِهِ ∗∗∗ وإذا هُمُ نَزَلُوا بِضَنْكٍ فانْزِلِ
(When you meet those eager for generosity, their hands dusty, in a barren, drought-stricken plain, then help them and rejoice in what they rejoice in; and when they alight in hardship, alight with them.)
This is from ”بَشُرَ، يَبْشُرُ“ when one rejoices. The origin of all this is that a person's skin (basharat al-insān) expands at times of joy; and from this is their saying ”فُلانٌ يَلْقانِي بِبِشْرٍ“ ("so-and-so meets me with bishr"), i.e. with a cheerful face.
”يَحْيى“ is a name which Allah the Exalted gave him; He, Mighty and Majestic, took that upon Himself, and no one before ”يَحْيى“ was named ”يَحْيى“. ”يَحْيى“ is a diptote whether it is Arabic or foreign: if it is foreign, foreignness and definiteness are combined in it; and if it were Arabic, it would be a diptote because of its resemblance to the verb and because it is a definite proper name. ”مُصَدِّقًا“ is put in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The meaning of ﴿مُصَدِّقًا بِكَلِمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ is: he will confirm the matter of ʿĪsā, because following ʿĪsā was made obligatory upon Yaḥyā — even though Yaḥyā was older than ʿĪsā. As for the meaning of ”سَيِّدًا وحَصُورًا“: ”اَلسَّيِّدُ“ is the one who surpasses his people in goodness; and the meaning of ”حَصُورًا“ is: he does not approach women. The one who does not approach women was called ”حَصُورٌ“ only because he was withheld from what comes from men, just as it is said of the one to whom speech does not come easily: ”قَدْ حُصِرَ في مَنطِقِهِ“ ("he has become constrained in his speech"). The ḥaṣūr is also the one who does not spend on drinking companions, being among those on whom others are generous. The poet said:
وَشارِبٍ مُرْبِحٍ بِالكَأْسِ نادَمَنِي ∗∗∗ لا بِالحَصُورِ ولا فِيها بِسَوّارِ
(Many a drinker, generous with the cup, has kept me company — neither niggardly nor violent over it.)
It is also transmitted as ”وَلا فِيها بِسَآرِ“. That is: he kept me company while he was noble and spending on the drinking companions. The sawwār is the quarrelsome drunkard who assails (yusāwiru) his companion, i.e. leaps upon him; and the saʾʾār is the one who leaves a remainder in his vessel when he drinks. The ḥaṣūr is also the one who keeps a secret, i.e. confines the secret within himself. Jarīr said:
وَلَقَدْ تُسْقِطُنِي الوُشاةُ فَصادَفُوا ∗∗∗ حَصِرًا بِسِرِّكِ يا أُمَيْمُ ضَنِينا
(The slanderers have tried to trip me up, but they found me close-mouthed about your secret, O Umaym, and grudging of it.)
The ḥaṣīr is this woven mat on which one sits; it was called ”حَصِيرًا“ only because its parts are interlaced with one another in the weaving, i.e. one part is held against another. The prison is called ”اَلْحَصِيرُ“ because people are confined (yuḥṣarūn) in it. One says ”حَصَرْتُ الرَّجُلَ“ when you confine him, and ”أحْصَرَهُ المَرَضُ“ when illness prevents him from travelling. The ḥaṣīr is also the king. And the saying of Allah, Majestic and Exalted: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكافِرِينَ حَصِيرًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 8] means: a prison. One says ”أصابَ فُلانًا حَصَرٌ“ when his bowels are retained, and concerning urine one says ”أصابَهُ أسْرٌ“ when his urine is retained. The meaning of ﴿مِنَ الصّالِحِينَ﴾: the righteous one is he who renders to Allah what is due from him and renders to people their rights.

zajjaj:40-40.t:
His saying, Majestic and Exalted: ﴿قالَ رَبِّ أنّى يَكُونُ لِي غُلامٌ﴾, that is: how shall I have a boy? Al-Kumayt said:
أنّى ومِن أيْنَ آبَكَ الطَّرَبْ ∗∗∗ مِن حَيْثُ لا صَبْوَةٌ ولا لَعِبْ
(How, and from where, has rapture come back to you, when there is no youthful passion and no play?)
That is: how? and from where has rapture returned to you? One says ”غُلامٌ بَيِّنُ الغُلُومِيَّةِ، والغُلامِيَّةِ، والغُلُومَةِ“ ("a boy of evident boyhood").
His saying, Majestic and Exalted: ﴿وَقَدْ بَلَغَنِيَ الكِبَرُ﴾ has the meaning: I have reached old age; and in another place: ﴿وَقَدْ بَلَغْتُ مِنَ الكِبَرِ عِتِيًّا﴾ [Maryam: 8]. Everything that you have encountered and reached has also encountered you and reached you.
The meaning of ﴿كَذَلِكَ اللَّهُ يَفْعَلُ ما يَشاءُ﴾ is: like that Allah does what He wills. Zakariyyā asked only because he wished to know: would the child come to him while his wife was barren and he was aged, or would Allah put him in the state of one to whom children are born and put his wife likewise, or would the child come to them while they remained in the state with which a child does not occur? So Allah informed them both that this was easy for Him, just as He brought them into being when they had been nothing, and that He would give them the child while they were at this age.
Concerning ”عاقِرٌ“ (barren) one says: ”قَدْ عَقُرَتِ المَرْأةُ“ and ”عَقَرَتْ“, and she is ”عاقِرٌ“. This is evidence that ”عاقِرًا“ occurs by way of relation (nasab, i.e. "one possessing barrenness"), because for "faʿulat" the active participles are on the pattern ”فَعِيلَةٌ“, as in ”ظَرُفَتْ، فَهي ظَرِيفَةٌ“; ”عاقِرٌ“ is only "one possessed of barrenness (ʿuqr)". One says ”قَدْ عَقَرَ الرَّجُلُ، يَعْقِرُ عَقْرًا“ when speech fails him from fatigue and exhaustion. Al-ʿaqār is any property that has a root (i.e. real estate); it has also been said that date-palms specifically are called ”عَقارٌ“. ”عُقْرُ دارِ قَوْمٍ“ is the root of their residence on which they depend, so that when they move away from it in search of pasture, their return is to it. It is narrated from ʿAlī that he said: ”ما غُزِيَ قَوْمٌ في عُقْرِ دارِهِمْ إلّا ذُلُّوا“ ("No people were ever attacked in the heart of their home but they were humiliated"), i.e. they were not attacked in the place that is the root of their residence (without being humiliated).

zajjaj:41-41.t:
The meaning of ﴿رَبِّ اجْعَلْ لِي آيَةً﴾ is: a sign by which I will know the time at which You will grant him the boy [Translator's note: the text switches here from "me" to "him"]. ﴿قالَ آيَتُكَ ألا تُكَلِّمَ النّاسَ ثَلاثَةَ أيّامٍ إلا رَمْزًا﴾: that is, the sign of that is that your tongue will be held back from speech while you are healthy and sound. And He said in another place: ﴿آيَتُكَ ألا تُكَلِّمَ النّاسَ ثَلاثَ لَيالٍ سَوِيًّا﴾ [Maryam: 10], i.e. while you are sound. The meaning of ”اَلرَّمْزُ“ is moving the lips with the utterance without making it clear by voice; it is only a gesture with the lips. It has also been said that ramz is a gesture with the eyes, or the eyebrows, and the mouth. ”اَلرَّمْزُ“ in the language is anything by which you point to an explanation through an utterance, i.e. with whatever you gesture — with the mouth, the hand, or the eyes. ”اَلرَّمْزُ“ and ”اَلتَّرَمُّزُ“ in the language mean motion and moving.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَسَبِّحْ بِالعَشِيِّ والإبْكارِ﴾: it has been said that ”سَبِّحْ“ means ”صَلِّ“ ("pray"). One says ”فَرَغْتُ مِن سَبْحَتِي“, i.e. from my prayer. Prayer was called ”تَسْبِيحًا“ only because tasbīḥ is magnifying Allah and declaring Him free of evil; in prayer Allah is declared One, praised, and described with everything that declares Him free of evil — for that reason the prayer was called ”اَلسَّبْحَةَ“. Concerning ”اَلْإبْكارُ“ one says: ”أبْكَرَ الرَّجُلُ، يُبْكِرُ، إبْكارًا“, and ”بَكَّرَ، يُبَكِّرُ، تَبْكِيرًا“, and ”بَكَرَ يَبْكُرُ“, of anything in which one is early. People's saying about fruits that come early, ”قَدْ هَرِفَ“, is an error; it is only a word of tardiness. The Arabs only say in such a case ”قَدْ بَكَّرَ“, and what comes early of it is called ”اَلْباكُورَةَ“.

zajjaj:42-42.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإذْ قالَتِ المَلائِكَةُ يا مَرْيَمُ إنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفاكِ وطَهَّرَكِ﴾. The meaning of ”اِصْطَفاكِ“ is: He chose you. Concerning ”طَهَّرَكِ“ they said: He purified you from menstruation and postnatal bleeding. The meaning of ”طَهَّرَكِ“ — and Allah knows best — is: He made you pure from all impurities; however, the first has come in the exegesis. It has been said that the meaning of ”اصْطَفاكِ عَلى نِساءِ العالَمِينَ“ is: over the women of the people of her era; and it is possible that it is over the women of all the worlds, i.e. He chose you for ʿĪsā over the women of all the worlds, for the like of ʿĪsā was not produced from any woman among the women of the worlds.

zajjaj:43-43.t:
The meaning of ﴿اقْنُتِي لِرَبِّكِ﴾ is: worship Him with word and deed.
﴿واسْجُدِي وارْكَعِي﴾: concerning the meaning of rukūʿ (bowing) it has been said: prostration. The meaning is: bow and prostrate; however, the wāw, when mentioned, means combination, and there is no evidence in it that one of the two things comes before the other, because it signals combination and action, while the context (al-ḥāl) indicates the precedence of the one of the two that comes first.

zajjaj:44-44.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ذَلِكَ مِن أنْباءِ الغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ إلَيْكَ﴾, that is: the reports which We have narrated to you concerning Zakariyyā, Yaḥyā, Maryam and ʿĪsā are among the tidings of the unseen, i.e. among reports of what was absent from you. In this is evidence establishing the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ, because he told of what is known only from a book or from revelation, and they are agreed that the Prophet ﷺ was unlettered; so his informing them of the reports that are in their books, as they truly are, without reading books, is evidence that he is a prophet and that Allah revealed them to him. The meaning of ﴿إذْ يُلْقُونَ أقْلامَهم أيُّهم يَكْفُلُ مَرْيَمَ﴾ is: this too is among what you did not witness. The meaning of al-aqlām here is the divining arrows (qidāḥ): arrows on which they placed marks by which they would know which of them would take charge of Maryam, by way of casting lots. The arrow was called ”اَلْقَلَمُ“ only because it is pared (yuqlamu), i.e. shaved; everything from which you cut something piece after piece you have "qalamta" it. From that is ”اَلْقَلَمُ“ with which one writes; it was so named only because it is pared time after time. And from this is ”قَلَّمْتُ أظافِرِي“ ("I pared my nails").
The meaning of ﴿أيُّهم يَكْفُلُ مَرْيَمَ﴾ is: so that they might see which of them is entitled to the guardianship of Maryam, which is the guarantee of looking after her affairs. The meaning of ﴿لَدَيْهِمْ﴾ is: with them and in their presence. ﴿إذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ﴾: ”إذْ“ is put in the accusative by His saying ”وَما كُنْتَ لَدَيْهِمْ“, and the second ”إذْ“ is attached (muʿallaqa) to ”يَخْتَصِمُونَ“, i.e. "when they were disputing, when the angels said"; so ”إذْ“ is in the accusative by ”يَخْتَصِمُونَ“, and the meaning would be that they disputed on account of Maryam and ʿĪsā. It is also possible that the accusative of ”إذْ“ is on the basis of "and you were not with them when the angels said" — this too is among what he did not witness.

zajjaj:174-174.t: His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فانْقَلَبُوا بِنِعْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وفَضْلٍ﴾. The meaning is: they did not fear what they had been made to fear, and they went to the appointed meeting-place at which they had been promised [battle], and so they returned with a blessing (نِعْمَةٍ), that is, they returned as believers, their enemy having fled from them. It has been said in the exegesis (tafsīr) that they stayed three days and bought provisions of seasoning (أُدْمًا) and raisins, on which they made a profit. All of this is possible, except that their returning "with a blessing" is the blessing of faith and of victory over their enemy.

zajjaj:175-175.t: His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿إنَّما ذَلِكُمُ الشَّيْطانُ يُخَوِّفُ أوْلِياءَهُ﴾, that is: that frightening which took place was the doing of Satan, that is, it was his speech [put in the mouths] of those who were spreading fear. ﴿يُخَوِّفُ أوْلِياءَهُ﴾: the people of Arabic [grammar] said: its meaning is "he makes you fear his allies (يُخَوِّفُكم أوْلِياءَهُ)", that is, [makes you afraid] of his allies. The proof of this is His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَلا تَخافُوهم وخافُونِ إنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, that is: if you are believers in the truth, then I have informed you that I will grant you victory over them, so fear has fallen away from you. Some of them said: ”يُخَوِّفُ أوْلِياءَهُ“ means: only the hypocrites, and those whose faith has no reality, are afraid; ﴿فَلا تَخافُوهُمْ﴾, that is: do not fear the polytheists.

zajjaj:178-178.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَلا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أنَّما نُمْلِي لَهم خَيْرٌ لأنْفُسِهِمْ﴾. It has been read: ”وَلا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أنَّما نُمْلِي لَهم خَيْرٌ“, and it has also been read: ”وَلا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إنَّما نُمْلِي“. The meaning of ”نُمْلِي لَهم“ is: We grant them respite. These are a people concerning whom Allah informed the Prophet ﷺ that they would never believe, and that their remaining [alive] only increases them in unbelief and sin.

As for the i'rab: Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: Whoever reads with the yāʾ, ”يَحْسَبَنَّ“, gives ”أنَّ“ a fatḥa, and it then stands in for the two objects, the noun and the predicate [of ḥasiba]; you say: ”حَسِبْتُ أنَّ زَيْدًا مُنْطَلِقٌ“ ("I reckoned that Zayd was departing"). The kasra [i.e. ”إنَّ“] is also valid with the yāʾ, though it is ugly: ”وَلا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إنَّما نُمْلِي لَهم“ with a kasra on ”إنَّ“. This is permissible despite its ugliness, because reckoning (al-ḥusbān) is not a real [physical] action, so its government is suspended with ”إنَّ“ just as it is suspended with the lām; you say: ”حَسِبْتُ لَعَبْدُ اللَّهِ مُنْطَلِقٌ“ ("I reckoned: ʿAbdullāh is indeed departing"), and likewise it may be allowed, though far-fetched: ”حَسِبْتُ إنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ مُنْطَلِقٌ“. Whoever reads ”وَلا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا“ [with the tāʾ] is not permitted — according to the Basrans — anything but a kasra on ”إنَّ“; the meaning is: "Do not reckon those who disbelieve [thus]: Our granting of respite is good for them," with ”إنَّ“ entering for emphasis. If you put a fatḥa on ”أنَّ“, the meaning becomes: ”وَلا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إمْلاءَنا...“ ("do not reckon those who disbelieve Our respite…").

Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: In my view, in this place it is permissible as a badal (substitute) for ”اَلَّذِينَ“; the meaning is: "Do not reckon Our granting respite to those who disbelieve to be good for them." A great many people have read it this way. An instance of this reading in poetry is the poet's saying:
؎فَما كانَ قَيْسٌ هُلْكُهُ هُلْكَ واحِدٍ ∗∗∗ ولَكِنَّهُ بُنْيانُ قَوْمٍ تَهَدَّما
(Qays — his perishing was not the perishing of a single man; rather it was the edifice of a whole people that collapsed.)
He made ”هُلْكُهُ“ a badal of ”قَيْسٌ“; the meaning is: "The perishing of Qays was not the perishing of a single man."

zajjaj:179-179.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿ما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيَذَرَ المُؤْمِنِينَ عَلى ما أنْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ حَتّى يَمِيزَ الخَبِيثَ مِنَ الطَّيِّبِ﴾. It is narrated in the exegesis that the unbelievers said to the Prophet ﷺ: "You tell us that a person is in the Fire, and then when he becomes one of the people of your religion, you say that he is one of the people of Paradise." So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that the ruling on whoever disbelieves is that it be said of him: he is one of the people of the Fire; and whoever believes is — as long as he believes, persists in his faith and performs what has been made obligatory upon him — one of the people of Paradise. And He made known that the believers, who are "the good" (الطَّيِّبُ), are distinguished from "the wicked" (الخَبِيثِ), that is, they are set apart pure.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيُطْلِعَكم عَلى الغَيْبِ﴾, that is: Allah was not going to inform you which of you would become a believer after his unbelief, because only the messengers are given knowledge of the unseen, in order to establish the proof that they are messengers and that what they have brought is from Allah. It has been said in the exegesis [that they said]: "What is the matter with us that we are not prophets?" So Allah made known that this belongs to Him, and that He chooses for His messages whom He wills.

zajjaj:180-180.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَلا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ بِما آتاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ هو خَيْرًا لَهُمْ﴾. By this He means the scholars of the Jews who withheld (بَخِلُوا) what Allah had given them of knowledge of the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ, and [who engaged in] opposition to him and enmity towards him. It has also been said that they are those who are miserly with wealth and so withhold the zakāt.

The people of Arabic [grammar] said: the meaning is: "Let not those who are miserly reckon the miserliness (البُخْلَ) — it is better for them," and ”يَبْخَلُونَ“ indicates the miserliness. ”هو“ here is a faṣl (separating pronoun), which is what the Kufans call the ʿimād ("support"). We have explained it [before], except that we neglected one thing about it which we will mention here: Sībawayh claimed that ”هو“, ”هُما“, ”هم“, ”أنا“, ”أنْتَ“, ”نَحْنُ“, ”هي“ and the rest of these [pronouns] only serve as faṣl with the verbs that require a noun and a predicate, and Sībawayh did not mention the faṣl with the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate). Yet if someone interpreting him took his mention of the faṣl here to indicate that it is permissible with the mubtadaʾ or the khabar, that would not be impossible.

Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: What I myself hold in this [verse] is ”وَلا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ“ with the yāʾ, the noun [i.e. the first object, "miserliness"] being omitted. ”وَلا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ“ [with the tāʾ] may also be permissible, in the sense of "do not reckon the miserliness of those who are miserly", but omitting "miserliness" from this [construction] has some ugliness in it, whereas in omitting it from your saying ”وَلا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ“, ”يَبْخَلُونَ“ indicates the miserliness, just as you say: ”مَن كَذَبَ كانَ شَرًّا لَهُ“ ("Whoever lies, it [lying] is worse for him"). [Still,] the reading with the tāʾ is not, in my view, to be rejected; it would then be like ﴿واسْألِ القَرْيَةَ﴾ [Yusuf: 82], that is, "the people of the town", and likewise the meaning of this would be: "Do not reckon the miserliness of the misers to be good for them."

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ مِيراثُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾, that is: Allah causes their inhabitants to perish (يُغْنِي), and so the two of them are left bare (فَيُغْنَيانِ) of what is in them, with no one having any possession in them. [Translator's note: the verbs يُغْنِي / فَيُغْنَيانِ are translated as written; the sense suggests "causes to perish / are emptied" (cf. يُفْني / فَيَفْنَيان); the reading in the source may be a copying variant.] So the people were addressed in terms they understand, because they consider whatever returns to a person to be an inheritance (مِيراثًا) if it becomes his possession.

zajjaj:181-181.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿لَقَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوْلَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا إنَّ اللَّهَ فَقِيرٌ ونَحْنُ أغْنِياءُ﴾. These are the leaders of the People of the Book. When ﴿مَن ذا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا فَيُضاعِفَهُ لَهُ أضْعافًا كَثِيرَةً﴾ [al-Baqara: 245] was revealed, they said: "We see that the god of Muḥammad seeks a loan from us; so we, then, are rich and He is poor." They said this to confuse the weak among them, while they knew that Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — does not seek a loan out of need, but rather He tests the virtuous. They knew that Allah called giving and charity a "loan" (قَرْضًا), thereby emphasising that its multiples return to those who give it, and that He — Mighty and Majestic is He — withholds and extends, that is, He makes [provision] ample and makes it scant. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that He had heard their statement, and made known that it is recorded against them, that they will return to Him and He will recompense them for it, and that He is fully aware of their deeds.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿سَنَكْتُبُ ما قالُوا وقَتْلَهُمُ الأنْبِياءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ ونَقُولُ ذُوقُوا عَذابَ الحَرِيقِ﴾. The meaning of ”عَذابَ الحَرِيقِ“ is: "a punishment that burns with fire", because punishment can be by something other than fire; so He made known that the recompense of these people is this punishment. His saying ”ذُوقُوا“ ("taste!") is a word said in a matter where pardon is despaired of; one says: ”ذُقْ ما أنْتَ فِيهِ“ ("taste what you are in"), that is: you will not escape from it.

zajjaj:183-183.t: His saying — exalted be His mention —: ﴿الَّذِينَ قالُوا إنَّ اللَّهَ عَهِدَ إلَيْنا﴾. This is part of the naʿt (description) of "the servants" (العَبِيدِ) who said: ﴿حَتّى يَأْتِيَنا بِقُرْبانٍ تَأْكُلُهُ النّارُ﴾, that is: He enjoined upon us that we not believe in a messenger until his sign is this sign. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that messengers had come to their forebears with clear proofs and with what they had demanded, and they killed them; so He said: ﴿فَلِمَ قَتَلْتُمُوهُمْ﴾. They themselves had not undertaken the killing, but they were pleased with the killing of those prophets, and so they shared with them in the killing.

zajjaj:184-184.t: His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿والزُّبُرِ والكِتابِ المُنِيرِ﴾. ”اَلزُّبُرُ“ is the plural of ”زَبُورٌ“, and ”اَلزَّبُورُ“ is any book containing wisdom. One says ”زَبَرْتُ“ when one writes, and ”زَبَرْتُ“ when one reads.

zajjaj:185-185.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَإنَّما تُوَفَّوْنَ أُجُورَكم يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ﴾. ”أُجُورُكم“ is not permissible, with "wages" in the nominative and ”ما“ taken in the sense of ”اَلَّذِي“ ("that which"), because ”يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ“ would then become part of the ṣila (relative clause) of ”تُوَفَّوْنَ“, while ”تُوَفَّوْنَ“ is part of the ṣila of ”ما“; so [a part of] the ṣila of ”ما“ would come after ”أُجُورَكم“, and ”أُجُورَكم“ is the khabar (predicate). [Translator's note: the phrase «فَلا يَأْتِي ”ما“ في الصِّلَةِ بَعْدَ ”أُجُورَكم“» is translated according to its evident intent: the predicate would separate the relative clause from part of itself.]

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَمَن زُحْزِحَ عَنِ النّارِ﴾, that is: [whoever] is moved away and removed [from the Fire] has succeeded (فازَ). It is said of everyone who escapes from destruction, and of everyone who meets with something for which he is envied: ”قَدْ فازَ“ ("he has succeeded"); its interpretation is: he has got far from what is disliked and met with what he loves. As for people's word ”مَفازَةٌ“ (desert), it is really [a place] of destruction (مَهْلَكَةٌ), but they took a good omen by calling the place of destruction ”مَفازَةً“, for ”اَلْمَفازَةُ“ means the place of safety — just as they took a good omen by calling one stung [by a scorpion or snake] ”اَلسَّلِيمَ“ ("the sound one"), and as they called the blind man ”اَلْبَصِيرِ“ ("the seeing one").

zajjaj:97-97.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِيهِ آياتٌ بَيِّناتٌ مَقامُ إبْراهِيمَ﴾ — it has been related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read it: "آيَةٌ بَيِّنَةٌ مَقامُ إبْراهِيمَ" ("a clear sign: the station of Abraham"), making the station of Abraham itself the sign. What the people follow is "فِيهِ آياتٌ بَيِّناتٌ", and the meaning is: "In it are clear signs; those signs are the station of Abraham." Among the signs also is the security of whoever enters it, because the meaning of ﴿وَمَن دَخَلَهُ كانَ آمِنًا﴾ indicates that security is in it. As for the nominative (rafʿ) of "مَقامُ إبْراهِيمَ", it is on the basis of an implied (muqaddar) "هي مَقامُ إبْراهِيمَ" ("it is the station of Abraham"). The grammarians said: the meaning is "فِيهِ مَقامُ إبْراهِيمَ" ("in it is the station of Abraham"), and this is as we have explained. The meaning of the security of whoever enters it is that Abraham, upon him be peace, asked Allah to make the inhabitants of Mecca secure, saying: ﴿رَبِّ اجْعَلْ هَذا بَلَدًا آمِنًا﴾ [al-Baqara: 126]. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made the security of Mecca a sign for Abraham. People used to be snatched away all around Mecca; Allah said: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أنّا جَعَلْنا حَرَمًا آمِنًا ويُتَخَطَّفُ النّاسُ مِن حَوْلِهِمْ﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 67]. When a tyrant intended (to attack) Mecca, Allah broke him; Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأصْحابِ الفِيلِ﴾ [al-Fīl: 1]. Persia had taken the people of Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis) captive, but as for the people of Mecca, no tyrant ever coveted them. One says: "قَدْ أمِنَ الرَّجُلُ، يَأْمَنُ، أمْنًا، وأمانًا" ("the man became secure, he becomes secure, security"); "إمْنًا" has also been related, but the more common and more eloquent is "أمْنٌ" with fatḥa on the alif. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَيُبَدِّلَنَّهم مِن بَعْدِ خَوْفِهِمْ أمْنًا﴾ [al-Nūr: 55].

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ عَلى النّاسِ حِجُّ البَيْتِ﴾ is read with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and with kasra on the ḥāʾ, and the original is the fatḥa. One says: "حَجَجْتُ الشَّيْءَ أحُجُّهُ حَجًّا" when you head for it (intend it), and "اَلْحِجُّ", with kasra on the ḥāʾ, is the name of the act.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَنِ اسْتَطاعَ إلَيْهِ سَبِيلا﴾ — the position of "مَن" is genitive (khafḍ), as a badal (substitute) for "اَلنّاسِ". The meaning is: "And to Allah, upon whoever of the people is able, is (owed) the pilgrimage to the House, that he perform the pilgrimage."
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ عَنِ العالَمِينَ﴾ — more than one view has been given on it. Some said: "whoever disbelieves" means whoever says that the pilgrimage is not obligatory. Some said: whoever was able to perform the pilgrimage and postponed it until he died, while he was capable of it, has disbelieved. And it was said: it was said only of the Jews, because they said that heading for Mecca is not obligatory, whether for pilgrimage or for prayer. As for the first (view), it is agreed upon: there is no disagreement within the community that whoever says the pilgrimage is not obligatory upon one who is capable of it is a disbeliever.

zajjaj:99-99.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ يا أهْلَ الكِتابِ لِمَ تَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ مَن آمَنَ تَبْغُونَها عِوَجًا﴾, that is: you seek crookedness for it. In matters and in religion one says "عِوَجٌ", and of everything that slants one says "عِوَجٌ" [Translator's note: the text as printed vocalizes both words identically; the well-known lexical distinction is عِوَج (with kasra) for matters and religion versus عَوَج (with fatḥa) for physical objects, which may be what is intended here.]. The Arabs say: "اِبْغِنِي كَذا وكَذا", meaning: seek it for me; and they say "أبْغِنِي كَذا وكَذا", with fatḥa on the alif, meaning: help me in seeking it, i.e. seek it along with me — just as you say "أعْكِمْنِي" and "أحْلِبْنِي", i.e. help me with the bundling (al-ʿakm) and the milking (al-ḥalb). The meaning of ﴿وَأنْتُمْ شُهَداءُ﴾ is: while you bear witness, by what has become established in your souls, that the matter of the Prophet is true; and Allah is not heedless of what you do.

zajjaj:100-100.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنْ تُطِيعُوا فَرِيقًا مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتابَ﴾ — by "the party" He means the class of those who disbelieved. That is: if you follow them blindly, they will turn you back into disbelievers; i.e. even while you are not of their religion, you would be disbelievers in that conviction of yours. So likewise, if you obey them or follow them, you are disbelievers.

zajjaj:101-101.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ وأنْتُمْ تُتْلى عَلَيْكم آياتُ اللَّهِ وفِيكم رَسُولُهُ﴾, that is: in what state can disbelief occur from you, while the signs of Allah — which the Prophet ﷺ brought, pointing to the oneness of Allah and the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ — are recited to you, and His Messenger is among you making these signs clear to you?! It is permissible to say "His Messenger is among you" while the Prophet is present, and it is permissible to say to us now: "The Messenger of Allah is among you", because his traces, his signs, and the Quran which he brought are among us, and it is one of the mighty signs.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَن يَعْتَصِمْ بِاللَّهِ﴾, that is: whoever seeks protection in Allah and holds fast to the rope of Allah has been guided to a straight path. "يَعْتَصِمْ" is jussive (majzūm) by "مَن", and the apodosis (jawāb) is "فَقَدْ هُدِيَ". The meaning of "اِعْتَصَمْتُ بِكَذا وكَذا" in the language is: I held fast to it and protected myself by it from something else. Likewise: ﴿لا عاصِمَ اليَوْمَ مِن أمْرِ اللَّهِ﴾ [Hūd: 43]; and the meaning of ﴿سَآوِي إلى جَبَلٍ يَعْصِمُنِي مِنَ الماءِ﴾ [Hūd: 43] is: it will protect me from the water — i.e. [Translator's note: this explains ﴿لا عاصِمَ﴾ above.] "there is none possessing protection" and "none possessing refuge from Allah".

zajjaj:102-102.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقاتِهِ﴾, that is: fear Him in that in which it is due from you to fear Him. Some said: "حَقَّ تُقاتِهِ" ("His due fear") is that He be obeyed and not disobeyed, and remembered and not forgotten. The meaning of "remembered and not forgotten" is that He be remembered at the point where His command becomes binding, so that His command is not transgressed. Some said: this verse is abrogated; it was abrogated by His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ ما اسْتَطَعْتُمْ﴾ [al-Taghābun: 16].
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إلا وُسْعَها﴾ [al-Baqara: 286]. "تُقاةٌ": its origin is "وُقاةٌ", and it is from "وَقَيْتُ" ("I guarded"), except that the wāw did not come in this pattern in its original form; nothing has been said in this pattern except with the tāʾ substituted for the wāw. Likewise they said "تُخْمَةٌ" (indigestion), which is only from "اَلْوَخامَةُ" (unwholesomeness). Likewise they said in (the pattern) "فُعالٌ", for example "اَلتُّراثُ" (inheritance), "اَلتُّجاهُ" and "تُجاهٌ", in the sense of facing. This pattern has several possibilities: if you build "فُعْلَةٌ" from "وَقَيْتُ" you say "تُقاةٌ", and this is what the grammarians prefer; nothing has come in the language on this pattern except that the tāʾ has been substituted for its wāw. It is also permissible to say "وُقاةٌ" and "أُقاةٌ", because when the wāw takes a ḍamma and is initial, you have the choice in substituting for it: if you wish you substitute a hamza for it, and if you wish you leave it in its form, and if you wish — in this pattern specifically — you substitute the tāʾ for it.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلا تَمُوتُنَّ إلا وأنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ — the wording of the prohibition falls on death, while the meaning falls on the command to remain steadfast in Islam. The meaning is: be in Islam, so that when death comes upon you it finds you in that state. This is permissible only because there is no ambiguity in the speech, since it is known from it that they are not forbidden from what they do not (themselves) do. Its like in ordinary speech is "لا أرَيَنَّكَ هَهُنا" ("let me not see you here"): the prohibition falls in the wording on the speaker [Translator's note: the Arabic says "على المخاطبة" ("on the addressing"); in the wording, the verb "see" belongs to the speaker, not the one addressed.], while the meaning is: "Do not be here, for whoever is here, I will see him." But the speech was aimed at concision and brevity, since there was no deficiency of meaning in it.

zajjaj:103-103.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿واعْتَصِمُوا بِحَبْلِ اللَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ — "جَمِيعًا" is accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The meaning is: be united in holding fast to it.
The explanation of "واعْتَصِمُوا بِحَبْلِ اللَّهِ" is: hold fast to the covenant of Allah. "اَلْحَبْلُ" (the rope) in the language of the Arabs is the covenant. Al-Aʿshā said:
؎وَإذا أجُوزُ بِها حِبالَ قَبِيلَةٍ ∗∗∗ أخَذَتْ مِنَ الأُخْرى إلَيْكَ حِبالَها
(And whenever I pass with her through the "ropes" [i.e. the covenants of protection] of one tribe, she takes from the next tribe its "ropes" on her way to you.)
The meaning of ﴿وَلا تَفَرَّقُوا﴾ is: support one another upon the religion of Allah. The origin of "تَفَرَّقُوا" is "تَتَفَرَّقُوا", except that a tāʾ was dropped because two letters of the same kind came together in one word. The one dropped is the second, because the first indicates the future (imperfect), and it is not permissible to drop the letter that indicates the future. It is jussive (majzūm) by the prohibition; the origin is "وَلا تَتَفَرَّقُونَ", and the nūn was dropped to indicate the jussive.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿واذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكم إذْ كُنْتُمْ أعْداءً فَألَّفَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِكم فَأصْبَحْتُمْ بِنِعْمَتِهِ إخْوانًا﴾ — Allah reminded them of the great blessing upon them in Islam, because in their Jāhiliyya they used to kill one another, and every one of them who prevailed would treat as lawful (the life and property of) whomever he overcame. Then Islam made lives and properties inviolable to them except by their right. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known to them the share they have in the immediate world by entering Islam.
It was said: it was revealed concerning al-Aws and al-Khazraj, because there had been constant wars between them in the Jāhiliyya over which many years had passed; then Islam removed those wars, and they became brothers in Islam, loving one another in that. The origin of "اَلْأخُ" (brother) in the language is that the brother's aim is the aim of his brother; likewise it is in friendship, that the will of each of the two brothers agrees with what his companion wants. The Arabs say: "فُلانٌ يَتَوَخّى مَسارَّ فُلانٍ" ("So-and-so seeks what pleases so-and-so"), i.e. he aims at what pleases him.
His saying, Majestic and Exalted is He: ﴿وَكُنْتُمْ عَلى شَفا حُفْرَةٍ مِنَ النّارِ﴾, that is: you had come to the very edge of the Fire. "شَفا الشَّيْءِ" is its edge; it is maqṣūr (ending in a short alif), written with alif, and its dual is "شَفَوانِ". And He said ﴿فَأنْقَذَكم مِنها﴾ and did not say "مِنهُ", because what is intended in the statement is the Fire; that is: He rescued you from it through the Prophet ﷺ.
His saying, Majestic and Exalted is He: ﴿كَذَلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكم آياتِهِ﴾ — the kāf is in the position of the accusative (naṣb). The meaning is: like the clarification that is recited to you, Allah makes clear to you His signs. The meaning of ﴿لَعَلَّكم تَهْتَدُونَ﴾ is: so that you may be in hope of His guidance.

zajjaj:45-45.t:
﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكِ بِكَلِمَةٍ مِنهُ﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, named ʿĪsā ”اَلْمَسِيحَ“ and named him ”عِيسى“, and the beginning of his affair was called ”كَلِمَةً مِنهُ“ ("a word from Him"); so he ﷺ is a word from Allah which He cast to Maryam, then He formed that word into a human being.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿اسْمُهُ﴾ (masculine), although what was mentioned was "the word" (feminine), because the meaning of "the word" is the meaning of "the child"; the meaning is: "Allah gives you glad tidings of this child". ﴿وَجِيهًا في الدُّنْيا والآخِرَةِ﴾: ”وَجِيهًا“ is in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The wajīh is the one who has a lofty standing with people of rank and knowledge. One says ”قَدْ وجُهَ الرَّجُلُ، يَوْجُهُ، وجاهَةً“, and ”لِفُلانٍ جاهٌ عِنْدَ النّاسِ، ووَجاهَةٌ عِنْدَ النّاسِ“ ("so-and-so has standing among people"), i.e. a lofty position. Some grammarians said: ”وَجِيهًا“ is in the accusative by "qaṭʿ" (severance) from ”عِيسى“. But "qaṭʿ" here is an absurd word, because he was announced only in this state, i.e. in the state of his excellence — so how could it be severed from him? And he did not say why this severance puts it in the accusative. If the severance is only a meaning, that meaning is not present in this wording; and if the severance is the governing factor (ʿāmil), he did not explain what it is; and if he meant that the alif and lām (the definite article) were severed from it, that is absurd, because all ḥāls are indefinite while the alif and lām are for something previously known — so how can something be severed from a thing which was never in it at all?

zajjaj:46-46.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَيُكَلِّمُ النّاسَ في المَهْدِ﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ”وَجِيهًا“; the meaning is: He gives you glad tidings of him as one eminent and as one speaking to people in the cradle. It is permissible to conjoin "yafʿalu" (an imperfect verb) to "fāʿilun" (an active participle), because of its resemblance to the verb of an agent. The poet said:
باتَ يَعِيشُها بِغَضَبٍ باتِرْ ∗∗∗ يَقْصِدُ في أسْواقِها وجائِرْ
(He spent the night [tending] them with a cutting [blade], keeping straight at their shanks and swerving.) [Translator's note: the printed text reads بِغَضَبٍ ("with anger"); the sense of the verse suggests بِعَضْبٍ ("with a sharp sword"). The point of the verse is the conjunction of the participle جائِرْ to the verb يَقْصِدُ.]
﴿وَكَهْلا﴾, that is: and he will speak to people as a mature man (kahl). Allah informed her that ʿĪsā would remain until the state of maturity. It has also been said that ”كَهْلًا“ means: he will descend from heaven to kill the Dajjāl while he is a mature man; and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:47-47.t: The meaning of ﴿كَذَلِكِ اللَّهُ يَخْلُقُ ما يَشاءُ﴾ is: Allah creates what He wills like that.

zajjaj:48-48.t:
﴿وَيُعَلِّمُهُ الكِتابَ والحِكْمَةَ والتَّوْراةَ والإنْجِيلَ﴾, that is: He will teach him that by revelation and inspiration. ﴿وَرَسُولا إلى بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 49] is in the accusative on two possible bases. One of them: "and He will make him a messenger to the Children of Israel". The preferred view in my opinion — and Allah knows best — is: "and he will speak to people as a messenger to the Children of Israel". The evidence for that is that He said: ﴿أنِّي قَدْ جِئْتُكم بِآيَةٍ مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 49]; so the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "and he will speak to them as a messenger, (saying) that I have come to you with a sign from your Lord". If it were read ”إنِّي قَدْ جِئْتُكم“ with kasra, it would be correct; the meaning: "Indeed I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, i.e. with a mark that establishes my message."
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أنِّي أخْلُقُ لَكم مِنَ الطِّينِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 49] may be in the genitive or in the nominative. The genitive is as a badal (substitute) for ”آيَةٍ“; the meaning: "I have come to you with (the sign) that I create for you from clay". It is also possible that it is ”إنِّي أخْلُقُ لَكم مِنَ الطِّينِ“ (with kasra), informing them what this sign is, i.e. "I say to you: indeed I create for you from clay the like of the form of a bird". It is said that he made something like the form of a bat and breathed into it, and it became a bird. It is permissible that ﴿فَأنْفُخُ فِيهِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 49] (masculine pronoun) refers to the word "clay", and He said in another place: ﴿فَتَنْفُخُ فِيها فَتَكُونُ طَيْرًا بِإذْنِي﴾ [al-Māʾida: 110] (feminine pronoun), referring to the word "form (hayʾa)".
﴿وَأُبْرِئُ الأكْمَهَ والأبْرَصَ وأُحْيِي المَوْتى بِإذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 49]: ”اَلْأكْمَهُ“ is the one born blind. The rajaz poet said:
هَرَّجْتُ فارْتَدَّ ارْتِدادَ الأكْمَهِ
(I shouted at him, and he turned back as the one born blind turns back.)
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَأُنَبِّئُكم بِما تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 49], that is: I will inform you of what you eat. It is possible that ”ما“ here is in the place of ”اَلَّذِي“ (a relative noun), the meaning being: "I will inform you of that which you eat and store up"; and it is possible that ”ما“ together with what comes after it is equivalent to a maṣdar (verbal noun), the meaning being: "I will inform you of your eating and your storing". The first is better.
As for the meaning of ﴿تَدَّخِرُونَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 49], it has come in the exegesis: what you eat in your mornings. ”تَدَّخِرُونَ“ is said with dāl and with dhāl. Some grammarians said: ”تَدَّخِرُونَ“ was chosen only because tāʾ is assimilated into dhāl, as in ”تَذَّكَّرُونَ“, but they disliked ”تَذَّخِرُونَ“ because it does not resemble that; so they sought a letter between tāʾ and dhāl, and that letter was dāl. The one who holds this needs to know the voiced (majhūr) and voiceless (mahmūs) letters, which — according to what al-Khalīl claimed — are of two kinds. The voiced is a letter on whose place of articulation the pressure is full, so that it prevents the breath from flowing with it; the voiceless is a letter on whose place of articulation the pressure is weak, so that the breath flows with it. It was said ”تَدَّخِرُونَ“, though its origin is ”تَذَّخِرُونَ“, i.e. "yaftaʿilūn" from ”اَلذُّخْرُ“, only because dhāl is a voiced letter with which the breath cannot flow, owing to the strength of its pressure at its place, while tāʾ is voiceless; so in place of the tāʾ there was substituted, from the tāʾ's place of articulation, a voiced letter resembling dhāl in its voicing, namely dāl. So it became ”تَذْدَخِرُون“, then the dhāl was assimilated into the dāl; and this is the basic rule of assimilation — that you assimilate the first into the second. ”تَذَّخِرُونَ“ is also permissible. As for what he said about confusion (malbas), ”تَذَّخِرُونَ“ being confusing is nothing (i.e. not a valid argument).

zajjaj:50-50.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَمُصَدِّقًا لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ مِنَ التَّوْراةِ﴾: ”مُصَدِّقًا“ is in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "and I have come to you confirming what is before me", i.e. the Book that was sent down before me; so it commands you to follow me.
﴿وَلأُحِلَّ لَكم بَعْضَ الَّذِي حُرِّمَ عَلَيْكم وجِئْتُكم بِآيَةٍ مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾, that is: I have not made anything lawful for you without proof, so following me is a duty upon you, because I bring you a proof and the making lawful of good things that had been made unlawful for you. ﴿فاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وأطِيعُونِ﴾, that is: follow me. Abū ʿUbayda said concerning the meaning of ﴿وَلأُحِلَّ لَكم بَعْضَ الَّذِي حُرِّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: its meaning is "all of what was made unlawful for you". This is impossible in the language, in the exegesis, and in what practice is based on. As for its impossibility in the language: "some" (al-baʿḍ) and "part" (al-juzʾ) cannot be "all" (al-kull). Abū ʿUbayda recited on this a verse whose meaning he got wrong, namely the saying of Labīd:
تَرّاكُ مَنزِلَةٍ إذا لَمْ أرْضَها ∗∗∗ أوْ يَعْتَلِقْ بَعْضَ النُّفُوسِ حِمامُها
(I readily abandon a dwelling if I am not pleased with it — unless its fated death seizes some soul.)
He said: the meaning is "or its fated death seizes every soul". But this is a way of speaking people use: someone says ”بَعْضُنا يَعْرِفُكَ“ ("one of us knows you"), meaning "I know you"; so this is only a genuine partitive. ʿĪsā only brought them the making lawful of what had been unlawful for them. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿فَبِظُلْمٍ مِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا حَرَّمْنا عَلَيْهِمْ طَيِّباتٍ أُحِلَّتْ لَهُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 160] — these are such things as fats and what goes along with them in prohibition. As for his having made lawful for them killing, theft and fornication, that is absurd.
The meaning of ﴿هَذا صِراطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 51] is: this is the path of religion, straight.

zajjaj:52-52.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَلَمّا أحَسَّ عِيسى مِنهُمُ الكُفْرَ﴾: the meaning of ”أحَسَّ“ in the language is: he knew and found. One says "هَلْ أحَسْتَ؟" in the sense of "هَلْ أحْسَسْتَ؟" ("did you perceive?"), and one says "حَسَيْتُ بِالشَّيْءِ" when I know and recognise it. Al-Aṣmaʿī recited:
سِوى أنَّ العِتاقَ مِنَ المَطايا ∗∗∗ حَسَيْنَ بِهِ فَهُنَّ إلَيْهِ شُوسُ
(Except that the noble riding camels sensed him, so they look at him askance.)
One also says ”حَسَّهُمُ القائِدُ“, i.e. the commander killed them. As for the meaning of ﴿مَن أنْصارِي إلى اللَّهِ﴾, it has come in the exegesis: "Who are my helpers with Allah?" ”إلى“ here only approaches ”مَعَ“ in meaning, in that if the expression were rendered with ”مَعَ“ it would convey a similar meaning — not that ”إلى“ has the meaning of ”مَعَ“. If you said ”ذَهَبَ زَيْدٌ إلى عَمْرٍو“ ("Zayd went to ʿAmr"), ”ذَهَبَ زَيْدٌ مَعَ عَمْرٍو“ ("Zayd went with ʿAmr") would not be valid (as its equivalent), because ”إلى“ marks a limit, while ”مَعَ“ joins one thing to another. So the meaning is: "who will add his help to me to the help of Allah?" Their saying that ”إلى“ is in the sense of ”مَعَ“ is nothing. Particles may come close in what they convey, so that one weak in knowledge of the language thinks their meaning is one. Of this is His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلأُصَلِّبَنَّكم في جُذُوعِ النَّخْلِ﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 71]; had it been ”عَلى“ here, it would have conveyed this meaning, for if you said ”لَأُصَلِّبَنَّكم عَلى جُذُوعِ النَّخْلِ“ it would be sound. But the basic sense of ”في“ is only for a container, and the basic sense of ”عَلى“ is for what is upon a thing, as when you say ”اَلتَّمْرُ في الجِرابِ“ ("the dates are in the sack"); if you said ”اَلتَّمْرُ عَلى الجِرابِ“ ("the dates are on the sack") it would not be valid in this meaning. Yet ”وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكم في جُذُوعِ النَّخْلِ“ is permissible because the trunk encloses the crucified one, since it has taken him from his sides. And if you say ”زَيْدٌ عَلى الجَبَلِ“ ("Zayd is on the mountain") and ”في الجَبَلِ“ ("in the mountain"), it is valid, because the mountain has enclosed Zayd. On this basis is the figurative use (majāz) of these particles.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿قالَ الحَوارِيُّونَ نَحْنُ أنْصارُ اللَّهِ﴾: those skilled in the language said: ”اَلْحَوارِيُّونَ“ are the elite of the prophets (peace be upon them), those who were pure and sincere in believing them and helping them; so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, named them ”اَلْحَوارِيُّونَ“. It has also been said that they were fullers, and were called al-ḥawāriyyūn because they whitened clothes; then this name came to be used for those of the believers who resembled them, by way of likening them to them. It has been said that they were kings, and it has been said they were fishermen. What the people of the language hold is that they are the elite, as I have told you. It is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "«Al-Zubayr is the son of my paternal aunt, and my ḥawārī from my community»". The women of the Anṣār are called ”حَوارِيّاتٌ“ because by their cleanliness they are far from the roughness of Bedouin women. Abū ʿUbayda and others recited, by Abū Jilda al-Yashkurī:
فَقُلْ لِلْحَوارِيّاتِ يَبْكِينَ غَيْرَنا ∗∗∗ ولا تَبْكِنا إلّا الكِلابُ النَّوابِحُ
(Tell the fair town-women to weep for others than us; let none weep for us but the barking dogs.)
The people of the language have two views about the miḥwar — the rod on which the pulley turns. Some of them said: it was called ”مِحْوَرٌ“ only because of turning, since it returns to the place from which it moved. And it has been said: it was called ”مِحْوَرٌ“ only because by its turning it becomes polished until it becomes white. From this one says ”دَقِيقٌ حُوّارى“ ("fine white flour"), i.e. its choicest part has been taken; and likewise ”عَجِينٌ مُحَوَّرٌ“, for dough whose surface is wiped with water until it becomes clear. One says ”عَيْنٌ حَوْراءَ“ when its white is intense and pure and its black is intense. One does not say ”اِمْرَأةٌ حَوْراءُ“ unless, together with the ḥawar of her eyes, she is fair-skinned. As for what is narrated in the ḥadīth, "We seek refuge with Allah from al-ḥawar after al-kawar", its meaning is: we seek refuge with Allah from going back and leaving the community after al-kawar, i.e. after we were in the kawar, i.e. in the community. One says ”كارَ الرَّجُلُ عِمامَتَهُ“ when he winds it round his head, and ”حارَ عِمامَتَهُ“ when he unwinds it. It has also been said "after al-kawn", meaning: after we were upright; however, with "al-kawn" there is something omitted in the speech which is indicated. As for the meaning of His saying ﴿فاكْتُبْنا مَعَ الشّاهِدِينَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 53], it is: write us among those who bore witness to the prophets by believing them. The reality of the witness is that he is the one who makes clear the soundness of the claimant's claim; so the meaning is: we have believed in Allah, acknowledged the truth of what the Prophet ﷺ brought, and stood firm — so write us among those who have done as we have done.

zajjaj:186-186.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿لَتُبْلَوُنَّ في أمْوالِكم وأنْفُسِكُمْ﴾. Its meaning is: you will surely be tested, that is, trials will befall you, so that the believer is distinguished from others. This nūn entered for emphasis together with the lām of the oath, and the wāw was given a ḍamma because of its being vowelless and the nūn being vowelless. To one male one says: ”لَتُبْلَيَنَّ يا رَجُلُ“ ("you will surely be tested, O man"), to two: ”لَتُبْلَيانِّ يا رَجُلانِ“, and to a group of men: ”لَتُبْلَوُنَّ“. The yāʾ of ”لَتُبْلَيَنَّ“ takes a fatḥa, according to Sībawayh, because of its being vowelless and the nūn being vowelless; according to others it is indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because the nūn is joined to it, just as what precedes the feminine hāʾ is made indeclinable. To a woman one says: ”تُبْلَيِنَّ يا امْرَأةُ“ [Translator's note: so in the source, without the lām; the expected form is «لَتُبْلَيِنَّ»], to two women: ”لَتُبْلَيانِّ يا امْرَأتانِ“, and to a group of women: ”لَتُبْلَيْنانِّ يا نِسْوَةُ“ — the alif was added because of the coming together of the nūns.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَلَتَسْمَعُنَّ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتابَ مِن قَبْلِكم ومِنَ الَّذِينَ أشْرَكُوا أذًى كَثِيرًا﴾. It is narrated that Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq — may Allah be pleased with him — heard a man of the Jews saying: "Allah is poor and we are rich," so Abū Bakr — may Allah be pleased with him — slapped him. The Jew complained of that to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet asked him: "What made you slap him?" Abū Bakr said: "I heard from him a word at which I could not restrain myself from slapping him." So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — revealed: ﴿وَلَتَسْمَعُنَّ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتابَ مِن قَبْلِكم ومِنَ الَّذِينَ أشْرَكُوا أذًى كَثِيرًا﴾. ”أذًى“ is maqṣūr (ending in a short-written alif) and is written with yāʾ; one says: ”قَدْ أذِيَ فُلانٌ، يَأْذى، أذًى“ ("so-and-so was hurt"), when he hears what distresses him.

zajjaj:187-187.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿لَتُبَيِّنُنَّهُ لِلنّاسِ﴾, and ”لَيُبَيِّنُنَّهُ“ — with the yāʾ and with the tāʾ. Whoever says ”لَيُبَيِّنُنَّهُ“ with the yāʾ does so because they are absent [third persons]; whoever says it with the tāʾ reports the direct address that took place at the time the covenant was taken. The meaning is that Allah took the covenant from them that they would make clear the matter of the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿فَنَبَذُوهُ وراءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ﴾: the meaning of ”نَبَذُوهُ“ is: they threw it away. Of one who discards a thing and pays it no heed it is said: ”قَدْ جَعَلْتَ هَذا الشَّيْءَ بِظَهْرٍ“ ("you have put this thing behind a back") and ”قَدْ رَمَيْتَهُ بِظَهْرٍ“ ("you have thrown it behind a back"). Al-Farazdaq said:
؎تَمِيمُ بْنَ قَيْسٍ لا تَكُونَنَّ حاجَتِي ∗∗∗ بِظَهْرٍ فَلا يَعْيا عَلَيَّ جَوابُها
(O Tamīm ibn Qays, let my request not be cast behind your back, so that its answer does not fail me.)
That is: do not leave it unheeded. And Allah informed [us] of what drove the Jews who were leaders to conceal the matter of the Prophet ﷺ, saying: ﴿واشْتَرَوْا بِهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلا﴾, that is: they accepted bribes for that, and a position of leadership was established for them by which they gained [wealth]; that is what drove them to disbelieve in what they conceal.

zajjaj:188-188.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿لا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِما أتَوْا ويُحِبُّونَ أنْ يُحْمَدُوا بِما لَمْ يَفْعَلُوا﴾. These are a group of the People of the Book who went in to the Prophet ﷺ and came out from him, and told those who saw them at that time that the Prophet ﷺ had brought them things which they recognised [as true]; so those of the Muslims who witnessed them praised them for that. But they concealed the opposite of what they displayed, and persisted after that in unbelief. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — informed the Prophet ﷺ of their affair, and informed him that they are not in a place of escape (بِمَفازَةٍ) from the punishment, that is, they are not far from the punishment.

”فَلا تَحْسَبَنَّهم“ occurs repeated because of the length of the account. When the account grows long, the Arabs repeat [verbs] such as ”حَسِبْتُ“ and the like, to make known that what has followed is connected to the first, and to emphasise the first. So you say: ”لا تَظُنَّنَّ زَيْدًا إذا جاءَكَ وكَلَّمَكَ بِكَذا وكَذا، فَلا تَظُنَّنَّهُ صادِقًا“ ("Do not think Zayd — when he comes to you and speaks to you of such and such — do not think him truthful"), repeating ”فَلا تَظُنَّنَّ“ for emphasis. If you said ”لا تَظُنَّ زَيْدًا إذا جاءَكَ وحَدَّثَكَ بِكَذا وكَذا صادِقًا“, it would be permissible, but the repetition is more emphatic and makes the account clearer.

zajjaj:189-189.t: His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ واللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾, that is: He is their Creator. The proof of this is His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ”خالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ“ and ”خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ“. And He made known that in their creation and in the alternation of night and day there are signs for those of understanding (لِأُولِي الألْبابِ), that is, people of intellect. ”اَلْآياتُ“ means the signs (marks); that is: among the signs in them is a proof that their Creator is One, nothing being like unto Him.

zajjaj:191-191.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ﴾. This is part of the naʿt (description) of ”أُولِي الألْبابِ“; that is: these people infer the oneness of Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — from the creation of the heavens and the earth, and they remember Allah in all their states, ﴿قِيامًا وقُعُودًا وعَلى جُنُوبِهِمْ﴾, meaning: and lying down. It is sound in the language for [a phrase with] ”عَلى“ to be conjoined to ”قِيامًا وقُعُودًا“, because its meaning conveys one of the states of a person's activity. You say: ”أنا أسِيرُ إلى زَيْدٍ ماشِيًا وعَلى الخَيْلِ“ ("I travel to Zayd walking and on horseback"), the meaning being "walking and riding". So these who infer the truth of Allah's oneness remember Allah in all these states. Some of them said: ”يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ قِيامًا وقُعُودًا وعَلى جُنُوبِهِمْ“ means: they pray in all these states, according to their ability in their health and their sickness. Its true sense in my view — and Allah knows best — is that they affirm the oneness of Allah in every state, ﴿وَيَتَفَكَّرُونَ في خَلْقِ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾, and that increases them in insight, because their reflection shows them how great the matter of the two is, so their magnifying of Allah is in proportion to what they come upon of the traces of His mercy.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿رَبَّنا ما خَلَقْتَ هَذا باطِلا﴾. Its meaning is: "[they say:] Our Lord, You did not create this in vain," that is: You created it as a proof of You and of the truthfulness of what Your prophets brought, because the prophets bring what created beings are incapable of, so it is like the heavens and the earth in being a proof of the oneness of Allah. ﴿سُبْحانَكَ﴾ means: declaring You free of evil, and declaring You exalted above having created the two in vain. ﴿فَقِنا عَذابَ النّارِ﴾, that is: we have believed Your messengers and that You have a Paradise and a Fire, so protect us from the punishment of the Fire.

zajjaj:194-194.t:
﴿رَبَّنا وآتِنا ما وعَدْتَنا عَلى رُسُلِكَ﴾: its meaning — and Allah knows best — is: on the tongues of Your messengers.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَلا تُخْزِنا يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ﴾, that is: we have believed in the Day of Resurrection, so do not disgrace us. ”اَلْمُخْزى“ in the language is one who is humiliated and despised through a matter that has been made binding on him by an argument; likewise ”أخْزَيْتَهُ“, that is, you bound him with an argument by which you humiliated him.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿إنَّكَ لا تُخْلِفُ المِيعادَ﴾, that is: You have promised Paradise to whoever believes in You and affirms Your oneness.

zajjaj:195-195.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فاسْتَجابَ لَهم رَبُّهم أنِّي لا أُضِيعُ عَمَلَ عامِلٍ مِنكُمْ﴾. The meaning is: their Lord answered them [saying] that (بِأنِّي) "I do not let the deed of any doer among you be lost, whether male or female." If it were read ”إنِّي لا أُضِيعُ عَمَلَ عامِلٍ مِنكم“ with a kasra on ”إنَّ“, it would be permissible, and the meaning would be: "Their Lord said to them: I do not let the deed of any doer among you be lost."

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿ثَوابًا﴾ is an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of ﴿وَلأُدْخِلَنَّهم جَنّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ﴾ is "I will surely reward them". Similar to it is ﴿كِتابَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ [al-Nisa: 24], because His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكم أُمَّهاتُكم وبَناتُكُمْ﴾ [al-Nisa: 23] means "Allah has prescribed this for you", so ”كِتابَ اللَّهِ“ is emphatic. Likewise His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَتَرى الجِبالَ تَحْسَبُها جامِدَةً وهي تَمُرُّ مَرَّ السَّحابِ صُنْعَ اللَّهِ الَّذِي أتْقَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾ [al-Naml: 88]: it is already known [from what precedes] that this is the making of Allah.

zajjaj:196-196.t: His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿لا يَغُرَّنَّكَ تَقَلُّبُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا في البِلادِ﴾ is an address to the Prophet ﷺ, and in this place an address to [all] people; the meaning is: "Let it not deceive you, O believers." It is narrated that a group of the unbelievers used to trade and make profit on journeys they would undertake, so Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that this is not something for which they should be envied, because their destination, on account of their unbelief, is the Fire, and there is no good in a good that is followed by the Fire. So He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿مَتاعٌ قَلِيلٌ ثُمَّ مَأْواهم جَهَنَّمُ وبِئْسَ المِهادُ﴾ [Al ʿImran: 197], that is: that gain and profit which they make is a brief enjoyment.

zajjaj:198-198.t: And He — Majestic and Mighty is He — made known that whoever seeks Allah and fears Him shall have Paradise, saying: ﴿لَكِنِ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا رَبَّهم لَهم جَنّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها نُـزُلا مِن عِنْدِ اللَّهِ﴾. ”نُزُلًا“ is also emphatic, because their abiding forever in it is their being lodged (إنْزالُهم) in it. The singular of ”اَلْأبْرارُ“ is ”بارٌّ“, ”بارٌّ“ / ”أبْرارٌ“ being like ”صاحِبٌ“ / ”أصْحابٌ“. It may also be ”بَرٌّ“ / ”أبْرارٌ“, on the pattern faʿl / afʿāl; you say: ”بَرَرْتُ والِدِي، فَأنا بَرٌّ“ ("I was dutiful to my father, so I am barr"). Its origin is ”بَرَرَ“, but the rāʾ was assimilated because of the doubling.

zajjaj:199-199.t: His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿خاشِعِينَ لِلَّهِ﴾, that is: among the People of the Book there is one who believes, humbly submissive to Allah, ﴿لا يَشْتَرُونَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلا﴾. He mentioned these only because mention of those who disbelieved had come before mention of them, where He said: ﴿فَنَبَذُوهُ وراءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ واشْتَرَوْا بِهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلا﴾ [Al ʿImran: 187]. He — Majestic and Mighty is He — told what drove the Jews to unbelief, and told the state of those of the People of the Book who believed: that they believed in a state of humility, and turned away from selling the signs of Allah for a small price.

zajjaj:200-200.t: His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اصْبِرُوا﴾, that is: [be patient] in your religion; ﴿وَصابِرُوا﴾, that is: [outdo in patience] your enemy; ﴿وَرابِطُوا﴾: remain steadfast in striving against your enemy with war and with argument; ﴿واتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ in all that He has commanded you and forbidden you; ﴿لَعَلَّكم تُفْلِحُونَ﴾. ”لَعَلَّ“ expresses hope (tarajjī), and it is a hope [held out] for them, that is: so that they may be in hope of success. It was said to them ”لَعَلَّكم تُفْلِحُونَ“ only in the sense of: perhaps you will be safe from deeds that would nullify these deeds of yours. As for the believers whom Allah — exalted be His praise — has described, they have already succeeded; Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿قَدْ أفْلَحَ المُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ [al-Muʾminun: 1] ﴿الَّذِينَ هم في صَلاتِهِمْ خاشِعُونَ﴾ [al-Muʾminun: 2], to the end of the description of the believers. These have succeeded without doubt; hope is only [expressed] together with a deed that is supposed to be part of righteous action.

zajjaj:104-104.t:
His saying, Majestic and Exalted is He: ﴿وَلْتَكُنْ مِنكم أُمَّةٌ يَدْعُونَ إلى الخَيْرِ ويَأْمُرُونَ بِالمَعْرُوفِ ويَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ المُنْكَرِ﴾ — the lām is given sukūn, and its original vowel is kasra; the origin is "وَلِتَكُنْ مِنكم", but the kasra was dropped because the wāw became, together with the word, like a single letter, and the dropping was made obligatory. If it is read "وَلِتَكُنْ" with kasra, that is good, according to the original, but the lightening is better and more frequent in the speech of the Arabs. The meaning of "وَلْتَكُنْ مِنكم أُمَّةٌ" — and Allah knows best — is: let all of you be a community calling to good and enjoining what is right; but "مِن" enters here to single out those addressed from all other kinds, and it emphasizes that the command is for those addressed. Its like in the Book of Allah is ﴿فاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الأوْثانِ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 30]: He is not commanding them to avoid some of the idols; rather the meaning is: avoid the idols, for they are filth. Its like in poetry is the poet's saying:
؎أخُو رَغائِبَ يُعْطِيها ويَسْألُها ∗∗∗ يَأْبى الظُّلامَةَ مِنهُ النَّوْفَلُ الزَّفَرُ
(A man of great gifts, who gives them and is asked for them; from him the generous giver, the bearer of burdens, refuses injustice.)
That is: he is the nawfal, the zufar, because he has described him as giving great gifts. "اَلنَّوْفَلُ" is the one who gives many voluntary gifts (nawāfil), and "اَلزَّفَرُ" [Translator's note: so vocalized in the printed text; the word is usually vocalized زُفَر.] is the one who carries heavy burdens. The proof that all of them were commanded to enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong is His saying, Majestic and Exalted is He: ﴿كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخْرِجَتْ لِلنّاسِ تَأْمُرُونَ بِالمَعْرُوفِ وتَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ المُنْكَرِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 110]. It is also possible that a group among them was commanded, because His saying ﴿وَلْتَكُنْ مِنكم أُمَّةٌ يَدْعُونَ إلى الخَيْرِ﴾ mentions those who call to faith, and those who call ought to be knowledgeable about what they call to, and not all people are scholars; in knowledge some people stand in for others, and likewise in jihad.
His saying, Majestic and Exalted is He: ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ المُفْلِحُونَ﴾, that is: those whom We have mentioned are the successful. "اَلْمُفْلِحُ" is the one who attains what he is gladdened by. "هم" may be a mubtadaʾ (subject), and "اَلْمُفْلِحُونَ" the khabar (predicate) of "أُولَئِكَ", and "هم" a faṣl (separating pronoun), which is what the Kufans call al-ʿimād (the support). [Translator's note: the sentence is reproduced as printed; the sense is evidently two alternatives — either "هم" is a mubtadaʾ (with "اَلْمُفْلِحُونَ" as its khabar, the clause being the khabar of "أُولَئِكَ"), or "اَلْمُفْلِحُونَ" is the khabar of "أُولَئِكَ" and "هم" is a faṣl.]

zajjaj:105-105.t: His saying, Exalted be His praise: ﴿وَلا تَكُونُوا كالَّذِينَ تَفَرَّقُوا واخْتَلَفُوا مِن بَعْدِ ما جاءَهُمُ البَيِّناتُ﴾, that is: do not be like the People of the Book — meaning by them the Jews and the Christians, whose book, for all of them, is the Torah, and they are divided: each sect of them, even if it agrees in the matter of Christianity or Judaism, is also divided, like the Christians who are Nestorians, Jacobites and Melkites. So Allah commanded unity upon His Book, and made known that division over it brings its people out into the like of what the People of the Book came out into in their disbelief. Then Allah made known that for them is a great punishment, saying: ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ لَهم عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾.

zajjaj:106-106.t:
Then He told of the time of that punishment, saying: ﴿يَوْمَ تَبْيَضُّ وُجُوهٌ وتَسْوَدُّ وُجُوهٌ﴾, that is: the punishment is established for them on that day. Their whitening is their radiance and brightness; Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُسْفِرَةٌ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 38] ﴿ضاحِكَةٌ مُسْتَبْشِرَةٌ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 39] — they shine and rejoice at what they are coming to of Allah's reward and mercy. "And faces will be blackened": their blackening is for what they are coming to of punishment; Allah said: ﴿وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَلَيْها غَبَرَةٌ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 40]. The (correct) speech is "تَسْوَدُّ" and "تَبْيَضُّ" with fatḥa on the tāʾ; the origin is "تَسْوَدِدُ" and "تَبْيَضِضُ", except that when two (identical) letters come together and both are voweled, the first is assimilated into the second. Many of the Arabs give kasra to this tāʾ: "تِسْوَدُّ", "تِبْيَضُّ". The reading is with fatḥa; the kasra is rare, except that many of the Arabs give kasra to this tāʾ to show that it is from your saying "أبْيَضُ" and "أسْوَدُ", as though the kasra were an indication that it is thus in the past tense [Translator's note: i.e. that the past tense begins with a kasra-bearing hamza: اِبْيَضَّ، اِسْوَدَّ.]. Some read "تَسْوادُّ" and "تَبْياضُّ", which is good in Arabic, except that the muṣḥaf has no alif in it, so I dislike it for contradicting it — granted that alifs are sometimes omitted (in writing) in the Quran, like the alif of "إبْراهِيمُ" and "إسْماعِيلُ", and like the alif of "اَلرَّحْمَنُ"; but there is consensus on pronouncing these alifs that are omitted in the written text, whereas "تَبْيَضُّ" and "تَسْوَدُّ" are by consensus without alif, so it ought not to be read with the alif.
His saying, Majestic and Exalted is He: ﴿فَأمّا الَّذِينَ اسْوَدَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ﴾ indicates that the reading is "تَسْوَدُّ"; whoever reads with the alif, "تَسْوادُّ" and "تَبْياضُّ", must read "فَأمّا الَّذِينَ اسْوادَّتْ وُجُوهُهم". The apodosis (jawāb) of "أمّا" is omitted together with the (verb of) saying; the meaning is: then it will be said to them: ﴿أكَفَرْتُمْ بَعْدَ إيمانِكُمْ﴾. The saying was omitted because there is an indication of it in the speech, and this is frequent in the Quran, as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿والمَلائِكَةُ يَدْخُلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِن كُلِّ بابٍ﴾ [al-Raʿd: 23] ﴿سَلامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ [al-Raʿd: 24], the meaning being: saying, "Peace be upon you"; and likewise His saying: ﴿وَإسْماعِيلُ رَبَّنا تَقَبَّلْ مِنّا﴾ [al-Baqara: 127], the meaning being: the two of them saying, "Our Lord, accept from us." This alif (أ) has the form of an interrogative, and its meaning is affirmation (taqrīr) and rebuke. It was said to them only ﴿أكَفَرْتُمْ بَعْدَ إيمانِكُمْ﴾ because they disbelieved in the Prophet ﷺ while they had believed in him before his being sent; and this is an address to the People of the Book.

zajjaj:107-107.t: His saying, Majestic and Exalted is He: ﴿فَفِي رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ هم فِيها خالِدُونَ﴾, that is: in the reward — to which Allah has brought them by mercy — they abide forever. He made known that the Garden is entered only by His mercy, even if the striver strives in obedience to Allah, because the blessings of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, short of the Garden, cannot be repaid by the striving of human beings. He said ﴿فَفِي رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ﴾ while intending the reward of Allah's mercy, just as He said: ﴿واسْألِ القَرْيَةَ﴾ [Yūsuf: 82], the meaning being: the people of the town; and as the Arabs say: "بَنُو فُلانٍ يَطَؤُهُمُ الطَّرِيقُ" ("the road treads on the Banū So-and-so"), meaning: the passers-by on the road tread on them. The mention of "فِيها" a second time is by way of tawkīd (emphasis).

zajjaj:108-108.t: His saying, Majestic and Exalted is He: ﴿تِلْكَ آياتُ اللَّهِ نَتْلُوها عَلَيْكَ بِالحَقِّ وما اللَّهُ يُرِيدُ ظُلْمًا لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾, that is: those which have been mentioned are the proofs and signs of Allah; We recite them to you, i.e. We make them known to you. ﴿وَما اللَّهُ يُرِيدُ ظُلْمًا لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾, that is: whomever Allah has made known that He will punish, He punishes him deservedly.

zajjaj:109-109.t:
His saying, Majestic and Exalted is He: ﴿وَإلى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الأُمُورُ﴾ — had it been "وَإلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُ الأُمُورُ", it would have been good, but repeating the name of Allah is more majestic and more emphatic. When something of majesty has been mentioned, the Arabs repeat its word overtly rather than as a pronoun. The grammarians recited the poet's saying:
لا أرى المَوْتَ يَسْبِقُ المَوْتَ شَيْءٌ ... نَغَّصَ المَوْتُ ذا الغِنى والفَقِيرا
(I see nothing outrunning death — death has spoiled (life) for the rich man and the poor.)
So they repeated the mention of death because of its majesty in their souls.

zajjaj:110-110.t:
His saying, Majestic and Exalted is He: ﴿كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخْرِجَتْ لِلنّاسِ﴾ — by it He means the community of Muhammad ﷺ. It was said concerning the meaning of ﴿كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخْرِجَتْ لِلنّاسِ﴾: you were (so) with Allah in the Preserved Tablet. And it was said: you have been, since you believed, the best community. Some said, regarding the meaning of "كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ": this address was originally directed to the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and it includes all the rest of the community of Muhammad. The condition of being best is what is in the text, namely His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَأْمُرُونَ بِالمَعْرُوفِ وتَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ المُنْكَرِ وتُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ﴾, that is: you affirm the oneness of Allah by believing in His Messenger, because whoever disbelieves in the Prophet ﷺ has not affirmed the oneness of Allah. That is because he claims that the miraculous signs which the Prophet ﷺ brought were of his own making, so he has made someone other than Allah do the act of Allah, whereas none but Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is capable of the signs of the prophets. What shows that His saying ﴿وَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ﴾ means: you acknowledge that Muhammad ﷺ is the Prophet of Allah, is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْ آمَنَ أهْلُ الكِتابِ لَكانَ خَيْرًا لَهُمْ﴾. The People of the Book disbelieved in the Prophet ﷺ and so became disbelievers in Allah. Then Allah made known that some of them — the few among them — believed in Allah, saying: ﴿مِنهُمُ المُؤْمِنُونَ وأكْثَرُهُمُ الفاسِقُونَ﴾. "اَلْفاسِقُ" is one who has gone out from the command of Allah.
Allah promised the Prophet ﷺ and the believers, concerning the People of the Book, that they would be given victory over them, and that no extermination or defeat would befall them from the People of the Book, saying: ﴿لَنْ يَضُرُّوكم إلا أذًى﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 111], that is: they will harm you with slander and distortion, but as for the final outcome, it will belong to the believers. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَئِنْ نَصَرُوهم لَيُوَلُّنَّ الأدْبارَ ثُمَّ لا يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ [al-Ḥashr: 12], meaning by it the People of the Book. And He made known to them in this verse that if they fought them, they would turn their backs to them and be deprived of victory; and so it was with the matter of the Jews.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Āl ʿImrān
﷽
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿الم﴾ ﴿اللَّهُ لا إلَهَ إلا هُوَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 2]: the readers agreed on giving the mīm a fatḥa. It has been reported from al-Ruʾāsī: ”المْ اَللَّهُ“ with a quiescent mīm, and some transmitted this reading from ʿĀṣim; but what is accurately recorded from ʿĀṣim, in the transmission of Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh, and [from] Abū ʿAmr, is the fatḥa of the mīm, and the fatḥa of the mīm is [the subject of] consensus. We have already explained the meaning of ”الم“.

The grammarians differed about the reason for the fatḥa of the mīm.
