One of the Basrans said: it is possible that the mīm was given fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and it is possible that the fatḥa of the hamza was cast onto it, because the letters of the alphabet are intended to be in pause (waqf); and this is also the view of the Kufans. Abū l-Ḥasan al-Akhfash mentioned that if the mīm were given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, so that one said ”المِ اللَّهُ“, it would be permissible. This is an error on the part of Abū l-Ḥasan, because before the mīm there is a yāʾ preceded by a kasra, so it is entitled to fatḥa for the meeting of two quiescent letters, and that is because of the heaviness of the kasra together with the yāʾ.

As for ﴿القَيُّومُ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 2], it has been reported from ʿUmar and Ibn Masʿūd, both of them, that they read: ”اَلْقَيّامُ“; and it has also been transmitted as ”اَلْقَيِّمُ“. What ought to be read is what is in the Muṣḥaf, namely ”اَلْقَيُّومُ“ with the wāw. ”اَلْقَيِّمُ“ is also good, fully [correct] and frequent in Arabic, but reading contrary to what is in the Muṣḥaf is not permissible, because the Muṣḥaf is agreed upon, and consensus is not to be opposed by a report whose soundness is not known. The meaning of ”اَلْقَيُّومُ“ is: the One who undertakes the management of all that He created — giving life, bringing into being, providing and causing death. The original form of ”قَيُّومٌ“ is ”قَيْوُومٌ“, except that when the yāʾ precedes the wāw with a sukūn, the wāw is changed [into yāʾ] for its sake and the yāʾ is assimilated into it. Likewise ”اَلْقَيّامُ“: its original form is ”اَلْقَيْوامُ“.

The meaning of ”الكِتابَ“ is: what has been written; the Qurʾān is called ”كِتابٌ“ because it is written. The meaning of ”يُكْتَبُ“ in the language is: [parts of it] are gathered one to another. ”اَلْكُتْبَةُ“ in the language is the stitch [of a leather bag], and its plural is ”كُتُبٌ“; and ”اَلْكَتِيبَةُ“ is a large detachment of an army, named so only because its parts are gathered together.

The meaning of ﴿مُصَدِّقًا لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 3] is: [confirming] the books that preceded it and the messengers who brought them.

zajjaj:3-3.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَأنْـزَلَ التَّوْراةَ والإنْجِيلَ﴾ ﴿مِن قَبْلُ هُدًى لِلنّاسِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 4], i.e. before the Qurʾān.

The grammarians differed over ”تَوْراةٌ“. The Kufans said: ”تَوْراةٌ“ may be [on the pattern] ”تَفْعَلَةٌ“, from ”وَرَيْتُ بِكَ زِنادِي“ (through you my fire-stick has struck fire); so the original in their view is ”تَوْرَيَةٌ“, except that the yāʾ was changed to alif because it was vowelled and preceded by fatḥa. But ”تَفْعَلَةٌ“ is hardly found in the language; they only said ”تَتْفَلَةٌ“ for ”تُتْفَلَةٌ“. One of them said: it may be ”تَفْعِلَةٌ“, like ”تَوْصِيَةٌ“, but changed from ”تَفْعِلَةٌ“ to ”تَفْعَلَةٌ“ — as though he would allow ”تَوْصاةٌ“ for ”تَوْصِيَةٌ“. This is poor; ”تَوْفاةٌ“ for ”تَوْفِيَةٌ“ is not established, nor ”تَوْقاةٌ“ for ”تَوْقِيَةٌ“. The Basrans said: its original [pattern] is ”فَوْعَلَةٌ“, and ”فَوْعَلَةٌ“ is frequent in the language, like ”اَلْحَوْقَلَةُ“ and ”دَوْخَلَةٌ“ and the like; and for everything about which you say ”فَوْعَلْتُ“, its maṣdar (verbal noun) is ”فَوْعَلَةٌ“. So its original in their view is ”وَوْرَيَةٌ“, but the first wāw was changed to tāʾ, as in ”تَوْلَجٌ“, which is really ”فَوْعَلٌ“ from ”وَلَجَتْ“, and as [the wāw] was changed in ”تُراثٌ“; the final yāʾ was also changed [to alif], because it was vowelled and preceded by fatḥa, by consensus. «[Translator's note: the Arabic of this last sentence is compressed («وكما قلبت في تراث، الياء الأخيرة، قلبت أيضاً…»); it is rendered here according to the evident sense.]»

And ”إنْجِيلٌ“ is ”إفْعِيلٌ“, from ”اَلنَّجْلُ“, which is the origin (al-aṣl); thus all the lexicographers say about ”إنْجِيلٌ“.

The meaning of ﴿مِن قَبْلُ هُدًى لِلنّاسِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 4] is: before the Qurʾān. The meaning of ﴿وَأنْـزَلَ الفُرْقانَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 4] is: that by which He distinguished between truth and falsehood; and it is reported from some of the exegetes that every book of Allah is a ”فُرْقانٌ“. The meaning of ﴿واللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ ذُو انْتِقامٍ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 4] is: everything has become humbled before Him through the trace of His making in it. And the meaning of ”ذُو انْتِقامٍ“ is: possessor of retributions (dhū anqām) against whoever disbelieves in Him, because mention of the disbelievers has occurred here. «[Translator's note: «أنقام» as printed; perhaps intended as a plural of «نقمة» or a misprint for «انتقام».]»

zajjaj:5-5.t: The meaning of ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَخْفى عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ في الأرْضِ ولا في السَّماءِ﴾ is: it is manifest to Him, and He — Majestic and Mighty is He — brought it into being.

zajjaj:6-6.t: The meaning of ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي يُصَوِّرُكم في الأرْحامِ كَيْفَ يَشاءُ﴾ is: according to what He wills of largeness, smallness, colour, weakness and strength; and He — Majestic and Mighty is He — has wisdom in that, as He said: ﴿لا إلَهَ إلا هو العَزِيزُ الحَكِيمُ﴾. «[Translator's note: the text reads «وصِغَرِ لَوْنٍ» ("smallness of colour"); rendered as a list, which the sense requires.]»

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿مِنهُ آياتٌ مُحْكَماتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ الكِتابِ وأُخَرُ مُتَشابِهاتٌ﴾: it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās — may Allah be pleased with him and his father — that he said: ”اَلْمُحْكَماتُ“ are the verses at the end of al-Anʿām, namely His saying — Exalted is He —: ﴿قُلْ تَعالَوْا أتْلُ ما حَرَّمَ رَبُّكم عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 151] to the end of these verses; and the mutashābih (ambiguous) verses are ”الم“ and ”المر“, and what of these and their like was ambiguous to the Jews.

Others said: the meaning of ”مِنهُ آياتٌ مُحْكَماتٌ“ is: they have been made firm (uḥkimat) in clarity, so that when the hearer hears them he does not need their interpretation, because they are evident and clear — like the stories of the prophets that Allah related, which the People of the Book acknowledged, and what Allah reported about the bringing-into-being of creation, from His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿ثُمَّ خَلَقْنا النُّطْفَةَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقْنا العَلَقَةَ مُضْغَةً فَخَلَقْنا المُضْغَةَ عِظامًا فَكَسَوْنا العِظامَ لَحْمًا ثُمَّ أنْشَأْناهُ خَلْقًا آخَرَ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 14]. This the people acknowledged, and they affirmed that Allah is their Creator; and [likewise] what Allah reported of His creating every living thing from water, and the fruits He created for them, and the ships and winds He made subservient to them, and the like. This is what they did not deny. But they denied what required reflection and contemplation of them: that Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — will resurrect them after they have become dust. So He said: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا هَلْ نَدُلُّكم عَلى رَجُلٍ يُنَبِّئُكم إذا مُزِّقْتُمْ كُلَّ مُمَزَّقٍ إنَّكم لَفي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾ [Sabaʾ: 7] ﴿أفْتَرى عَلى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا أمْ بِهِ جِنَّةٌ﴾ [Sabaʾ: 8], and ﴿وَكانُوا يَقُولُونَ أإذا مِتْنا وكُنّا تُرابًا وعِظامًا أإنّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 47] ﴿أوَآباؤُنا الأوَّلُونَ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 48]. This is what was ambiguous (mutashābih) to them. So Allah informed them of the way by which they ought to infer that this which was ambiguous to them is like the evident, if they contemplate it and reflect on it. He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَضَرَبَ لَنا مَثَلا ونَسِيَ خَلْقَهُ قالَ مَن يُحْيِي العِظامَ وهي رَمِيمٌ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 78] ﴿قُلْ يُحْيِيها الَّذِي أنْشَأها أوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وهو بِكُلِّ خَلْقٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 79] ﴿الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكم مِنَ الشَّجَرِ الأخْضَرِ نارًا﴾ [Yā Sīn: 80], and He said: ﴿أوَلَيْسَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ بِقادِرٍ عَلى أنْ يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَهُمْ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 81]; i.e. since you have acknowledged the human being and the first beginning, what is it you deny of the resurrection and the raising? «[Translator's note: «بالإنسان» as printed; the sense suggests «بالإنشاء» ("the bringing into being").]» This is the view of many people, and it is clear and evident; and the first view is also good.

As for ”أُخَرُ“, it is a diptote (ghayr maṣrūf). Sībawayh and al-Khalīl held that ”أُخَرُ“ departed from its sisters and from the basis on which its sisters are formed, because the origin of ”أُخَرُ“ is that it be an adjective with the alif and lām, as you say ”اَلصُّغْرى“ and ”اَلصُّغَرُ“, ”اَلْكُبْرى“ and ”اَلْكُبَرُ“. So when it deviated (ʿudila) from the course of the alif and lām and from the origin of ”أفْعَلُ مِنكَ“, being among the words that are only ever adjectives, it was denied declension (tanwīn).

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَأمّا الَّذِينَ في قُلُوبِهِمْ زَيْغٌ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ ما تَشابَهَ مِنهُ﴾: ”اَلزَّيْغُ“ is deviation and swerving from the right course; one says ”زاغَ، يَزِيغُ“ when he deviates. The meaning of ﴿ابْتِغاءَ الفِتْنَةِ﴾ is: they do that seeking fitna and seeking the interpretation. Fitna in the language is of several kinds. The kind these people sought is the corruption of mutual relations, in religion and in wars. ”اَلْفِتْنَةُ“ in the language is infatuation with a thing and excess in it; one says: ”فُلانٌ مَفْتُونٌ في طَلَبِ الدُّنْيا“ (so-and-so is infatuated with seeking worldly things), i.e. he has gone to excess in seeking it and exceeded the measure. And ”اَلْفِتْنَةُ“ is testing, as in His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ فَتَنّا بَعْضَهم بِبَعْضٍ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 53], i.e. We tested. The meaning of their seeking its interpretation (taʾwīl) is that they sought the interpretation of their resurrection and their being brought back to life; so Allah made known that its interpretation and its time are known only to Allah. The proof of that is His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إلا تَأْوِيلَهُ يَوْمَ يَأْتِي تَأْوِيلُهُ يَقُولُ الَّذِينَ نَسُوهُ مِن قَبْلُ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 53], i.e. on the day they see what they were promised of the resurrection, the raising and the punishment, those who forgot it before will say — i.e. those who abandoned it, and abandoned what the Prophet ﷺ conveyed from Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — about their resurrection and their recompense.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿قَدْ جاءَتْ رُسُلُ رَبِّنا بِالحَقِّ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 53], i.e. we have seen what the messengers told us. So the complete stop (al-waqf al-tāmm) is His saying: ﴿وَما يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ إلا اللَّهُ﴾, i.e. no one other than Allah knows when the resurrection will be. The meaning of ﴿والرّاسِخُونَ في العِلْمِ﴾ is: those firmly established; one says ”رَسَخَ الشَّيْءُ، يَرْسَخُ، رُسُوخًا“ when it is firm. That is: they say: we affirm that Allah will resurrect us, and they believe that the resurrection is true just as the first creation is true, and they say: ﴿كُلٌّ مِن عِنْدِ رَبِّنا﴾. What indicates that they did not contemplate the matter that was ambiguous to them is His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَما يَذَّكَّرُ إلا أُولُو الألْبابِ﴾, i.e. possessors of intellects; i.e. none takes heed of the Qurʾān and of what the Messenger ﷺ brought except those possessed of minds.

zajjaj:54-54.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَمَكَرُوا ومَكَرَ اللَّهُ واللَّهُ خَيْرُ الماكِرِينَ﴾. ”اَلْمَكْرُ“ (scheming) on the part of creatures is cunning and deception, while makr on the part of Allah is requital for that; it was called by the name of that because it is a requital for it. Just as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿اللَّهُ يَسْتَهْزِئُ بِهِمْ﴾ [al-Baqara: 15] — He made His requiting them for mockery with punishment take the wording of mockery; and as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَجَزاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ سَيِّئَةٌ مِثْلُها﴾ [al-Shūrā: 40] — the first is an evil deed, and the requital for it was called by its name, though in reality it is not an evil deed. It is also possible that Allah's makr is His leading them on step by step from where they do not know, for Allah set Persia over them, and it overcame them and killed them. The evidence for that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿الم﴾ [al-Rūm: 1] ﴿غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ﴾ [al-Rūm: 2] ﴿فِي أدْنى الأرْضِ﴾ [al-Rūm: 3]. It has also been said in the exegesis that Allah's makr against them was in the matter of ʿĪsā: he ﷺ was in a house in which there was an opening; a man entered to kill him, and ʿĪsā was raised from the house, and the man came out in his likeness, telling them that he was not in the house, so they killed him. The sum of makr on Allah's part is His requiting them for what they did.

zajjaj:55-55.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إذْ قالَ اللَّهُ يا عِيسى﴾. ”عِيسى“ is a foreign name, altered from its foreign wording to this form. It is a diptote when definite, because foreignness and definiteness are combined in it. The model of its derivation from the speech of the Arabs is that ”عِيسى“ is on the pattern ”فِعْلى“, and the alif could be for the feminine, in which case it would be a diptote both when definite and indefinite, and its derivation would be from one of two things: one of them ”اَلْعَيَسُ“, which is whiteness in camels; and the other from ”اَلْعَوْسُ“ and ”اَلْعِياسَةُ“, except that the wāw was changed to yāʾ because of the kasra before it. As for ʿĪsā (peace be upon him), the name is altered from ”يَشُوعُ“ (Yashūʿ); so say the people of Syriac.
The grammarians said concerning the meaning of His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ ورافِعُكَ إلَيَّ ومُطَهِّرُكَ﴾ that there is fronting and postponement (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr); the meaning is: "I will raise you, purify you, and take you in full (mutawaffīka)". Some of them said: the meaning follows this wording, like His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿اللَّهُ يَتَوَفّى الأنْفُسَ حِينَ مَوْتِها﴾ [al-Zumar: 42]; so the meaning, according to the view of these, is that the speech stands on this wording (as it is ordered).
As for ﴿وَجاعِلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوكَ فَوْقَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾, the reading is with the tanwīn (nunation) dropped (i.e. jāʿilu in a genitive construct). Tanwīn is permissible (grammatically), but you do not read with it unless a transmission of it has been established. As for the meaning of ﴿فَوْقَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ﴾, there are two views on it. One is that they are above them in argument and in establishing proof; the other is that they are above them in power, ascendancy and dominance. And "those who followed you" would be Muḥammad ﷺ and those who followed him; so they are aided and uppermost.

zajjaj:56-56.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَأُعَذِّبُهم عَذابًا شَدِيدًا في الدُّنْيا والآخِرَةِ﴾. The punishment in this world is the killing which has befallen them and befalls them, the capture of their offspring, and the taking of the jizya; and the punishment of the Hereafter is the Fire which Allah has prepared for them.
﴿وَما لَهم مِن ناصِرِينَ﴾, that is: they have no one to protect them in this world, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made Islam prevail over their religion and given dominance to its people; and no one will help them in the Hereafter against the punishment of Allah.

zajjaj:57-57.t: The meaning of ﴿واللَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ الظّالِمِينَ﴾ is: He does not have mercy on them, He punishes them, and He does not praise them with good. This is the meaning of hatred on the part of Allah; and the meaning of love on His part is mercy, forgiveness and beautiful praise.

zajjaj:58-58.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ذَلِكَ نَتْلُوهُ عَلَيْكَ﴾, that is: the narrative that has gone before, We recite it to you; ﴿مِنَ الآياتِ﴾, that is: among the clear signs indicating the establishment of your message, since they were reports which only a reader of a book, or one who has been taught, or one to whom they were revealed would know. It is known that the Prophet ﷺ was unlettered: he did not write, nor did he read books, being unacquainted with studying them and benefiting from them, and no one among people taught him ﷺ. So nothing remains but revelation; and telling these reports, on which the People of the Book agree in agreement with his account of them, is among the miraculous signs.
The meaning of ﴿والذِّكْرِ الحَكِيمِ﴾ is: possessed of wisdom in its composition, its arrangement, and its making clear the benefits in it. It is also valid that ”ذَلِكَ“ be in the sense of ”اَلَّذِي“ (a relative noun), and ”نَتْلُوهُ“ be its ṣila (relative clause), so that the meaning is: "that which We recite to you is of the signs and the wise reminder"; then ”ذَلِكَ“ would be the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) would be ”مِنَ الآياتِ“.

zajjaj:59-59.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسى عِنْدَ اللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ آدَمَ خَلَقَهُ مِن تُرابٍ﴾. ”آدَمَ“: we have explained that it is fully declined [Translator's note: so in the text (يَنْصَرِفُ); the name آدَم is a diptote in the Quranic text, and the printed wording may be defective], and that his name is taken from ”أدِيمُ الأرْضِ“, which is the surface of the earth; and for this reason one whose colour resembles the colour of the earth is called ”آدَمُ“. ﴿خَلَقَهُ مِن تُرابٍ﴾ is not connected to ”آدَمَ“ (as a qualifier); it only explains the story of Ādam. It is not permissible in speech to say ”مَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ قامَ“, because Zayd is definite: ”قامَ“ is not connected to it, nor is it joined to it (as a ṣila), and it cannot be a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the past cannot be a state in which (the action) came. But you say ”مَثَلُكَ مَثَلُ زَيْدٍ“ ("your likeness is the likeness of Zayd"), meaning that you resemble him in his action, then you relate Zayd's story and say "he did such-and-such". It was said that his likeness is as the likeness of Ādam only because Allah brought Ādam into being without a father — He created him from dust; so just as He created Ādam without a father, likewise He created ʿĪsā (peace be upon him). It is narrated in the exegesis: «A group of Christians from Najrān came to the Prophet ﷺ and said to him: "You have reviled our master." He said: "And who is your master?" They said: "ʿĪsā." He said: "And what did I say about him?" They said: "You said that he is a servant." He ﷺ said: "That is no disgrace for my brother, nor a defect; he is a servant, and I am a servant." They said: "Then show us his like." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down: ﴿إنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسى عِنْدَ اللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ آدَمَ﴾ to the end of the verse.»

zajjaj:60-60.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿الحَقُّ مِن رَبِّكَ﴾ is in the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). The meaning: what We have told you in the story of ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) is the truth from your Lord. ﴿فَلا تَكُنْ مِنَ المُمْتَرِينَ﴾, that is: among the doubters. The address to the Prophet ﷺ is an address to (all) creatures, because the Prophet ﷺ did not doubt the story of ʿĪsā. The meaning of ”مِن رَبِّكَ“ is: it has come to you from your Lord.

zajjaj:61-61.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَمَن حاجَّكَ فِيهِ﴾, that is: concerning ʿĪsā; ﴿مِن بَعْدِ ما جاءَكَ مِنَ العِلْمِ﴾. This was said to him after the decisive proofs and arguments establishing the matter of ʿĪsā — that he is a servant — had been revealed to him. So he was commanded to engage in mubāhala (mutual imprecation) after the argument had been established, because the argument had reached the utmost in clarity. Allah commanded that he gather together with the women and sons of the believers, and that he call them to gather themselves, their fathers and their women, and then they would invoke earnestly (yabtahilūn). The meaning of ”اَلِابْتِهالُ“ in the language is exerting oneself to the utmost in supplication, and its origin is mutual cursing. One says ”بَهَلَهُ اللَّهُ“, i.e. Allah cursed him; and the meaning of "Allah cursed him" is: Allah distanced him from His mercy. One says ”ناقَةٌ باهِلٌ، وباهِلَةٌ“ when she has no udder-tie on her, and ”قَدْ أبْهَلَ الرَّجُلُ ناقَتَهُ“ when he has left her without an udder-tie, and ”رَجُلٌ باهِلٌ“ when he has no staff with him. So the interpretation of ”اَلْبَهْلُ“ in the language is distancing and separation from a thing. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called them to the mubāhala for two reasons, both of which make clear that their scholars had come to realise that the matter of the Prophet ﷺ was true: because when they refused to engage in mutual cursing, their refusal showed that they knew that if they engaged him in mubāhala something hateful would befall them; and because when they abandoned the mubāhala, that showed their weakness, and (showed) to whoever had no knowledge that their flight from the mubāhala is evidence that they are liars and that the Prophet ﷺ is truthful. It has been said that some of them said to others: "If you engage him in mubāhala, the valley will blaze upon you with fire, and no Christian man or woman will remain until the Day of Resurrection." It is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "«Had they engaged me in mubāhala, the valley would have blazed upon them with fire, and no Christian man or woman would have remained until the Day of Resurrection.»"
This is a place in which one should look carefully, so that the believers may know clearly what they are upon, and what misguidance those who oppose them are upon; for no one has narrated that they engaged the Prophet ﷺ in mubāhala, nor that they accepted that.

zajjaj:62-62.t: The meaning of His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنَّ هَذا لَهو القَصَصُ الحَقُّ﴾ is: this which We have revealed to you of these clear proofs and arguments which We have given you is indeed the true narrative. It is valid that ”هو“ here be a faṣl (separating pronoun) — which the Kufans call ʿimād (support) — and that "the narrative" be the khabar (predicate) of ”إنَّ“. It is also valid that ”هو“ be a mubtadaʾ (subject) and ”اَلْقَصَصُ“ its khabar, the two together being the khabar of ”إنَّ“. As for the meaning of ﴿وَما مِن إلَهٍ إلا اللَّهُ﴾: ”مِن“ entered as tawkīd (emphasis) and as an indication of the negation of all those whom the polytheists claimed to be gods — i.e. that ʿĪsā is not a god, because they claimed he is a god. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that there is no god but He, and that one to whom Allah has given signs which created beings are incapable of, that does not take him out of servitude to Allah, and calling him "a god" is disbelief in Allah. The meaning of ﴿العَزِيزُ﴾ is the One whom nothing can frustrate, and ﴿الحَكِيمُ﴾ is the Possessor of wisdom, who does nothing but what is wisdom.

zajjaj:63-63.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَإنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِالمُفْسِدِينَ﴾, that is: if they turn away from the clear explanation you have brought, then Allah knows who among His creatures does corruption, and He will requite him for his corruption.

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿رَبَّنا لا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنا بَعْدَ إذْ هَدَيْتَنا﴾, i.e. do not make them swerve from guidance and the right course; i.e. do not lead us astray after You have guided us. It has also been said: ”﴿لا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنا﴾“: do not bind us in worship to what would be a cause of the swerving of our hearts. Both are good.

zajjaj:9-9.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿رَبَّنا إنَّكَ جامِعُ النّاسِ لِيَوْمٍ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾ points to the interpretation of His saying: ﴿وَما يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ إلا اللَّهُ والرّاسِخُونَ في العِلْمِ يَقُولُونَ آمَنّا بِهِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 7]. Their saying ”﴿إنَّكَ جامِعُ النّاسِ لِيَوْمٍ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾“ is an affirmation of the resurrection and a proof that they opposed those who follow the ambiguous (al-mutashābih), because those who sought the ambiguous are the ones who denied the resurrection. ﴿لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾: there is no doubt about it; this has been explained exhaustively earlier in our book.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُخْلِفُ المِيعادَ﴾ may be a quotation of the monotheists' words, and may be a statement from Allah. It is also permissible to give fatḥa: ”أنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُخْلِفُ المِيعادَ“, and then the meaning would be: [You are] the gatherer of mankind because You do not break the promise; i.e. You have informed us of that, and we do not doubt it.

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ هم وقُودُ النّارِ﴾, i.e. the disbelievers are punished, and they are the fuel of themselves: every time their skins and bones are roasted by the burning, they are given other skins in exchange, so He punishes them through their skins and bones.

zajjaj:11-11.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ والَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ﴾, i.e. like the case of Pharaoh's people, and like the affair of Pharaoh's people — thus the lexicographers said. My view on it — and Allah knows best — is that ”دَأْبِ“ here means their exertion in their disbelief and their banding together against the Prophet ﷺ, like the banding together of Pharaoh's people against Moses — peace be upon him.

The position of the kāf is nominative: it is in the position of the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject); the meaning is: their habit is like the habit of Pharaoh's people, and ”كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ والَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ“. One says: ”دَأبْتُ، أدْأبُ، دَأْبًا، ودُؤُوبًا“ when you exert yourself in a thing. It is not valid for the kāf to be in the position of the accusative governed by ”كَفَرُوا“, because ”كَفَرُوا“ is within the ṣila (relative clause) of ”اَلَّذِينَ“: it is not valid [to construe it as] "those who disbelieved like the disbelief of Pharaoh's people", because the kāf is outside the ṣila, and what is in the ṣila does not govern it.

zajjaj:12-12.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَتُغْلَبُونَ﴾, and it is [also] read ”سَيُغْلَبُونَ“. Whoever reads with tāʾ, it is for direct quotation and address, i.e. say to them in your address: you will be overcome. Whoever says ”سَيُغْلَبُونَ“, the meaning is: convey to them that they will be overcome. In this there is the greatest sign for the Prophet ﷺ, because he informed them of what had not yet happened — he informed them of something unseen — and then the truth of what he had informed them became clear, because he ﷺ overcame them all, as he had informed them. The meaning of ﴿وَبِئْسَ المِهادُ﴾ is: evil is the abode, and evil is the bed.

zajjaj:13-13.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿قَدْ كانَ لَكم آيَةٌ في فِئَتَيْنِ التَقَتا﴾: ”آيَةٌ“ is a sign among the signs of the Prophet ﷺ that point to his truthfulness. ”اَلْفِئَةُ“ in the language is a party (firqa), and it is taken from their saying ”فَأوْتُ رَأْسَهُ بِالسَّيْفِ“ and ”فَأيْتُهُ“, when I split it [with the sword]. The meaning of ”فِئَتَيْنِ“ is: two parties.

﴿فِئَةٌ تُقاتِلُ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وأُخْرى كافِرَةٌ﴾: the nominative and the genitive are both permissible. Whoever puts it in the nominative, the meaning is: one of them fights in the path of Allah and the other is disbelieving. Whoever puts it in the genitive makes ”فِئَةٍ تُقاتِلُ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وأُخْرى كافِرَةٍ“ a badal (substitute) for ”فِئَتَيْنِ“; the meaning is: there was for you a sign in a party fighting in the path of Allah and in another that was disbelieving. They recited the verse of Kuthayyir in two ways:
؎وَكُنْتُ كَذِي رِجْلَيْنِ رِجْلٌ صَحِيحَةٌ ∗∗∗ ورِجْلٌ رَمى فِيها الزَّمانُ فَشُلَّتِ
(I was like one with two legs: one leg sound, and one leg that time struck so that it withered.)
And they also recited:
؎رِجْلٍ صَحِيحَةٍ ∗∗∗ ورِجْلٍ رَمى فِيها الزَّمانُ
as a badal for ”اَلرِّجْلَيْنِ“.

The lexicographers differed about His saying: ﴿يَرَوْنَهم مِثْلَيْهِمْ رَأْيَ العَيْنِ﴾, and we shall explain what they said, if Allah wills, and what the right interpretation is — and Allah knows best. Al-Farrāʾ held that the meaning of ”يَرَوْنَهم مِثْلَيْهِمْ“ is: they see them as three times their number. He said: because when you say ”عِنْدِي ألْفٌ وأحْتاجُ إلى مِثْلِها“ (I have a thousand and I need the like of it), you need two thousand, so it is as if you said ”أحْتاجُ إلى مِثْلَيْها“ (I need twice it); and when you say ”عِنْدِي ألْفٌ وأحْتاجُ إلى مِثْلَيْها“, you need three thousand. This is a matter of error; there is a clear error in it with respect to all measures and all things, because we understand the "like" (mithl) of a thing only as what is equal to it, and we understand its "two likes" (mithlayhi) as what equals it twice over; if we do not know what the "like" is, distinction is void. He only said this because the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ were three hundred and fourteen men and the polytheists were nine hundred and fifty men. So what he said fails in the wording, and fails in the meaning of pointing to the sign that is miraculous, because if they saw them as they actually were, this would not be a sign. And if he claims that the sign in this is the few overcoming the many, he is also wrong, because the few overcoming the many is something that always occurs. So what he said fails in the language and in the meaning.

Rather, the sign in this is that the polytheists were nine hundred and fifty and the Muslims were three hundred and fourteen, and Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — showed the polytheists that the Muslims were fewer than three hundred. Allah had informed the Muslims that a hundred would overcome two hundred, so He showed them the polytheists in the measure [in which] He had informed them that they would overcome them, in order to strengthen their hearts; and He showed the polytheists the Muslims as fewer than the [actual] number of the Muslims, then, together with that, He cast terror into their hearts, so they kept seeing a small number together with intense terror, until they were overcome. The proof of the correctness of this view is the saying of Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَإذْ يُرِيكُمُوهم إذِ التَقَيْتُمْ في أعْيُنِكم قَلِيلا ويُقَلِّلُكم في أعْيُنِهِمْ لِيَقْضِيَ اللَّهُ أمْرًا كانَ مَفْعُولا﴾ [al-Anfāl: 44]. This is what contains a sign: that a thing is seen contrary to its [actual] form — and Allah knows best.

The accusative of ”فِئَةٌ تُقاتِلُ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وأُخْرى كافِرَةٌ“ is also permissible, though I know of no one who read it so. Its accusative is from two angles: one of them is the ḥāl (circumstantial), the meaning being: they met, one believing and one disbelieving; and its accusative is also permissible on [the implied verb] ”أعْنِي فِئَةً تُقاتِلُ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وأُخْرى كافِرَةً“ (I mean a party fighting in the path of Allah and another disbelieving).

zajjaj:112-112.t:
His saying, Majestic and Exalted is He: ﴿ضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذِّلَّةُ أيْنَ ما ثُقِفُوا إلا بِحَبْلٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وحَبْلٍ مِنَ النّاسِ﴾ — "اَلْحَبْلُ" (the rope) is the covenant. Allah made known that, after the might they had been in, they would reach a degree of humiliation that the people of Mecca did not reach — and they had been people of strength and wealth. So Allah made known that they would be humiliated forever, unless they are given strength by the protection (dhimma) granted to them in Islam. What comes after the exception (istithnāʾ) is not of (the same kind as) the first [Translator's note: i.e. it is a disjoint exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ).]: they are humiliated, except that they take refuge in the covenant when they are given it.
And Allah made known that this severe punishment of theirs was made their punishment in this world and the Hereafter because of the gravity of what they committed, saying, Majestic and Exalted is He: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّهم كانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ ويَقْتُلُونَ الأنْبِياءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ﴾. The position of "ذَلِكَ" is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the meaning is: "their affair is that", and "that is what they deserved for their disbelief and their killing of the prophets". He repeated the mention of "ذَلِكَ" a second time, saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِما عَصَوْا وكانُوا يَعْتَدُونَ﴾. "اَلِاعْتِداءُ" (transgression) is overstepping in everything, overstepping the measure. The meaning is: (that is) what it deserved, because of their disbelief.

zajjaj:113-113.t:
Then Allah made known that they are not equal, saying: ﴿لَيْسُوا سَواءً﴾ — and this is a complete stop (waqf al-tamām) — that is: those of the People of the Book whom we have mentioned are not alike. Abū ʿUbayda said: "لَيْسُوا سَواءً": "لَيْسَ" is put in the plural while it comes first, as the speaker said: "أكَلُونِي البَراغِيثُ" ("the fleas ate me", with plural marking on the fronted verb), and as He said: ﴿عَمُوا وصَمُّوا كَثِيرٌ مِنهُمْ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 71]. This is not as he said, because mention of the People of the Book has already occurred; so Allah informed that they are not equal, saying "لَيْسُوا سَواءً", and then announced their division, saying: ﴿مِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ أُمَّةٌ قائِمَةٌ﴾. The lexicographers said: the meaning of "قائِمَةٌ" is "upright (mustaqīma)", but they did not explain the reality of this. Al-Akhfash mentioned that the meaning of "أُمَّةٌ قائِمَةٌ" is: people of an upright way (dhawū umma qāʾima). "اَلْأُمَّةُ" is the way (al-ṭarīqa), from "أمَمْتُ الشَّيْءَ" ("I headed for the thing"), when you aim for it. So the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: among the People of the Book is an upright umma, i.e. people of an upright way. Al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī said:
؎حَلَفْتُ فَلَمْ أتْرُكْ لِنَفْسِكَ رِيبَةً ∗∗∗ وهَلْ يَأْثَمَن ذُو أُمَّةٍ وهْوَ طائِعُ؟!
(I swore, and left no doubt for your soul — and would a man of (religious) way commit a sin while obedient?!)
That is: would one who follows one of the ways of religion sin while he is obedient?! So the meaning is only that those who killed the prophets without right are not equal to those who recite the signs of Allah in the hours of the night while being people of an upright way.
The meaning of ﴿آناءَ اللَّيْلِ﴾ is: the hours of the night. The lexicographers said: the singular of "آناءُ اللَّيْلِ" is "إنْيٌ", and "آناءُ" is like "نِحْيٌ" and "أنْحاءُ". The lexicographers recited, concerning this, the poet's saying:
؎حُلْوٌ ومُرٌّ كَطَعْمِ القِدْحِ مِرَّتُهُ ∗∗∗ بِكُلِّ إنْيٍ حَذاهُ اللَّيْلُ يَنْتَعِلُ
(Sweet and bitter, his toughness like the taste of the arrow-shaft; in every hour of the night that it shod him with, he puts on sandals [i.e. he travels at every hour of the night].)
They said: its singular is "إنًى", like "مِعًى" and "أمْعاءُ"; and al-Akhfash related "إنْوٌ".
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهم يَسْجُدُونَ﴾ means: while they pray, because recitation is not (done) in prostration; prayer was referred to by prostration only because prostration is the utmost of the humility, submissiveness and supplication in it. The meaning of "يَتْلُونَ" in the language is: they make parts of something follow one another; and "قَدِ اسْتَتْلاكَ الشَّيْءُ" is said when a thing makes you follow it. The poet said:
؎قَدْ جَعَلَتْ دَلْوِي تَسْتَلِينِي ∗∗∗ ولا أُحِبُّ تَبْعَ القَرِينِ
إنْ لَمْ يُرِدْ سَماحَتِي ولِينِي
(My bucket has begun to make me follow it, and I do not like following a companion, if he does not want my generosity and gentleness.)
Some of the lexicographers said: the meaning is: among them is an upright community, and a community otherwise; and he recited for this the poet's saying:
؎عَصانِي إلَيْها القَلْبُ إنِّي لِأمْرِهِ ∗∗∗ سَمِيعٌ فَما أدْرِي أرُشْدٌ طِلابُها
(My heart disobeyed me (in going) to her — indeed I heed its command — and I do not know: is seeking her right guidance?)
and he did not say "or is it in error?", because there is an indication of it in the speech. He said: the Arabs leave this implied when they know the like of this — (when) they know the meaning. What he said is a gross error in a place such as this, because mention of the People of the Book has occurred in this account, (namely) that they used to disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right; then Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, made known that among them are the believers, who are an upright community — so what need is there to say "not upright"? What was started with here was only what most of them did of disbelief and hostility toward the Prophet ﷺ; then He mentioned those who were distinct from these. It is mentioned in the exegesis that this refers to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his companions. The meaning of ﴿وَيَأْمُرُونَ بِالمَعْرُوفِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 114] here is: they command following the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ المُنْكَرِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 114]: (they forbid) persisting in hostility toward him ﷺ.

zajjaj:115-115.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَما يَفْعَلُوا مِن خَيْرٍ فَلَنْ يُكْفَرُوهُ﴾ was read with yāʾ and with tāʾ, and both are correct, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُ﴾ [al-Zalzala: 7]; so the address is to all of creation. And whoever said "فَلَنْ تُكْفَرُوهُ", it is for these (people) mentioned, and all the rest of creation is included with them in that. [Translator's note: the passage is translated as printed; which reading is meant by "the address is to all of creation" is not stated explicitly.] The position of "يَفْعَلُوا" is jussive (jazm) by the conditional, which is "ما", and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is "فَلَنْ يُكْفَرُوهُ".

zajjaj:116-116.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَنْ تُغْنِيَ عَنْهم أمْوالُهم ولا أوْلادُهم مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا﴾, that is: their children will not protect them from what is descending upon them. [Translator's note: the words "wealth is mentioned" are added for clarity.] Wealth is mentioned because they inclined toward wealth in their obstinacy against the Prophet ﷺ, since leadership was established for them — I mean the leaders of the Jews — only through their obstinacy against the Prophet ﷺ. The proof that they earned (gain) by that is His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ يَكْتُبُونَ الكِتابَ بِأيْدِيهِمْ ثُمَّ يَقُولُونَ هَذا مِن عِنْدِ اللَّهِ لِيَشْتَرُوا بِهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلا فَوَيْلٌ لَهم مِمّا كَتَبَتْ أيْدِيهِمْ ووَيْلٌ لَهم مِمّا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 79].

zajjaj:117-117.t: Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that the likeness of what they spend in their mutual backing against the Prophet ﷺ, in the harm (it brings) to them, is ﴿كَمَثَلِ رِيحٍ فِيها صِرٌّ﴾ — "اَلصِّرُّ" is intense cold — ﴿أصابَتْ حَرْثَ قَوْمٍ﴾, that is: the crops of a people ﴿ظَلَمُوا أنْفُسَهُمْ﴾, so Allah punished them by taking away their crops, ﴿فَأهْلَكَتْهُ﴾. So He made known that the harm of their spending upon them is like the harm of this wind to this crop. It was said: the people of Mecca are meant by it, when they cooperated and spent wealth on backing one another against the Prophet ﷺ. Some said: "the likeness of what they spend", i.e. the likeness of their deeds in their polytheism, is like the likeness of this wind; and "صِرٌّ" was placed in it, meaning: a sound — and this can be derived in the language. He placed a sound in it only because he placed a fire in it, as though it were a fire that burned the crop; so "اَلصِّرُّ" according to this view is the sound of the flame of fire. All of this is not impossible, and its sum is that what is spent in mutual backing upon enmity toward the religion is harmful, destroying its people in the immediate (world) and the deferred.

zajjaj:118-118.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا بِطانَةً مِن دُونِكم لا يَأْلُونَكم خَبالا﴾ — "اَلْبِطانَةُ" are the intimates who are taken into one's inner confidence and with whom one is at ease. One says: "فُلانٌ بِطانَةٌ لِفُلانٍ" ("So-and-so is an intimate of so-and-so"), i.e. close to him and familiar with him. So the meaning is that the believers were commanded not to be intimate with the hypocrites nor with the Jews, because these spared no effort in confusing the believers; so they were commanded not to be intimate with them, lest they corrupt their religion for them. And Allah informed the believers that they "لا يَأْلُونَهم خَبالًا" (spare them no ruin), i.e. they spare no effort in casting them into what harms them. The origin of "اَلْخَبالُ" in the language is the loss (going away) of a thing. The poet said:
؎أبَنِي سُلَيْمى لَسْتُمُ لِيَدٍ ∗∗∗ إلّا يَدًا مَخْبُولَةَ العَضُدِ
(O sons of Sulaymā, you are no (strong) hand — except a hand whose upper arm is crippled.)
That is: its upper arm has gone. ﴿وَدُّوا ما عَنِتُّمْ﴾, that is: they wished for your distress. The meaning of "اَلْعَنَتُ" is bringing hardship upon a person. One says: "فُلانٌ مُتَعَنِّتٌ فُلانًا", i.e. he aims at bringing hardship and harm upon him. And one says: "قَدْ عَنِتَ العَظْمُ، يَعْنَتُ، عَنَتًا" when something befalls the bone after it has been set. The origin of all this is from their saying: "أكَمَةٌ عُنُوتٌ" ("a hard hillock"), when it is high and its path is hard going. So the interpretation of "أعْنَتُّ فُلانًا" is: I subjected him to hardship.

zajjaj:119-119.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ها أنْتُمْ أُولاءِ تُحِبُّونَهم ولا يُحِبُّونَكُمْ﴾ is an address to the believers, in which they were informed that the hypocrites among the People of the Book do not love them, while they (the believers) accompany these hypocrites with the kindness and good counsel that a lover shows, and that the hypocrites are the opposite of that. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, informed the believers of what the hypocrites concealed — and this is one of the signs (miracles) of the Prophet ﷺ. One of the grammarians said: when the Arabs come to a pronoun (ism mukannā) that has been qualified by "هَذا", they put it between "ها" and "ذا"; so one asks "أيْنَ أنْتَ؟" ("Where are you?"), and the one answering says "هَأنَذا" ("Here I am"). He said: that is when they intend the sense of taqrīb (presentative proximity). He said: they did this only to distinguish between taqrīb and other (uses). The meaning of taqrīb according to him is that you do not intend to give information about this noun, as when you say "هَذا زَيْدٌ" ("This is Zayd"). Our view on "هَذا" is that the usage with the pronoun is merely more frequent — I mean separating "ها" from "ذا" — because the particle of alerting (tanbīh) being placed next to the pronoun is clearer.
If someone says "ها زَيْدٌ ذا" or "هَذا زَيْدٌ", it is permissible; there is no disagreement among people about that. This (construction) according to us is of two kinds: it is possible — first — that it is in the sense of "اَلَّذِينَ" (relative noun), as though it were said: "هَأنْتُمُ الَّذِينَ تُحِبُّونَهم ولا يُحِبُّونَكم" ("Here you are, the ones who love them while they do not love you"). And it is possible that "تُحِبُّونَهم" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), "أنْتُمْ" a mubtadaʾ (subject) and "أُولاءِ" the khabar (predicate); the meaning: look at yourselves, loving them — they were forbidden (this) in the state of their loving them. They did not explain why "أُولاءِ" is given kasra. "أُولاءِ" is originally with sukūn, because it is for pointing (a demonstrative), but the hamza was given kasra because of its sukūn and the sukūn of the alif (before it). "وَتُؤْمِنُونَ" is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to "تُحِبُّونَ". The meaning of ﴿وَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِالكِتابِ كُلِّهِ﴾ is: you believe in all the books of Allah. ﴿وَإذا لَقُوكم قالُوا آمَنّا﴾, that is: they acted hypocritically toward you; ﴿وَإذا خَلَوْا عَضُّوا عَلَيْكُمُ الأنامِلَ مِنَ الغَيْظِ﴾. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, announced their hypocrisy here as He announced it in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَإذا لَقُوا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قالُوا آمَنّا وإذا خَلا بَعْضُهم إلى بَعْضٍ قالُوا أتُحَدِّثُونَهم بِما فَتَحَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ [al-Baqara: 76]. One says: "عَضَضْتُ، أعَضُّ" ("I bit, I bite"), and one says "رَجُلٌ عِضٌّ" when a man clings to an opponent, i.e. persists in disputing; the verb from it is "عَضَضْتُ". "اَلْعُضُّ" is the fodder of the settled lands that camels are fed, such as date-stones, "اَلْقَتُّ" (dried clover) and "اَلْكُسْبُ" (oil-cake); it was called "عُضٌّ" only because it lasts longer in the livestock and preserves more fat. "اَلْأنامِلُ" (fingertips): its singular is "أُنْمُلَةٌ", and they are the ends of the fingers. Nothing has come on this pattern without the (feminine) hāʾ meaning something other than the singular [Translator's note: so in the printed text; the intended sense appears to be that no singular noun has come on the pattern أَفْعُل without the hāʾ], except their saying "قَدْ بَلَغَ أشُدَّهُ" ("he has reached his full strength"); as for the plural, it is frequent in it, or such as "أكْعَبُ", "أفْلَسُ", "أيْمَنُ" and "أشْمَلُ". [Translator's note: these plurals are vocalized thus in the printed text; on the pattern أَفْعُل they are usually أكْعُب، أفْلُس، أيْمُن، أشْمُل.]

zajjaj:120-120.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنْ تَمْسَسْكم حَسَنَةٌ تَسُؤْهُمْ﴾, that is: if you gain victory and enjoy plenty, that grieves them; ﴿وَإنْ تُصِبْكم سَيِّئَةٌ يَفْرَحُوا بِها﴾, that is: if the opposite of that befalls you, they rejoice; ﴿وَإنْ تَصْبِرُوا وتَتَّقُوا لا يَضُرُّكم كَيْدُهم شَيْئًا﴾ — Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, guaranteed victory to the believers if they are patient, and informed them that their (enemies') aggression and scheming would not harm them. In "لا يَضُرُّكم" the best is the ḍamma, because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the origin is "لا يَضْرُرْكم", but many of the readers and of the Arabs assimilate in the position of the jussive, while the people of the Hijaz pronounce the doubled letter separately. In this verse both dialects have come together: His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿إنْ تَمْسَسْكُمْ﴾ is according to the dialect of the people of the Hijaz,
and His saying ﴿لا يَضُرُّكُمْ﴾ is according to the dialect of other Arabs; and both ways are good. "لا يَضُرَّكم" and "لا يَضُرِّكم" are also permissible: whoever gives fatḥa does so because fatḥa is light and is used for the meeting of two quiescent letters in doubled (verbs), and whoever gives kasra does so according to the basic rule for the meeting of two quiescent letters; we have explained this earlier in the book. It was also read "لا يَضِرْكم", from "اَلضَّيْرُ"; "اَلضَّيْرُ" and "اَلضُّرُّ" both have one meaning, and likewise "اَلضُّرُّ". It has come in the Quran: ﴿قالُوا لا ضَيْرَ إنّا إلى رَبِّنا مُنْقَلِبُونَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 50], and it has come: ﴿وَإذا مَسَّكُمُ الضُّرُّ في البَحْرِ ضَلَّ مَن تَدْعُونَ إلا إيّاهُ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 67]. Al-Farrāʾ mentioned that al-Kisāʾī heard one of the people of al-ʿĀliya say: "ما تَضُورُّنِي" ("it does not harm me"), (and said) that if it were read accordingly, "لا يَضُرْكم", it would be permissible. This is not permissible: not a single letter of the Book of Allah is read in contradiction of the consensus on the word of one man from the people of al-ʿĀliya.

zajjaj:64-64.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿قُلْ يا أهْلَ الكِتابِ تَعالَوْا إلى كَلِمَةٍ سَواءٍ بَيْنَنا وبَيْنَكُمْ﴾. The meaning of ”سَواءٍ“ is the meaning of ”عَدْلٍ“ (just, equitable), and the meaning of ”كَلِمَةٍ“ is: speech containing the explanation of a matter, even if it is long. Likewise the Arabs call a qaṣīda (ode) ”كَلِمَةٌ“. It is narrated that Ḥassān ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī, when he was told "Recite!", would say to the speaker: "Has the kalima of al-Ḥuwaydira been recited?" — meaning his ode whose beginning is: بَكَرَتْ سُمَيَّةُ بُكْرَةً فَتَمَتَّعِي (Sumayya set off early in the morning, so take your enjoyment).
What is just is called ”سَواءٌ“, ”سَوًى“ and ”سُوًى“. Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā said:
أرُونِي خُطَّةً لا ضَيْمَ فِيها ∗∗∗ يُسَوِّي بَيْنَنا فِيها السَّواءُ
فَإنْ تُرِكَ السَّواءُ فَلَيْسَ بَيْنِي ∗∗∗ وبَيْنَكُمُ بَنِي حِصْنٍ بِناءُ
(Show me a course in which there is no injustice, in which equity makes us equal; but if equity is abandoned, then there is no bond between me and you, O Banū Ḥiṣn.)
By al-sawāʾ he means justice; so say the people of the language, and it is the truth; it is from the evenness (istiwāʾ) of a thing. If it were outside the Quran, ”سَواءً بَيْنَنا وبَيْنَكم“ (accusative) would be permissible. Whoever says ”سَواءٍ“ makes it a naʿt (adjective) of "the word", meaning "possessed of equity"; and whoever says ”سَواءً“ makes it a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of ”اِسْتِواءً“, as if he said "it is even, evenly".
The position of ﴿ألا نَعْبُدَ إلا اللَّهَ﴾ — the position of ”أنْ“ — is genitive, as a badal (substitute) for ”كَلِمَةٍ“; the meaning: "Come to (this:) that we worship none but Allah". It is also possible that ”أنْ“ is in the position of the nominative, as if someone said "What is the word?" and the answer was given: "It is that we worship none but Allah". If it were ”أنْ لا نَعْبُدُ إلّا اللَّهَ ولا نُشْرِكُ بِهِ شَيْئًا“ (in the indicative), it would be permissible, on the basis that it is an explanation of the matter in the sense of ”أيْ“ ("namely"), as if they said "namely: we worship none but Allah", just as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وانْطَلَقَ المَلأُ مِنهم أنِ امْشُوا﴾ [Ṣād: 6]. Some said: the meaning of ”أنْ“ here is the meaning of "saying: walk on"; and the meaning is the same, because "saying" here is an explanation of what they intended, and likewise ”أيْ“ is used to explain. If it were ”أنْ لا نَعْبُدْ إلّا اللَّهَ“ in the jussive, it would be permissible on the basis that ”أنْ“ is as we explained, in the sense of ”أيْ“, and ”أنْ لا نَعْبُدْ“ would be by way of prohibition, the one prohibited being in reality the one prohibiting, as if they prohibited themselves.
The meaning of ﴿وَلا يَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُنا بَعْضًا أرْبابًا مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ is: that we return to (the position) that the One we worship is Allah, and that ʿĪsā is a human being just as we are human beings, so we do not take him as a lord. The meaning of ﴿فَإنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَقُولُوا اشْهَدُوا بِأنّا مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ is: affirming the divine Oneness (tawḥīd), submitting to what the prophets brought us from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

zajjaj:65-65.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يا أهْلَ الكِتابِ لِمَ تُحاجُّونَ في إبْراهِيمَ وما أُنْـزِلَتِ التَّوْراةُ والإنْجِيلُ إلا مِن بَعْدِهِ﴾. In this He makes clear an argument against the Jews and the Christians together, because the Jews claim that Ibrāhīm was a Jew, and the Christians claim that he was a Christian and repudiate the Jews' claim; yet they do not repudiate the name of his description — that he was a Muslim, and that his name was not "Jew", nor "Christian", nor "polytheist". The Torah and the Gospel were sent down after him, and in neither of them is he named by any of the religions of the Jews, the Christians or the polytheists, while the name of Islam is his in all the scriptures. So their repudiating one another as to his being named by names other than Islam is a clear proof of the refutation of their saying, and a clear demonstration of Ibrāhīm's being free of all religions except the religion of Islam. As for the meaning of ﴿حَنِيفًا مُسْلِمًا﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 67]: the meaning of ”اَلْحَنَفُ“ in the language is the turning of the fronts of the two feet each towards the other — a turning that is congenital, with no going back from it ever. So the meaning of ḥanīfiyya in Islam is inclining to it and remaining firm upon that commitment.

zajjaj:68-68.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إنَّ أوْلى النّاسِ بِإبْراهِيمَ لَلَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ وهَذا النَّبِيُّ﴾, that is: they are the ones who are entitled to say "We are upon the religion of Ibrāhīm", and they have a bond of allegiance (wilāya). ﴿واللَّهُ ولِيُّ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, that is: He takes charge of helping them — for His party are the victorious — and He takes charge of requiting them with the best.

zajjaj:70-70.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لِمَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ وأنْتُمْ تَشْهَدُونَ﴾, that is: while you bear witness that they are the signs of Allah, because you used to tell of the matter of the Prophet ﷺ before he was sent. The origin of ”لِمَ تَكْفُرُونَ؟“ is ”لِما تَكْفُرُونَ؟“, and the meaning is: for what reason do you disbelieve? Likewise ﴿لِمَ تَقُولُونَ ما لا تَفْعَلُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 2], likewise ﴿عَمَّ يَتَساءَلُونَ﴾ [al-Nabaʾ: 1], and ﴿فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونَ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 54]. When you pause on these words you pause with hāʾ, saying ”لِمَهْ“ and ”بِمَهْ“, because the alif has been dropped in these interrogative nouns specifically, and so that was allowed; it is not allowed in the relative (mawṣūla) ”ما“, because the alif in them is not the end of the nouns — the alif is only in the middle. Its dropping is because the prepositions are a compensation for it, so it was dropped for lightness, since the fatḥa indicates it. It is not permissible to make these letters quiescent. Al-Kisāʾī claimed that the origin of ”كَمْ“ was ”كَمّا“. He said: "And I would have liked it to be with fatḥa for the meeting of two quiescent letters, in their saying ”كَمِ المالُ؟“ with kasra." This is an error on the part of Abū al-Ḥasan; had it been as he says, it would be ”كَمَ مالُكَ ؟“, just as you say ”لِمَ فَعَلْتَ؟“. This view is not one to be given attention.

zajjaj:71-71.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لِمَ تَلْبِسُونَ الحَقَّ بِالباطِلِ﴾, that is: why do you cover the truth with your falsehood while you know that it is the truth? One says ”لَبَسْتُ عَلَيْهِمُ الأمْرَ ألْبِسُهُ“ ("I confused the matter for them"); Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَلَبَسْنا عَلَيْهِمْ ما يَلْبِسُونَ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 9]. And one says ”لَبِسْتُ الثَّوْبَ ألْبَسُهُ“ ("I put on the garment"); Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَيَلْبَسُونَ ثِيابًا خُضْرًا﴾ [al-Kahf: 31]. If it had been said ”وَتَكْتُمُوا الحَقَّ“ (in the subjunctive), it would be permissible, on the pattern of your saying "Why do you combine this and that?"; but what is in the Quran is better in i'rab.

zajjaj:72-72.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَقالَتْ طائِفَةٌ مِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ﴾: the ṭāʾifa is the group, and they are the Jews. ﴿آمِنُوا بِالَّذِي أُنْـزِلَ عَلى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وجْهَ النَّهارِ﴾, that is: its beginning. The poet said:
مَن كانَ مَسْرُورًا بِمَقْتَلِ مالِكٍ ∗∗∗ فَلْيَأْتِ نِسْوَتَنا بِوَجْهِ نَهارِ
يَجِدِ النِّساءَ قَوائِمًا يَنْدُبْنَهُ ∗∗∗ قَدْ جِئْنَ قَبْلَ تَبَلُّجِ الأسْحارِ
(Whoever is glad at the killing of Mālik, let him come to our women at the beginning of the day; he will find the women standing, lamenting him, having come before the dawning of the pre-dawn hours.)
That is: at the beginning of the day. More than one view has been given on the interpretation of this. Some of them said: its meaning is: believe in their praying towards Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis) and disbelieve in their praying towards the House (the Kaʿba). It has also been said that the scholars of the Jews said to one another: "We used to tell our companions of things which Muḥammad ﷺ has brought; if we disbelieve in all of them, our companions will suspect us. Rather, let us believe in some and disbelieve in some, so as to make them imagine that we believe him in what he is to be believed in, and show them that we deny him in what is not with us."
It has also been said that they came to the Prophet ﷺ at the start of the day and said to him: "You are the one of whom we were told in the Torah that you would be sent; but give us respite until the evening so that we may consider our affair." When it was evening they came to the Anṣār and said to them: "We had informed you that Muḥammad is the prophet who is written in the Torah; however, we looked into the Torah and found that he is from the descendants of Hārūn, while Muḥammad is from the descendants of Ismāʿīl, so he is not the prophet that we have (described)." They did that only so that perhaps those who had believed in him would turn back. This is what has been said in the interpretation of the verse.

zajjaj:73-73.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلا تُؤْمِنُوا إلا لِمَن تَبِعَ دِينَكُمْ﴾. It has been said: the meaning is: do not make your confirmation of the Prophet in anything of what he has brought you except to the Jews, for if you say that to the polytheists, it will be a help to them in believing him. The people of the language and others among the people of exegesis said: "And do not believe that anyone will be given the like of what you have been given, except for whoever follows your religion", i.e. do not believe that anyone will be given, of the knowledge of the Prophet ﷺ, the like of what you have been given, or that they will argue with you before your Lord. The meaning of ﴿أوْ يُحاجُّوكم عِنْدَ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ is: no one will have an argument before Allah in believing in him, on account of knowledge from Him, except one who is like you. It has also been said concerning the meaning: ﴿قُلْ إنَّ الهُدى هُدى اللَّهِ أنْ يُؤْتى أحَدٌ مِثْلَ ما أُوتِيتُمْ﴾, i.e. guidance is this guidance; no one is given the like of what you have been given.
Some grammarians said: the meaning of ”أنْ“ here is the meaning of ”لا“; the meaning is only "that no one be given the like of what you have been given", i.e. "so that no one be given"; ”لا“ was omitted because there is in the speech an indication of it, just as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكم أنْ تَضِلُّوا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 176], i.e. so that you do not go astray. Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd (al-Mubarrad) said: ”لا“ is not among what is omitted here; rather, the genitive construct (iḍāfa) here is understood, so you omitted the first (term, the muḍāf) and put the second in its place; the meaning: "Allah makes clear to you out of aversion that you should go astray". And likewise here He said: "Guidance is the guidance of Allah, out of aversion that anyone be given the like of what you have been given", i.e. whoever opposes the religion of Islam, because Allah does not guide one who is a liar and an ingrate; so the guidance of Allah is far from those who are not believers.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قُلْ إنَّ الفَضْلَ بِيَدِ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَن يَشاءُ﴾, that is: His prophethood and His guidance — He gives it to whom He wills.

zajjaj:14-14.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿زُيِّنَ لِلنّاسِ حُبُّ الشَّهَواتِ مِنَ النِّساءِ والبَنِينَ﴾: two views have been given about ”زُيِّنَ“. Some said: Allah adorned them as a trial, as He said: ﴿إنّا جَعَلْنا ما عَلى الأرْضِ زِينَةً لَها لِنَبْلُوَهم أيُّهم أحْسَنُ عَمَلا﴾ [al-Kahf: 7]. Others said: Satan adorned them, because Allah has made [people] renounce them and made known that they are the enjoyment of delusion. The first view is better, because His making them an adornment that is loved is an existing fact, and Allah has made [people] renounce them by making known and showing their passing away.

The meaning of ﴿والقَناطِيرِ﴾ among the Arabs is: a great quantity of wealth; it is the plural of ”قِنْطارٌ“. As for the people of tafsīr, they gave views that do not depart from the usage of the Arabs. Some said: the qinṭār is the fill of a bull's hide in gold or silver. Some said: the qinṭār is eighty thousand dirhams. Some said: the qinṭār is a thousand dinars. And some said: a thousand raṭl of gold or silver. This is the sum of what people have said about ”اَلْقِنْطارُ“. What comes out in the language is that the qinṭār is taken from the tying of a thing and making it firm, and al-qanṭara (the arched bridge) is taken from that; so it is as though the qinṭār is the sum of wealth that forms a secure knot of it. As for those of the people of tafsīr who said that it is a full amount of gold, stronger than that in my view is what has been mentioned, that it is of gold and silver, because Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — mentioned the qanāṭīr in connection with both, so it is not sound that the qinṭār should apply to one of them and not the other.

The meaning of ﴿والخَيْلِ المُسَوَّمَةِ﴾ in the language is: horses bearing al-sīmāʾ and al-sūma, which is the mark. It is also possible — and it is good — that ”اَلْمُسَوَّمَةِ“ means "the grazing ones" (al-sāʾima), and ”أُسِيمَتْ“ means: they were put out to pasture. ”الأنْعامِ“ are livestock; its singular is ”نَعَمٌ“, used mostly of camels. ﴿والحَرْثِ﴾: crops.

All of this is made beloved to people, as Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said; then Allah made [them] renounce all of it. The interpretation of renouncing it is not abstaining from people sowing crops, nor from their earning things in some way; rather, the aspect of renunciation in it is the urging to charity and to following the paths of righteousness that He commanded, by refraining from amassing wealth and other things. This is the aspect of renunciation. So He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿ذَلِكَ مَتاعُ الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا﴾, i.e. what is enjoyed in it, ﴿واللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ حُسْنُ المَآبِ﴾. ”اَلْمَآبُ“ in the language is the place of return; one says: ”آبَ الرَّجُلُ، يَؤُوبُ، أوْبًا، وإيابًا، ومَآبًا“ (the man returned).

zajjaj:15-15.t:
And Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — made known that better than everything in this world is what He has prepared for His friends, saying: ﴿قُلْ أأُنَبِّئُكم بِخَيْرٍ مِن ذَلِكم لِلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها﴾. The nominative in ”جَنّاتٌ“ is the reading, and the genitive is permissible, with ”جَنّاتٌ“ being a badal (substitute) for ”خَيْرٍ“; the meaning [then] is: ”أؤُنَبِّئُكم بِجَنّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ؟“ (Shall I inform you of gardens beneath which rivers flow?), and ”لِلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ“ would be part of the completion of the first sentence. The meaning of ﴿وَأزْواجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ﴾ is: purified of impurities, and purified of what the women of the people of this world are subject to, such as menstruation and other things.

﴿وَرِضْوانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾: most readings have kasra on the rāʾ, and Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh transmitted from ʿĀṣim ”وَرُضْوانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ“ with ḍamma on the rāʾ throughout the Qurʾān. One says: ”رَضِيتُ الشَّيْءَ، أرْضاهُ، رِضًا، ومَرْضاةً، ورِضْوانًا، ورُضْوانًا“ (I was pleased with the thing). And the position of «[Translator's note: the sentence continues in the next entry (Āl ʿImrān 16).]»

zajjaj:16-16.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ﴾ is genitive, as a naʿt (adjective) of ”اَلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا“; the meaning is: for the God-fearing who say: ﴿رَبَّنا إنَّنا آمَنّا﴾. Likewise ﴿الصّابِرِينَ والصّادِقِينَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 17]. Had it been nominative as a resumption (istiʾnāf), that would have been permissible, but the reading is not to be departed from. The meaning of ”القانِتِينَ“ is: those who are constant in the worship of Allah; we have already explained ”اَلْقُنُوتُ“ earlier. The meaning of ”المُنفِقِينَ“ is: those who give charity and [spend on] everything in the path of Allah. ﴿والمُسْتَغْفِرِينَ بِالأسْحارِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 17]: ”اَلسَّحَرُ“ is the time before the rising of dawn. The Arabs say: ”جِئْتُكَ بِأعْلى السَّحَرِ“ (I came to you at the top of the saḥar), meaning: at the beginning of the saḥar, which is the first retreat of the night until the rising of the evident, clear dawn. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — described these people with affirming the truth, spending in His path and being constant in His worship, then described them as — in spite of that, because of the intensity of their fear and awe — seeking forgiveness in the hours before dawn.

zajjaj:18-18.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أنَّهُ لا إلَهَ إلا هو والمَلائِكَةُ وأُولُو العِلْمِ﴾: Abū ʿUbayda said: the meaning of ”شَهِدَ اللَّهُ“ is: Allah decreed. Its real meaning is that Allah knew and made clear, because the witness (al-shāhid) is the knower who makes clear what he knows. Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — has pointed to His oneness through everything He created, and made clear that no one is able to bring into being a single thing of what He brought into being. The angels bore witness because of what they knew of His power, and those possessed of knowledge bore witness by what was established for them and became clear from His creation, which no one other than He is able to do.

Most readings have ﴿أنَّهُ لا إلَهَ إلا هُوَ﴾ with fatḥa on the alif in ”أنَّهُ“; it has been transmitted with kasra from Ibn ʿAbbās, and it has been transmitted: ”أنَّ الدِّينَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الإسْلامُ“ with fatḥa on the alif. The majority is fatḥa in ”أنَّهُ“ and kasra in ”إنَّ الدِّينَ“. Whoever read ”إنَّهُ“ with kasra, the meaning is: "Allah bore witness: indeed the religion with Allah is Islam, and indeed there is no god but He". The fatḥa is better, as we described for the first, because speech, the declaration of oneness and the call of the adhān are: ”أشْهَدُ أنْ لا إلَهَ إلّا اللَّهُ“ (I bear witness that there is no god but Allah), and most occurrences of ”أشْهَدُ“ are with mention of [Allah's] oneness. It is permissible to give fatḥa to the first ”أنَّ“ and the second ”أنَّ“, so that the fatḥa of the second is from two angles: on [the construction] "Allah bore witness that there is no god but He, and bore witness that the religion with Him is Islam". «[Translator's note: only one of the two announced angles is stated in the text.]»

zajjaj:19-19.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿وَما اخْتَلَفَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتابَ إلا مِن بَعْدِ ما جاءَهُمُ العِلْمُ بَغْيًا بَيْنَهُمْ﴾: in ”جاءَهم“ you may use the open vowel (fatḥ) with full articulation (tafkhīm), and you may use imāla (inclining) towards kasra. The fatḥ is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz, and it is the highest and oldest dialect. As for ”جِاءَهم“ with kasra, it is the dialect of Tamīm and many of the Arabs, and it too is good and eloquent. The one who inclines towards kasra indicates that the verb is among those with yāʾ [as root letter]; and the one who uses fatḥ does so because the yāʾ's form has changed into alif, and the alif has its share of fatḥa. Each is correct.

”بَغْيًا“ is put in the accusative by His saying ”اِخْتَلَفَ“, and the meaning is: they differed out of transgression, i.e. for the sake of transgression; they did not differ because they saw insight and proof. Al-Akhfash said: the meaning is: ”وَما اخْتَلَفَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتابَ بَغْيًا بَيْنَهم إلّا مِن بَعْدِ ما جاءَهُمُ العِلْمُ“. What is best is that ”بَغْيًا“ be accusative by what ”وَما اخْتَلَفَ“ indicates, so that the meaning is: they differed out of transgression among themselves.

﴿وَمَن يَكْفُرْ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ فَإنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الحِسابِ﴾, i.e. swift in reckoning with him. The jussive is the right construction in ”وَمَن يَكْفُرْ“, and it is the reading; had it been read in the nominative, it would have had a basis in analogy (qiyās), but the jussive is better and more eloquent in meaning. The meaning of ”سَرِيعُ الحِسابِ“ is: swift in recompensing him, as He said: ﴿وَما أمْرُ السّاعَةِ إلا كَلَمْحِ البَصَرِ أوْ هو أقْرَبُ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 77]. They also said: it is possible that ”سَرِيعُ الحِسابِ“ means swift in making known to the doer his deed, because He — exalted be His praise — knows all that they did and does not need to establish anything or to recall anything.

﴿قائِمًا بِالقِسْطِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 18] is accusative as an emphatic ḥāl (circumstantial), because the emphatic ḥāl occurs with nouns other than demonstratives; you say: ”إنَّهُ زَيْدٌ مَعْرُوفًا“ (he is Zayd, well known), ”هو الحَقُّ مُصَدِّقًا“ (it is the truth, confirming), and ”لا إلَهَ إلّا هو قائِمًا بِالقِسْطِ“. ”اَلْقِسْطُ“ in the language is justice; Allah said: ﴿وَأقِيمُوا الوَزْنَ بِالقِسْطِ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 9], i.e. with justice. One says ”أقْسَطَ الرَّجُلُ“ when he acts justly, and ”قَسَطَ“ when he acts unjustly; the just one is ”مُقْسِطٌ“ and the unjust one ”قاسِطٌ“. Allah said: ﴿وَأقْسِطُوا إنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ المُقْسِطِينَ﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 9], i.e. act justly; Allah loves the just. And He said: ﴿وَأمّا القاسِطُونَ فَكانُوا لِجَهَنَّمَ حَطَبًا﴾ [al-Jinn: 15].

If someone says: how is it that from the word qisṭ there has come something meaning injustice, when its origin is justice? [The answer is that] it is just like your saying: ”عَدَلَ الرَّجُلُ عَلى القَوْمِ، يَعْدِلُ، عَدْلًا، ومَعْدِلَةً، ومَعْدَلَةً“ when he treats them fairly, and ”عَدَلَ عَنِ الحَقِّ، عَدْلًا“ when he deviates unjustly. Likewise there has come from the word qisṭ something meaning injustice, just as something meaning justice has come.

zajjaj:20-20.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَإنْ حاجُّوكَ فَقُلْ أسْلَمْتُ وجْهِيَ لِلَّهِ﴾: if you wish you may make the yāʾ of ”وَجْهِي“ quiescent, and if you wish you may give it fatḥa, saying: ”أسْلَمْتُ وجْهِي لِلَّهِ“; we have already explained the matter of this yāʾ earlier. The meaning is that Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — commanded the Prophet ﷺ to argue against the People of the Book and the polytheists that he followed the command of Allah, whom they all acknowledge to be their Creator; so he called them to what they acknowledged, and showed them the proofs and signs — whose mention we have explained — that he is His Messenger ﷺ. The meaning of ”أسْلَمْتُ وجْهِيَ لِلَّهِ“ is: I have directed my worship to Allah — exalted be His praise — and acknowledged that there is no god other than He; and likewise whoever follows me. It is also permissible in the language that ”أسْلَمْتُ وجْهِيَ“ mean: I have surrendered myself. Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿كُلُّ شَيْءٍ هالِكٌ إلا وجْهَهُ﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 88], and said: ﴿وَيَبْقى وجْهُ رَبِّكَ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 27]; the meaning is: and your Lord remains; and the meaning [of the first] is: everything perishes except Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He.

﴿وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَنِ﴾: you may omit the yāʾ or retain it; what I prefer in this is following the Muṣḥaf, because following it is Sunna and contravening it is innovation. Whatever of these yāʾs is omitted — like ”وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَنِ“, ”لَئِنْ أخَّرْتَنِ إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ“, and like ”فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أكْرَمَنِ“, ”فَيَقُولُ: رَبِّي أهانَنِ“ — is of two kinds with the nūn. When it is at the head (end) of a verse — and the lexicographers call the ends of verses ”اَلْفَواصِلَ“ (al-fawāṣil) — they permit the omission of the yāʾs, just as they permit it in the rhymes of poetry, as al-Aʿshā said:
؎وَمِن شانِئٍ كاسِفٍ وجْهُهُ ∗∗∗ إذا ما انْتَسَبْتُ لَهُ أنْكَرَنْ
؎وَهَلْ يَمْنَعَنِّي ارْتِيادِي البِلا ∗∗∗ دَ مِن حَذَرِ المَوْتِ أنْ يَأْتِيَنْ
(And many a hater, his face gloomy, who, when I state my lineage to him, disowns me; and will my roaming the lands out of fear of death prevent it from coming to me?)
The meaning is ”أنْ يَأْتِيَنِي“ and ”أنْكَرَنِي“. When it is not at the end of a rhyme or the end of a verse, retaining the yāʾ is more common, but omitting it is also good and fully [correct], especially with the nūns. However, the original of ”اِتَّبَعَنِي“ is ”اِتَّبَعَيِ“; but the nūn was added so that the fatḥa of the ʿayn [of the verb] would remain intact, and the kasra with the nūn substitutes for the yāʾ. When there is no nūn — as in ”غُلامِي“ and ”صاحِبِي“ — the best is to retain it, and omitting it without the nūn is less frequent than with the nūn, though it is permissible. We say: ”هَذا غُلامِ قَدْ جاءَ“ (this is my servant, he has come), but the best is ”هَذا غُلامِي قَدْ جاءَ“ and ”غُلامِيَ قَدْ جاءَ“, with fatḥa on the yāʾ or quiescence; and omitting it is permissible because the kasra indicates it.

His saying — blessed be His name —: ﴿وَقُلْ لِلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتابَ والأُمِّيِّينَ أأسْلَمْتُمْ﴾: ”اَلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتابَ“ are the Jews and the Christians, and the ummiyyūn (unlettered) are the polytheists of the Arabs, because they were attributed only to the state the nation (umma) is in by natural constitution, since a human being is created not knowing how to write; this is the meaning of ”اَلْأُمِّيِّينَ“. Some of the grammarians said: the meaning of ”أأسْلَمْتُمُ“ is the command; its meaning for them is: submit (aslimū). «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «مَعْنى ”أأسْلَمْتُمُ الأمْرَ“» with the closing quotation mark displaced; it is rendered as "the meaning of «أأسلمتم» is the command".]» The reality of this speech is that it is interrogative in wording, while its meaning is making [them] stop and confront [the matter] (tawqīf) and threat, as you say to a man after you have commanded him and insisted on it: ”أقَبِلْتَ، وإلّا فَأنْتَ أعْلَمُ“ (Have you accepted? Otherwise, you know best [what will happen]). You are only asking him while threatening him in your question; by my life, this is a proof that you are commanding him to do it.

The meaning of ﴿وَإنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإنَّما عَلَيْكَ البَلاغُ﴾ is: their guidance is not your duty; your duty is only to establish the proof for them; when you have conveyed [the message], you have discharged what is upon you.

His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿واللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِالعِبادِ﴾, i.e. All-Seeing of what cuts off their excuse in that by which He guided them to His oneness and to the confirmation of His messengers.

zajjaj:21-21.t:
And He said — following this verse —: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْفُرُونَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. the signs of Allah that you have brought them, ﴿وَيَقْتُلُونَ النَّبِيِّينَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ﴾; and it has been read: ”وَيُقاتِلُونَ“. As for the meaning of ”وَيَقْتُلُونَ النَّبِيِّينَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ“ here, two views have been given. It was said: [it means] their being content with the killing of the prophets by those of them who went before, like the killing of John (Yaḥyā) — peace be upon him — and this is possible — and Allah knows best. And it was said: ”وَيَقْتُلُونَ النَّبِيِّينَ“ because they fought the Prophet ﷺ and intended to kill him. Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿وَإذْ يَمْكُرُ بِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِيُثْبِتُوكَ أوْ يَقْتُلُوكَ أوْ يُخْرِجُوكَ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 30]. This is the meaning of ”وَيَقْتُلُونَ النَّبِيِّينَ“ — and Allah knows best.

The entry of the fāʾ into the khabar (predicate) of ”إنَّ“ is permissible [here], though ”إنَّ زَيْدًا فَقائِمٌ“ is not permissible. It is permissible here — ﴿فَبَشِّرْهم بِعَذابٍ ألِيمٍ﴾ — because ”اَلَّذِي“ takes a ṣila (relative clause), and its ṣila is like the protasis (sharṭ) for the apodosis (jazāʾ), so it is answered with the fāʾ. ”لَيْتَ الَّذِي يَقُومُ فَيُكْرِمُكَ“ is not valid, because ”إنَّ“ is as though it were not mentioned in the speech, so the entry of the answer with the fāʾ [in a sentence] with it is like its entry with the mubtadaʾ (subject); whereas the [sense of] wishing [in layta] enters and removes the meaning of the inchoative and the condition.

zajjaj:23-23.t: His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ إلى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا نَصِيبًا مِنَ الكِتابِ﴾: its meaning is: an ample share of it. And ﴿يُدْعَوْنَ إلى كِتابِ اللَّهِ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾, i.e. they are called to the Book of Allah which they acknowledge, and in which there is mention of the Prophet ﷺ and the announcement of his mission. ﴿ثُمَّ يَتَوَلّى فَرِيقٌ مِنهم وهم مُعْرِضُونَ﴾, i.e. a large group. They only turned away, except that they have no argument other than denying something that a group of their scholars have acknowledged to be in their book.

zajjaj:24-24.t: Then Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — told of what drove them to that, and reported what deluded them, saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّهم قالُوا لَنْ تَمَسَّنا النّارُ إلا أيّامًا مَعْدُوداتٍ وغَرَّهم في دِينِهِمْ ما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ﴾. The position of ”ذَلِكَ“ is nominative; the meaning is: ”شَأْنُهم ذَلِكَ، وأمْرُهم ذَلِكَ“ (their case is that, their affair is that), because of their saying and their supposing that they would be punished only for a numbered few days. It has come in the tafsīr that they said: we will be punished only forty days, [the days] in which our fathers worshipped the calf. So Allah — Blessed and Exalted is He — made known that this is a fabrication of theirs, and that it is what deluded them.

zajjaj:25-25.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿فَكَيْفَ إذا جَمَعْناهم لِيَوْمٍ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾: the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: so how will their state be at that time?! This expression is used in speech; you say: ”أنا أُكْرِمُكَ وأنْتَ لَمْ تَزُرْنِي، فَكَيْفَ إذا زُرْتَنِي؟!“ (I honour you while you have not visited me — so how [will it be] when you visit me?!).
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿لِيَوْمٍ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾, i.e. for the reckoning of a day about which there is no doubt.

zajjaj:121-121.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإذْ غَدَوْتَ مِن أهْلِكَ تُبَوِّئُ المُؤْمِنِينَ مَقاعِدَ لِلْقِتالِ﴾ — it is related «that the Prophet ﷺ saw in his sleep as though he were wearing a fortified coat of mail, and he interpreted it as Medina; so he ﷺ commanded the Muslims — when the polytheists advanced toward them — to stay in it until the polytheists reached them, so that the battle would be in it». That is his assigning of positions for battle. Some said: its meaning is "stations for battle", and the meaning is the same. What governs (al-ʿāmil) "إذْ" is the sense of "اُذْكُرْ" ("remember"); the meaning is: "Remember when you went out early in the morning."

zajjaj:122-122.t: What governs ﴿إذْ هَمَّتْ طائِفَتانِ مِنكم أنْ تَفْشَلا﴾ is "تُبَوِّئُ"; the meaning is: the assigning (of positions) was at that time. The meaning of "تَفْشَلا" is: that they (the two parties) lose courage and grow weak. ﴿واللَّهُ ولِيُّهُما﴾, that is: they were inclined to that, while Allah was their helper.

zajjaj:123-123.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ بِبَدْرٍ وأنْتُمْ أذِلَّةٌ﴾ — the meaning of "أذِلَّةٌ" is: your number was small. The Muslims in that battle were three hundred and some ten-odd; on the day of Uḥud they were seven hundred, and the disbelievers on the day of Uḥud were three thousand; and they were on the day of Ḥunayn twelve thousand. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, made known that whenever they kept to obedience, He would give them victory while they were few and their enemy many times their number. On the day of Uḥud there befell them what befell them because of disobeying the command of the Prophet ﷺ, in that they went beyond what they had been commanded; so Allah made that a punishment for them, so that they would not become cowardly. It has come in a report: "Fleeing from the advancing army is disbelief"; its meaning in my view — and Allah knows best — is: (it is) of the doing of the disbelievers, not that it takes a person out of faith into disbelief. Allah has pardoned (some) of it, saying: ﴿وَمَن يُوَلِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ دُبُرَهُ إلا مُتَحَرِّفًا لِقِتالٍ أوْ مُتَحَيِّزًا إلى فِئَةٍ فَقَدْ باءَ بِغَضَبٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ ومَأْواهُ جَهَنَّمُ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 16]. "أذِلَّةٌ" is the plural of "ذَلِيلٌ". The basic rule for "فَعِيلٌ", when it is an adjective, is to be pluralized on "فُعَلاءُ", e.g. "ظَرِيفٌ" / "ظُرَفاءُ" and "شَرِيكٌ" / "شُرَكاءُ"; but "فُعَلاءُ" was avoided with doubled roots: if "جُلَلاءُ" and "قُلَلاءُ" were said for "جَلِيلٌ" and "قَلِيلٌ", two letters of the same kind would come together. So it was diverted to "أفْعِلَةٌ", (taken) from the plural of nouns on "فَعِيلٌ", e.g. "جَرِيبٌ" / "أجْرِبَةٌ" and "قَفِيزٌ" / "أقْفِزَةٌ".

zajjaj:125-125.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَيَأْتُوكم مِن فَوْرِهِمْ هَذا﴾, that is: from their direction (right away). "هَذا" is a naʿt (adjective) of "فَوْرِهِمْ", and "يُمْدِدْكم" is the apodosis (jawāb) of the conditional. One says: "أمْدَدْتُ الجَيْشَ بِعُدَدٍ" ("I reinforced the army with equipment"); "أمَدَّ الجُرْحُ" — when pus has formed in it — "يُمِدُّ، فَهو مُمِدٌّ"; and "مَدَّ النَّهْرُ" ("the river rose") and "مَدَّهُ نَهْرٌ آخَرُ" ("another river fed it").
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿مُسَوِّمِينَ﴾ was read "مُسَوِّمِينَ" and "مُسَوَّمِينَ". The meaning of "مُسَوِّمِينَ" is taken from "اَلسُّومَةُ", which is the mark: they were marked with a tuft of wool, or a turban, or the like. "مُسَوَّمِينَ" means: marked. And it is possible that "مُسَوِّمِينَ" means: they have let their horses loose and made them graze freely (sāʾima).

zajjaj:126-126.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَما جَعَلَهُ اللَّهُ إلا بُشْرى لَكُمْ﴾ — He made the mention of the reinforcement only as glad tidings for you, and so that you would be made firm in your battle.
