zajjaj:127-127.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لِيَقْطَعَ طَرَفًا مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾, that is: to remove a portion of them; ﴿أوْ يَكْبِتَهُمْ﴾, that is: to rout them. Abū ʿUbayda said: one says "كَبَتَهُ اللَّهُ لِوَجْهِهِ", i.e. Allah threw him down on his face. And "the disappointed one" (al-khāʾib) is the one who did not attain what he hoped for.

zajjaj:128-128.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَيْسَ لَكَ مِنَ الأمْرِ شَيْءٌ أوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ أوْ يُعَذِّبَهم فَإنَّهم ظالِمُونَ﴾ — this was sent down to him ﷺ because «on the day of Uḥud his head was wounded and his front tooth was broken, and he said, while wiping the blood from his face: "How can a people prosper who have done this to their Prophet while he calls them to their Lord?!"». So Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, informed him that their prospering is not in his hands, and that nothing of the matter is his except to convey the message and strive until the religion prevails, and that his reward for that rests with Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He. The accusative of "أوْ يَتُوبَ" is on two ways: it may be conjoined to His saying: "لِيَقْطَعَ طَرَفًا مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أوْ يَكْبِتَهم أوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ أوْ يُعَذِّبَهم"; the second way is the accusative by "أوْ", since it is in the sense of "إلّا أنْ" ("unless"). So the meaning is: "Nothing of the matter is yours, i.e. they will not believe unless Allah turns to them, or until Allah turns to them."

zajjaj:130-130.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَأْكُلُوا الرِّبا أضْعافًا مُضاعَفَةً﴾ — "اَلرِّبا" (usury), little and much of it, has been forbidden in His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَأحَلَّ اللَّهُ البَيْعَ وحَرَّمَ الرِّبا﴾ [al-Baqara: 275]. This was (said) only because some people of al-Ṭāʾif used to practise usury, and when the term came due they would increase it and multiply the usury. Some said: its meaning is: do not multiply your wealth through usury. The meaning of ﴿لَعَلَّكم تُفْلِحُونَ﴾ is: so that you may be in hope of success. "اَلْمُفْلِحُ" is the one who has attained the good that he hoped for; its derivation is from "فَلَحَ الحَدِيدَ" ("he split the iron"), when he cleaves it; so it is an intensive expression for attaining what is reached for.

zajjaj:131-131.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿واتَّقُوا النّارَ الَّتِي أُعِدَّتْ لِلْكافِرِينَ﴾, that is: beware of making lawful what Allah has forbidden, for whoever makes lawful anything that Allah has forbidden is a disbeliever by consensus.

zajjaj:133-133.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُها السَّماواتُ والأرْضُ أُعِدَّتْ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾, that is: for whoever guards against the forbidden things. It is related from the Prophet ﷺ that between the two leaves of the gate of the Garden is a journey of forty years, and that a day will surely come upon it when people will crowd at it as camels crowd when they come to water hungry and thirsty.

zajjaj:134-134.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿والكاظِمِينَ الغَيْظَ والعافِينَ عَنِ النّاسِ﴾, that is: it was prepared for those who have been mentioned and for those who restrain anger. It is related from the Prophet ﷺ: "There is no draught that a person swallows greater in reward than a draught of anger (swallowed) for the sake of Allah." One says: "كَظَمْتُ الغَيْظَ، أكْظِمُهُ، كَظْمًا" when I hold in what is in my soul of it. And one says: "كَظَمَ البَعِيرُ عَلى جَرَّتِهِ" when the camel keeps its cud back in its throat; and "كَظَمَ البَعِيرُ والنّاقَةُ كُظُومًا" when it does not chew the cud. Al-Rāʿī said:
؎فَأفَضْنَ بَعْدَ كُظُومِهِنَّ بِجَرَّةٍ ∗∗∗ مِن ذِي الأباطِحِ أذْرَعَيْنِ حَقِيلا
(Then, after holding back, they brought up their cud — of the plants of Dhū al-Abāṭiḥ, Adhraʿayn and Ḥaqīl.)
"اَلْكِظامَةُ" is a thong by which the bowstring is tied onto the curved end of the Arab bow. "اَلْكَظِيمَةُ" and "اَلْكَظائِمُ" are channels dug from well to well so that water flows from one to another. "كاظِمَةٌ" is a place in the desert.

zajjaj:135-135.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إلا اللَّهُ﴾ — the nominative is construed according to the meaning; the meaning is: and who is there that forgives sins? None forgives them but Allah. ﴿وَلَمْ يُصِرُّوا عَلى ما فَعَلُوا﴾ — "اَلْإصْرارُ" (persistence) is remaining in a thing.

zajjaj:137-137.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِكم سُنَنٌ﴾ — the meaning of "قَدْ خَلَتْ" is: have passed; the meaning of "سُنَنٌ" is: people of ways (sunan), i.e. people of paths. "اَلسُّنَّةُ" is the way (al-ṭarīqa); people's saying "فُلانٌ عَلى السُّنَّةِ" ("So-and-so is on the sunna") means: on the way, and they did not need to say "on the straight way", because there is an indication of that in the speech. This is like our saying "مُؤْمِنٌ" ("believer"), which means "one who affirms as true", and in the speech there is an indication that he believes in the matters of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, which He commanded belief in. The meaning is: when you travel in your journeys you will know the reports of peoples who were destroyed for their denial.

zajjaj:75-75.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَمِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ مَن إنْ تَأْمَنهُ بِقِنْطارٍ يُؤَدِّهِ إلَيْكَ﴾. Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza agreed on making the hāʾ of ”يُؤَدِّهْ“ quiescent, and likewise everything in the Quran resembling this — they agreed on making the hāʾ quiescent in it, such as ”نُصْلِهْ جَهَنَّمَ“, ”نُؤْتِهْ مِنها“ and His saying ”نُوَلِّهْ ما تَوَلّى“ — except for one word reported from Abū ʿAmr: Abū ʿUbayda reported from Abū ʿAmr that he read with kasra in ”ألْقِهِ إلَيْهِمْ“, although there is no difference between this word and the other words in which he made it quiescent. As for the report from Abū ʿAmr about it and about others, it is an error: Abū ʿAmr used to pronounce the kasra in a snatched, reduced manner (ikhtilās). This is just as an error was attributed to him in ”بارِئِكم“: the Quran reciters reported from him that he dropped the vowel of the hamza in ”بارِئِكم“, whereas Sībawayh reported from him — and in this he is more precise than others — that he pronounced a hidden, light kasra. As for Nāfiʿ and the reciters of the people of Medina, they gave these words their full vowel, pronouncing kasra and keeping the yāʾs, as in ”يُؤَدِّهِ إلَيْكَ“ (yuʾaddihī ilayka). This quiescence which these people reported from him is a clear error which should not be recited, because the hāʾ should not be made jussive-like or quiescent in continuous recitation (waṣl); it is made quiescent only in pausing (waqf).
In these words there are four ways: it is permissible to keep the yāʾ, and permissible to drop it, saying "يُؤَدِّهِ إلَيْكَ" with kasra; it is permissible to say "يُؤَدِّهُو إلَيْكَ" with ḍamma, keeping the wāw after the hāʾ; and it is permissible to drop the wāw while keeping the ḍamma on the hāʾ. As for the pausal form (in continuous recitation), there is no justification for it, because the hāʾ is a faint letter, made clear in continuous speech by the wāw in the masculine. Sībawayh said: the wāw entered in the masculine just as the alif entered in the feminine, as in "ضَرَبْتُهُو" and "ضَرَبْتُها". His followers said: the wāw was chosen because it is from the edge of the lips while the hāʾ is from the throat, so the wāw made the hāʾ clear; and the yāʾ is dropped only for the reason that the wāw changes into it; when the yāʾ is dropped the kasra remains. As for the pausal form (in this position), it is not permissible at all. People have said much in explaining the qinṭār, and we have reported what people said about it; they did not agree on a definition of the amount of its weight, but they did agree that it is a large amount of wealth.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إلا ما دُمْتَ عَلَيْهِ قائِمًا﴾. Most of the reading is "دُمْتَ" with ḍamma on the dāl, and it has also been read "دِمْتَ". As for "دُمْتَ", it is from your saying "دُمْتُ، أدُومُ" when you remain at a thing, like "قُمْتُ، أقُومُ"; and as for "دِمْتَ" with kasra, it is on the basis of their saying "دِمْتَ تَدامُ", like your saying "خِفْتَ، تَخافُ". One says "قَدْ دِيمَ بِفُلانٍ، وأُدِيمَ بِهِ" in the sense of "دِيرَ بِهِ، وأُدِيرَ بِهِ" ("he became dizzy"), and he is the one afflicted with "دُوامٌّ", as in their saying "بِهِ دُوامٌّ", like their saying "بِهِ دُوارٌ" ("he has vertigo"). One says "دامَ المالُ — when it is still — يَدُومُ، فَهو دائِمٌ" [Translator's note: so in the text (المال, "wealth"); the context of still water suggests الماء, "water"]; and from this is the Prophet's ﷺ prohibition of urinating in "standing water (al-māʾ al-dāʾim)", i.e. still water. One says "قَدْ دَوَّمَ الطّائِرُ في الجَوِّ تَدْوِيمًا" ("the bird hovered in the air"); this may be from two aspects: from its circling in its flight, or from the slight motion of its wings, because it is seen as if its wings were still. The meaning of ﴿قائِمًا﴾ is: except by your constantly standing over the demanding of your debt.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأنَّهم قالُوا﴾, that is: their doing that is because of their saying ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْنا في الأُمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ﴾, i.e. there is no way (of blame) against us in taking their wealth.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, described their consuming of unlawful gain and their treachery. It has been said in the exegesis that they had dealings with some people from among the polytheists, and when these moved over to Islam, they said: "We have no obligation towards you; we only dealt with you while you were upon that religion of yours." So Allah made known that they lie. He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ عَلى اللَّهِ الكَذِبَ وهم يَعْلَمُونَ﴾, i.e. while they know that they are lying. So Allah rejected their saying and said: ﴿بَلى﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 76] — and in my view, and Allah knows best, this is a complete pause (waqf al-tamām). Then He began anew and said, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿مَن أوْفى بِعَهْدِهِ واتَّقى فَإنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ المُتَّقِينَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 76], i.e. then Allah loves him. It is also possible that He began the whole statement anew with His saying "بَلى", because their saying "there is no blame upon us in what we do" is like their saying "we are people of piety in this action of ours". So Allah made known that the people of fidelity to covenants and of piety are those whom Allah loves, and that they are the God-fearing (al-muttaqūn), i.e. those who guard against treachery and against disbelief in the Prophet ﷺ.

zajjaj:139-139.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلا تَهِنُوا ولا تَحْزَنُوا وأنْتُمُ الأعْلَوْنَ إنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, that is: do not weaken. One says: "وَهَنَ، يَهِنُ" when he becomes weak. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, guaranteed victory by His saying: ﴿وَأنْتُمُ الأعْلَوْنَ﴾.

zajjaj:77-77.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أُولَئِكَ لا خَلاقَ لَهم في الآخِرَةِ﴾: this clause is the khabar (predicate) of ”إنَّ“. The meaning of al-khalāq is an ample share of good. As for the meaning of His saying ﴿وَلا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ اللَّهُ ولا يَنْظُرُ إلَيْهِمْ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ﴾, in His saying ﴿وَلا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ there are two aspects. One of them is that Allah's making His friends hear His speech without an intermediary is a special distinction with which Allah singles out His friends, just as He spoke to Mūsā, and that was a distinction for him to the exclusion of all humankind. It is also possible that ﴿وَلا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ اللَّهُ ولا يَنْظُرُ إلَيْهِمْ﴾ is to be interpreted as anger against them and turning away from them, just as you say ”فُلانٌ لا يَنْظُرُ إلى فُلانٍ، ولا يُكَلِّمُهُ“ ("so-and-so does not look at so-and-so, nor speak to him"), its interpretation being that he is angry with him; and if he speaks to him with harsh words, that does not contradict it. The meaning of ﴿وَلا يُزَكِّيهِمْ﴾ is: He does not make them pure, nor does He praise them with good. The meaning of ﴿عَذابٌ ألِيمٌ﴾ is: painful.

zajjaj:140-140.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إنْ يَمْسَسْكم قَرْحٌ﴾ — and "قُرْحٌ": both are read, and according to the lexicographers they have one meaning, namely wounds and their pain. One says: "قَدْ قَرِحَ، يَقْرَحُ، قَرْحًا" and "أصابَهُ قَرْحٌ". Some said: it is as though "اَلْقُرْحُ" were the wound and "اَلْقَرْحُ" the pain. ﴿وَتِلْكَ الأيّامُ نُداوِلُها بَيْنَ النّاسِ﴾, that is: We give the turn of fortune (al-dawla) at one time or another to the disbelievers over the believers, when they disobey in what they are commanded regarding fighting the disbelievers; but when they obey, they are always given victory, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ألا إنَّ حِزْبَ اللَّهِ هُمُ المُفْلِحُونَ﴾ [al-Mujādila: 22]. The meaning of ﴿وَلِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ويَتَّخِذَ مِنكم شُهَداءَ﴾ is: so that Allah may know who remains firm in faith after defeat befalls him; i.e. He gives them (the disbelievers) the turn at one time or another so that He may know the believers.
The interpretation of ﴿وَلِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ — while Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, already knew them before that — is: "that He may know it as actually occurring from them", as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكم حَتّى نَعْلَمَ المُجاهِدِينَ مِنكم والصّابِرِينَ﴾ [Muḥammad: 31], that is: so that what We knew as unseen may occur, witnessed by people, and occur from you. Recompense falls only upon what Allah knows of creatures as actually occurring, not upon what has not occurred and what they have not done. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَإنَّما تُوَفَّوْنَ أُجُورَكم يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 185], and He said: ﴿إنَّما تُجْزَوْنَ ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 16].

zajjaj:78-78.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإنَّ مِنهم لَفَرِيقًا يَلْوُونَ ألْسِنَتَهم بِالكِتابِ﴾. This lām in ”وَإنَّ مِنهم لَفَرِيقًا“ emphasises the speech in addition to the emphasis of ”إنَّ“, because the meaning of ”إنَّ“ is emphasis of the speech; for that reason it came to be something with which the oath (al-ḍamm in the text) is connected in the affirmative [Translator's note: the text reads لِضَمٍّ / الضَّمَّ, apparently a corruption of القَسَم ("the oath"), which the examples require]. You say ”واللَّهِ إنَّ زَيْدًا قائِمٌ“ ("By Allah, Zayd is indeed standing"), and likewise you connect the oath with the lām, saying ”واللَّهِ لَزَيْدٌ قائِمٌ“ ("By Allah, Zayd is surely standing"). This lām does not come directly after ”إنَّ“: ”إنَّ لَزَيْدًا قائِمٌ“ is not permissible, by the consensus of all the grammarians and the people of the language.
The meaning of ﴿يَلْوُونَ ألْسِنَتَهم بِالكِتابِ﴾ is: they distort the Book, i.e. they deviate from the right course. ”يُلَوُّونَ“, with ḍamma on the yāʾ and doubling, is also permissible. ﴿لِتَحْسَبُوهُ﴾ and ”لِتَحْسِبُوهُ“, with kasra and fatḥa on the sīn: one says ”حَسِبَ، يَحْسَبُ، ويَحْسِبُ“, both. One says ”لَوَيْتُ الشَّيْءَ — إذا عَدَلْتُهُ عَنِ القَصْدِ — لَيًّا“ ("I twisted the thing", when I turned it from its straight course), and ”لَوَيْتُ الغَرِيمَ لِيانًا“ when I put off my creditor/debtor in paying his debt. The poet said:
قَدْ كُنْتُ دايَنْتُ بِها حَسّانا ∗∗∗ مَخافَةَ الإفْلاسِ واللِّيّانا
(I had given her as a debt-pledge to Ḥassān, fearing bankruptcy and delay in payment.)

zajjaj:79-79.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ما كانَ لِبَشَرٍ أنْ يُؤْتِيَهُ اللَّهُ الكِتابَ والحُكْمَ والنُّبُوَّةَ ثُمَّ يَقُولَ لِلنّاسِ كُونُوا عِبادًا لِي مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾, that is: Allah does not choose liars for His prophethood; and if a human being did that, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would strip him of the signs and marks of prophethood.
”ثُمَّ يَقُولَ“ is in the accusative (subjunctive) by sharing between ”أنْ يُؤْتِيَهُ“ and ”يَقُولَ“, i.e. the giving of prophethood and saying to people "Be servants to me" do not come together in a prophet. ﴿وَلَكِنْ كُونُوا رَبّانِيِّينَ﴾: ”اَلرَّبّانِيُّونَ“ are the masters of knowledge and clear exposition, i.e. be people of knowledge. The alif and nūn were added only for intensification in the relational adjective (nisba), just as they said of one with a large beard ”لِحْيانِيٌّ“ and of one with an abundant mass of hair ”جُمّانِيٌّ“. It has been read ﴿بِما كُنْتُمْ تُعَلِّمُونَ الكِتابَ﴾ and ”تَعَلَّمُونَ“, with ḍamma and with fatḥa on the tāʾ. ﴿وَبِما كُنْتُمْ تَدْرُسُونَ﴾, that is: by your knowledge and your study, teach people and make things clear to them. It has come in the exegesis: "Be rabbāniyyīn", i.e. scholars and jurists. Its meaning is not merely "as you teach"; rather, let your conduct and your intention in teaching be the conduct of the scholars and the wise, because the scholar should only be called "a scholar (ʿālim)" when he acts according to his knowledge; otherwise he is not a scholar. Allah said: ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمُوا لَمَنِ اشْتَراهُ ما لَهُ في الآخِرَةِ مِن خَلاقٍ﴾ [al-Baqara: 102], then He said: ﴿وَلَبِئْسَ ما شَرَوْا بِهِ أنْفُسَهم لَوْ كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 102], i.e. if they had given knowledge its due. We have explained what has been said about this in its place.

zajjaj:80-80.t: The meaning of ﴿وَلا يَأْمُرَكم أنْ تَتَّخِذُوا المَلائِكَةَ والنَّبِيِّينَ أرْبابًا﴾ is: nor does he command you to worship the angels and the prophets — because those who said that ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) is a god worshipped him and took him as a lord, and some of the disbelievers said: "The angels are our lords"; it is said that they are the Sabians. The nominative is also permissible in ”وَلا يَأْمُرُكم“, i.e. Allah does not command you.

zajjaj:26-26.t:
His saying — exalted be His affair —: ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ مالِكَ المُلْكِ﴾: Allah commanded the Prophet ﷺ to glorify Him and to mention what points to His oneness. The meaning of ”مالِكَ المُلْكِ“ is that Allah owns the servants and owns what they own. As for the meaning of ﴿تُؤْتِي المُلْكَ مَن تَشاءُ وتَنْـزِعُ المُلْكَ مِمَّنْ تَشاءُ﴾, there are two views on it: You give dominion — which is wealth, slaves and the court — to whom You will, and take it away from whom You will. And it was said: ”تُؤْتِي المُلْكَ مَن تَشاءُ“ by way of prevailing through religion and obedience; so Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made everything in the possession of a non-Muslim a possession of the Muslims as booty, and made them more entitled to all possessions than all the people of those who opposed the religion of Islam. «[Translator's note: the phrase «مِن كُلِّ أهْلٍ لِمَن خالَفُوا» is awkward in the Arabic; rendered according to its evident sense.]» It was said in the tafsīr that Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — commanded the Prophet ﷺ in these verses to ask Him to transfer the might of Persia to the Arabs and the abasement of the Arabs to Persia; and Allah knows best the truth of that.

As for the iʿrāb of ”اَللَّهُمَّ“: ḍamma on the hāʾ and fatḥa on the mīm; there is no disagreement among the grammarians about its pronunciation. As for the reason, the grammarians differed about it. One of them said: the meaning of the expression is ”يا اَللَّهُ أُمَّ بِخَيْرٍ“ (O Allah, aim [for us] with good). This is a great audacity, because in everything of this kind where a hamza has been dropped, most speech retains it: one says ”وَيْلَ أُمِّهِ“ and ”وَيْلُ امِّهِ“, and retaining the hamza is more common. Were it as he says, ”أُومِمْ“ and ”اَللَّهُ أُمَّ“ would be permissible, and the yāʾ of the vocative (yā al-nidāʾ) would have to accompany it necessarily, because the Arabs say ”يا اَللَّهُ اغْفِرْ لَنا“ (O Allah, forgive us); yet none of the Arabs has said anything but ”اَللَّهُمَّ“, and no one has said ”يا اَللَّهُمَّ“. Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَإذْ قالُوا اللَّهُمَّ إنْ كانَ هَذا هو الحَقَّ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 32], and said: ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ فاطِرَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾ [al-Zumar: 46]. So this view fails on several counts: one of them is that ”يا“ is not in the speech; another is that this omitted [element] has never been spoken in its original form, as we speak its like; and [another is] that what he mentioned is not placed before a supplication. He also claimed that the attribute (al-ṣifa) on the hāʾ is the ḍamma of the hamza that was in ”أُمَّ“. «[Translator's note: «الصفة» as printed; the sense requires "the ḍamma (vowel)".]» It is impossible that the ḍamma which is the indicator of the vocative of a single noun be abandoned, and that the ḍamma of ”أُمَّ“ be placed on ”اَللَّهُ“ — this is the state [of affairs] regarding the name of Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He. «[Translator's note: «هذا الحال في اسم الله» as printed; perhaps «هذا المحال» ("this is the impossibility") or «هذا إلحاد» ("this is a deviation regarding the name of Allah") was intended.]»

He also claimed that our saying ”هَلُمَّ“ is like that, its original being ”هَلْ أُمَّ“; whereas it is only ”لُمَّ“, with the hāʾ for drawing attention (tanbīh). The one arguing for this view said: ”يا“ is sometimes said with ”اَللَّهُمَّ“, so one says ”يا اَللَّهُمَّ“; but no one other than he transmits this from the Arabs. He claimed that one of them recited to him:
؎وَما عَلَيْكِ أنْ تَقُولِي كُلَّما ∗∗∗ صَلَّيْتِ أوْ سَبَّحْتِ يا اَللَّهُمَّ ما
؎اُرْدُدْ عَلَيْنا شَيْخَنا مُسَلَّما
(What harm is there for you in saying, whenever you pray or glorify: "O Allah, return our old man to us safe and sound"?)
But consensus — and what the Book of Allah the Exalted has brought, and what is found in the whole record (dīwān) of the Arabs — is not to be opposed by someone's saying: "one of them recited to me", when that "one" is neither known nor named.

Al-Khalīl, Sībawayh and all the grammarians whose knowledge is trusted said: ”اَللَّهُمَّ“ means ”يا اَللَّهُ“, and the doubled mīm is a substitute for ”يا“, because they did not find a yāʾ together with this mīm in [one] word, and they found the name of Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — used with ”يا“ when the mīm is not mentioned; so they knew that the mīm at the end of the word is equivalent to ”يا“ at its beginning. The ḍamma in it is the ḍamma of a single noun addressed in the vocative (munādā mufrad), and the mīm has fatḥa because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the mīm before it.

Sībawayh held that this noun cannot be qualified by an adjective, because the mīm has been joined to it. So he said — regarding His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ فاطِرَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾ [al-Zumar: 46] — that ”فاطِرَ“ is accusative as a vocative, and likewise ”مالِكَ المُلْكِ“, though he did not mention it in his Book. My view is that ”مالِكَ المُلْكِ“ is an adjective of ”اَللَّهُ“, and ”فاطِرَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ“ likewise; that is because the noun together with the mīm is equivalent to it together with ”يا“, so the adjective is not prevented with the mīm as it is prevented with ”يا“. «[Translator's note: the argument requires "just as it is not prevented with «يا»"; the text is translated as written.]»
This is the sum of the explanation and iʿrāb of ”اَللَّهُمَّ“.

The meaning of ﴿وَتَنْـزِعُ المُلْكَ مِمَّنْ تَشاءُ﴾ is according to what we mentioned regarding ”تُؤْتِي المُلْكَ مَن تَشاءُ“. The meaning of ﴿بِيَدِكَ الخَيْرُ﴾ is: in Your hand is all good, the good of this world and the good of the Hereafter.

zajjaj:27-27.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿تُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ في النَّهارِ وتُولِجُ النَّهارَ في اللَّيْلِ﴾: the meaning is: You make each of them enter the other. One says: ”وَلَجَ الشَّيْءُ - إذا دَخَلَ - يَلِجُ، وُلُوجًا، ووَلْجَةً“ (the thing entered); and ”اَلْوَلْجُ“ and ”اَلْوَلْجَةُ“ are something in front of a courtyard. So the meaning of ”تُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ في النَّهارِ“ is: You decrease the night and make that decrease enter the day as an increase, and You decrease the day and make that decrease enter the night as an increase.

﴿وَتُخْرِجُ الحَيَّ مِنَ المَيِّتِ﴾, i.e. You bring forth the human being from the sperm-drop and the bird from the egg, and You bring forth for people from the dead earth the grain by which they live. ﴿وَتُخْرِجُ المَيِّتَ مِنَ الحَيِّ﴾, i.e. You bring forth the sperm-drop from the human being and the egg from the bird. The meaning of ﴿وَتَرْزُقُ مَن تَشاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ﴾ is: without stinting. This is used in the language; it is said of one who spends liberally: ”فُلانٌ يُنْفِقُ بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ“ (so-and-so spends without reckoning), i.e. he is liberal with himself, as though he does not count what he spends.

zajjaj:28-28.t:
After this sanctification and magnification, Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — mentioned the affair of the hypocrites, saying: ﴿لا يَتَّخِذِ المُؤْمِنُونَ الكافِرِينَ﴾. The reading is with the jussive, with kasra on the dhāl because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Had you used the nominative, it would be a valid construction, saying: ”لا يَتَّخِذُ المُؤْمِنُونَ الكافِرِينَ أوْلِياءَ مِن دُونِ المُؤْمِنِينَ“. The meaning is that whoever is a believer ought not to take a disbeliever as an ally (walī), because the ally of a disbeliever is content with his disbelief, and so he is a disbeliever. Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿وَمَن يَتَوَلَّهم مِنكم فَإنَّهُ مِنهُمْ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 51], and said: ﴿والمُؤْمِنُونَ والمُؤْمِناتُ بَعْضُهم أوْلِياءُ بَعْضٍ﴾ [al-Tawba: 71].

The meaning of ”مِن دُونِ المُؤْمِنِينَ“ is: let him not grant alliance to one who is not a believer; i.e. let him not take up alliance from a place below (dūna) the place of the believers. This is speech that runs on the metaphor of place, as you say: ”زَيْدٌ دُونَكَ“ (Zayd is beneath you): you do not mean that he is in a low place and you in a raised place, but you have made nobility equivalent to elevation in place, and baseness like lowness in place. «[Translator's note: the printed text has «مُسْتَقِلٍّ» and «كالِاسْتِقْبالِ», evidently misprints for «مُسْتَفِلٍّ» (low) and «كالاسْتِفالِ» (lowness); rendered by the sense.]» So the meaning is that the elevated place in alliance is the place of the believers. This is the explanation of His saying ”مِن دُونِ المُؤْمِنِينَ“. The meaning of ﴿وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ فَلَيْسَ مِنَ اللَّهِ في شَيْءٍ﴾ is: whoever takes as allies other than the believers, Allah is quit of him.

﴿إلا أنْ تَتَّقُوا مِنهم تُقاةً﴾, and ”تَقِيَّةً“ — both have been read. So Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — permitted [an outward profession of] disbelief with al-qiṣṣa «[Translator's note: «القصة» as printed, evidently a misprint for «التقية» (precautionary dissimulation).]»; and ”اَلتَّقِيَّةُ“ is fear of being killed. However, this permission applies only with soundness of intention and fear of being killed.

﴿وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ وإلى اللَّهِ المَصِيرُ﴾: the meaning of ”نَفْسَهُ“ is ”إيّاهُ“ (Himself), except that here nafs suffices in place of ”إيّاهُ“, and that is [normal] speech. As for His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿تَعْلَمُ ما في نَفْسِي ولا أعْلَمُ ما في نَفْسِكَ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 116], it is among the things by which the servants are addressed according to the measure of their knowledge; its meaning is: You know what is with me and what is in my reality, and I do not know what is with You nor what is in Your reality.

In His saying: ﴿تُؤْتِي المُلْكَ مَن تَشاءُ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 26], i.e. You give dominion to whom You will to give it; and likewise ﴿وَتَنْـزِعُ المُلْكَ مِمَّنْ تَشاءُ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 26]: [from whom You will] to take it away; but it was omitted because there is in the speech what indicates it.

﴿يَوْمَ تَجِدُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 30] is accusative by His saying: ﴿وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 30], as if He said: ”وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ في ذَلِكَ اليَوْمِ“ (Allah warns you of Himself on that day). It is also possible that it is accusative on [the basis of] His saying: ﴿وَإلى اللَّهِ المَصِيرُ﴾ — on the day every soul finds. The first view is better.

zajjaj:81-81.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإذْ أخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثاقَ النَّبِيِّينَ﴾. The position of ”إذْ“ is accusative; the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "And mention in your narratives when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: 'Whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom…'" up to His saying ﴿لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ ولَتَنْصُرُنَّهُ﴾. ”ما“ here is of two kinds. It may be for condition and requital (sharṭ and jazāʾ), and this is the better of the two aspects, because the condition makes it necessary that everything that occurs of the affair of the messengers follows this course. The lām entered on ”ما“ just as it enters on the conditional ”إنْ“ when it is in the answer to an oath. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَلَئِنْ شِئْنا لَنَذْهَبَنَّ بِالَّذِي أوْحَيْنا إلَيْكَ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 86], and He said: ﴿قُلْ لَئِنِ اجْتَمَعَتِ الإنْسُ والجِنُّ عَلى أنْ يَأْتُوا بِمِثْلِ هَذا القُرْآنِ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 88]. The lām on ”إنْ“ entered as an emphasiser, paving the way for the lām of the oath; and the lām of the oath is the one that belongs to the oath itself, because in your saying ”واللَّهِ لَئِنْ جِئْتَنِي لَأُكْرِمَنَّكَ“ ("By Allah, if you come to me I shall surely honour you"), your swearing is only on your own action, except that the condition is attached to it; for that reason the lām entered on the condition. If ”ما“ has the sense of requital (i.e. is conditional), its position is accusative by His saying ”لَما آتَيْتُكم“, and the requital (apodosis) is His saying ”لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ“.
It is also possible that it is in the sense of ”اَلَّذِي“ (a relative noun), and its position would be nominative. The meaning: Allah took their covenant, i.e. made them swear: "Surely that which I have given you" — and the meaning is "which I have given you, you shall surely believe in him". So ”ما“ would be in the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ would be ”لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ“; the (resumptive) hāʾ was omitted from ”لَما آتَيْتُكم“ because of the length of the noun (with its ṣila). So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that He had charged every messenger to believe in the other messengers, so that the covenant came to embrace the whole group: that they believe in one another and help one another. The meaning of His saying ﴿فاشْهَدُوا وأنا مَعَكم مِنَ الشّاهِدِينَ﴾ is: make it clear, because the witness is the one who validates the claim of the claimant; and Allah's witness for the prophets is His making clear the matter of their prophethood by means of the miraculous signs.
It is also permissible — and it has been read so — ”لِما آتَيْتُكم“ (with kasra on the lām); then the lām with kasra is attached to His saying ”أخَذَ“; the meaning: He took the covenant because of His giving you the Book and wisdom. Some read: "لَمّا آتَيْناكم مِن كِتابٍ وحِكْمَةٍ", i.e. "when We gave you the Book and wisdom, the covenant was taken"; and the speech then resolves into requital, as you say "لَمّا جِئْتَنِي أكْرَمْتُكَ" ("when you came to me, I honoured you").

zajjaj:82-82.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَمَن تَوَلّى بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ﴾: ”ذَلِكَ“ is a pointing to the taking of the covenant, in meaning. ”فَمَن تَوَلّى“, that is: whoever turns away from faith after the covenant was taken from the prophets — and taking the covenant from the prophets includes taking it from their communities — i.e. whoever turns away after the taking of the covenant and the appearance of the signs of the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الفاسِقُونَ﴾, that is: those who have departed from the right course and from the whole of faith. It is valid that ”هم“ here be a noun functioning as mubtadaʾ (subject) and ”اَلْفاسِقُونَ“ its khabar (predicate), with ”هم“ together with ”اَلْفاسِقُونَ“ being the khabar of ”أُولَئِكَ“. It is also valid that ”اَلْفاسِقُونَ“ be in the nominative by ”أُولَئِكَ“ (as its khabar), with ”هم“ a faṣl (separating pronoun), which is what the Kufans call ”اَلْعِمادَ“ (the support).

zajjaj:83-83.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أفَغَيْرَ دِينِ اللَّهِ يَبْغُونَ﴾, that is: is it other than the religion of Allah that they seek? For He has made clear that it is the religion of Allah, and that they disbelieved, resisted stubbornly and envied out of transgression, as Iblīs did.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلَهُ أسْلَمَ مَن في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ طَوْعًا وكَرْهًا﴾. It has come in the exegesis that all who are in the heavens submitted willingly, while some of those on earth submitted willingly and some unwillingly. Since the practice (sunna) regarding those of the polytheists whom it was obligatory to fight was that they be fought until they submit (to Islam), that was called "unwillingly", even though when one submits he submits obediently; but the means to it was by compulsion. ”طَوْعًا“ is in the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), as if: they submitted willing and compelled — just as you say ”جِئْتُكَ رَكْضًا، ومَشْيًا“ ("I came to you running and walking") and ”جِئْتُ راكِضًا، وماشِيًا“ ("I came running and walking"). It is also possible — and Allah knows best — that it is in the sense of: ”﴿وَلَهُ أسْلَمَ مَن في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ طَوْعًا وكَرْهًا﴾“, i.e. they are subject to Him in respect of the nature on which He created them and by which He governs them: no one can refuse a natural disposition on which he was formed, nor is he able to change it, whether he loves that disposition or dislikes it. ﴿وَإلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُونَ﴾ points to the truth of this view, because the meaning is: He began you according to His will, whether you wished it or refused, and He will resurrect you as He began you. So the interpretation is: "Do you seek other than the religion whose description is this?"

zajjaj:84-84.t: Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded the Prophet ﷺ and his community to say: ﴿آمَنّا بِاللَّهِ وما أُنْـزِلَ عَلَيْنا﴾, and to say and believe that they make no distinction among any of the messengers in believing in them — they do not disbelieve in some of them, as the Jews and the Christians did.

zajjaj:85-85.t: Allah made known that He does not accept any religion other than the religion of Islam, nor any deed except from its people. So He said, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَمَن يَبْتَغِ غَيْرَ الإسْلامِ دِينًا فَلَنْ يُقْبَلَ مِنهُ وهو في الآخِرَةِ مِنَ الخاسِرِينَ﴾. ”يَبْتَغِ“ is jussive (majzūm) by ”مَن“, and His saying ”فَلَنْ يُقْبَلَ مِنهُ“ is the answer (jawāb al-sharṭ, apodosis). The meaning of ”مِنَ الخاسِرِينَ“ is: among those who have lost their deeds. The evidence for that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أضَلَّ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ [Muḥammad: 1].

zajjaj:86-86.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿كَيْفَ يَهْدِي اللَّهُ قَوْمًا كَفَرُوا بَعْدَ إيمانِهِمْ وشَهِدُوا أنَّ الرَّسُولَ حَقٌّ﴾. It is said that it was revealed about some people who apostatised and then wanted to return to Islam while their intention was disbelief; so Allah made known that there is no way for their guidance, because they have deserved to go astray through their disbelief, since they disbelieved after the clear proofs which are evidence of the soundness of the matter of the Prophet ﷺ. It has also been said that it was revealed about the Jews, because they disbelieved in the Prophet ﷺ after having been — before he was sent — believers, bearing witness to his prophethood; then when he (peace be upon him) was sent and brought them the miraculous signs, and told them what was in their books, which they could not repel, while he was unlettered, they disbelieved in him out of transgression and envy.

zajjaj:87-87.t: So Allah made known that their recompense is the curse, and He said: ﴿أُولَئِكَ جَزاؤُهم أنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةَ اللَّهِ والمَلائِكَةِ والنّاسِ أجْمَعِينَ﴾. The meaning of all people cursing them is that on the Day of Resurrection some of them will curse others, and whoever opposed them will curse them. The interpretation of Allah's curse upon them is His distancing them from His mercy and from His praise of them, because of their disbelief. The meaning of ”خالِدِينَ فِيها أبَدًا“ is: in what the curse entails, i.e. in the punishment of the curse. ﴿لا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمُ العَذابُ ولا هم يُنْظَرُونَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 88], that is: they will not be given a delay beyond the appointed time.

zajjaj:89-89.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ تابُوا مِن بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ وأصْلَحُوا﴾, that is: they made it known that they had been in misguidance, and set right what they had corrupted and by which they had deceived those who followed them from among those who had no knowledge. ﴿فَإنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that it is part of the vastness of His mercy and His bounty that He forgives one who has dared against Him with this daring — because this is something beyond which there is no further limit, namely that he disbelieved after the truth had become clear.

zajjaj:90-90.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بَعْدَ إيمانِهِمْ ثُمَّ ازْدادُوا كُفْرًا لَنْ تُقْبَلَ تَوْبَتُهم وأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الضّالُّونَ﴾. It is said in the exegesis that these are the band who apostatised after their Islam, then made a show of wanting to return to Islam; so Allah exposed their affair, because they made a show of returning to Islam while disbelief was in them. The evidence for that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الضّالُّونَ﴾, because had they been genuine in repentance they would not be transgressors; and that is indicated by [Translator's note: the source text breaks off here.]

zajjaj:141-141.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلِيُمَحِّصَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ويَمْحَقَ الكافِرِينَ﴾ — the meaning is: Allah made the days alternate among people, in order to purge the believers through what befalls them of being killed in their battle, or pain, or loss of wealth, and to annihilate the disbelievers, i.e. to uproot them. It is also possible that "He annihilates them" means: He nullifies their deeds. The interpretation of "اَلْمَحْصُ" in the language is: cleansing and freeing. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd (al-Mubarrad), may Allah have mercy on him, said: one says "مَحَصَ الحَبْلُ مَحْصًا" when the fibres go from a rope until it becomes smooth (slippery); "حَبْلٌ مَحِصٌ" or "مَلِصٌ" have one meaning. He said: the interpretation of people's saying "مَحِّصْ عَنّا ذُنُوبَنا" is: remove from us the sins that cling to us. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd informed us that Ḥunayf al-Ḥanātim came to a water called "طُوَيْلِعٌ" (Ṭuwayliʿ) and said: "By Allah, you are slippery of rope (maḥiṣ al-rishāʾ), far of drawing, overshadowing enemies; and if you asked me for the necks of camels, I would give them to you" — i.e. even if the necks of the camels were cut through (with fatigue) on the way to you, I would head for you. The meaning of "مَحِصُ الرِّشاءِ" is: it is pure clay, so the well-rope slips out of the hand. So the meaning of "يُمَحِّصُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا" is: He frees them from sins. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, may Allah have mercy on him, also said, as did others among the lexicographers: "مَحَصَ الظَّبْيُ، يَمْحَصُ" when the gazelle runs very fast. He alone said: its interpretation is that it does not mix its intensity in running with any slackening or languor. Another said: "مَحَصَ الظَّبْيُ، يَمْحَصُ، ومَحِصَ" have one meaning: when it runs a run in which it almost gives out from its intensity. And one says: "It is desirable in a horse that its legs be purged (tumaḥḥaṣ)", i.e. freed from flabbiness. Abū Isḥāq (al-Zajjāj) said: and I also read to him (the report) from al-Khalīl: "اَلْمَحْصُ" is freeing; one says "مَحَصْتُ الشَّيْءَ، أمْحَصُهُ، مَحْصًا" when I free it (from impurity). Some of the lexicographers said: "وَلِيُمَحِّصَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا" means: and so that Allah may purge the sins of those who believe — but they did not tell what the reality of maḥṣ is.

zajjaj:142-142.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أنْ تَدْخُلُوا الجَنَّةَ ولَمّا يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ جاهَدُوا مِنكم ويَعْلَمَ الصّابِرِينَ﴾ — al-Ḥasan read it "وَيَعْلَمِ الصّابِرِينَ" with kasra, by conjunction (ʿaṭf); and whoever read "وَيَعْلَمَ الصّابِرِينَ" (has it) accusative by the wāw. The meaning is: knowledge of the striving and knowledge of the patience of the patient has not yet occurred, and Allah has not yet known that as actually occurring from them — because He, Majestic and Mighty is He, knows it as unseen, and He only recompenses them for their deeds. The interpretation of "لَمّا" is that it is the reply to someone's saying "قَدْ فَعَلَ فُلانٌ" ("So-and-so has done (it)"), whose reply is "لَمّا يَفْعَلْ" ("he has not yet done it"); when he says "فَعَلَ" ("he did"), its reply is "لَمْ يَفْعَلْ" ("he did not do"); when he says "لَقَدْ" [Translator's note: so in the printed text; the reply that follows suggests something like "لَيَفْعَلَنَّ" or "هو يَفْعَلُ" is intended.], its reply is "ما يَفْعَلُ"; as though he said "واللَّهِ هو يَفْعَلُ" ("by Allah, he is doing"), intending the future — then its reply is "لَنْ يَفْعَلَ" and "لا يَفْعَلُ". This is the doctrine of the grammarians.

zajjaj:143-143.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ كُنْتُمْ تَمَنَّوْنَ المَوْتَ مِن قَبْلِ أنْ تَلْقَوْهُ﴾, that is: you used to wish for fighting, which is the cause of death. The meaning is: you used to wish for the cause of death; that is because they used to wish that fighting be permitted to them. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ إلى الَّذِينَ قِيلَ لَهم كُفُّوا أيْدِيَكم وأقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وآتُوا الزَّكاةَ فَلَمّا كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ القِتالُ إذا فَرِيقٌ مِنهم يَخْشَوْنَ النّاسَ كَخَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ أوْ أشَدَّ خَشْيَةً﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 77].
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَقَدْ رَأيْتُمُوهُ وأنْتُمْ تَنْظُرُونَ﴾ — more than one view has been given on it. Al-Akhfash said: its meaning is tawkīd (emphasis). Some said: "while you were looking at Muhammad ﷺ". The meaning — and Allah knows best — is: you have seen it while being clear-sighted, as you say "I have seen such-and-such" with no blindness in your eyes, i.e. I saw it with real sight; and this goes back to the sense of emphasis.

zajjaj:144-144.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَما مُحَمَّدٌ إلا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ﴾, that is: messengers have passed away before him. The meaning is: he will die as the messengers before him died. ﴿أفَإنْ ماتَ أوْ قُتِلَ انْقَلَبْتُمْ عَلى أعْقابِكُمْ﴾, that is: you turned back from your religion. It is related that some of those present on the day of Uḥud apostatized, and some of them went off a distance of three days. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, made known that the messengers do not remain among their communities forever, and that it is obligatory to hold fast to what they brought, even if the messenger is lost through death or killing. The alif of interrogation has entered upon the particle of condition, while its meaning is entry upon the apodosis (al-jazāʾ); the meaning is: "Will you turn back on your heels if Muhammad dies or is killed?" Because the condition and the apodosis are each dependent on the other, the alif of interrogation entered upon the condition and conveyed the sense of entering upon the apodosis — just as when you say "هَلْ زَيْدٌ قائِمٌ؟" ("Is Zayd standing?"), you are asking only about his standing, not about who he is. Likewise your saying "ما زَيْدٌ قائِمًا" ("Zayd is not standing"): you negated only the standing and did not negate Zayd, but you put "ما" before "زَيْدٌ" so that it be known who it is from whom standing is negated. Likewise His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أفَإنْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الخالِدُونَ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 34].

zajjaj:145-145.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَما كانَ لِنَفْسٍ أنْ تَمُوتَ إلا بِإذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ — the meaning is: no soul was to die except by the permission of Allah.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كِتابًا مُؤَجَّلا﴾ is by way of tawkīd (emphasis); the meaning is: Allah has written that as a decree with a term (kitāban muʾajjalan), i.e. a decree having a term; "اَلْأجَلُ" is the appointed time. Like this emphasis is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كِتابَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 24], because when He said ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكم أُمَّهاتُكم وبَناتُكُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 23], that indicated that it is prescribed for them, so His saying ﴿كِتابَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 24] was emphasis. Likewise His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿صُنْعَ اللَّهِ الَّذِي أتْقَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾ [al-Naml: 88], because when He said ﴿وَتَرى الجِبالَ تَحْسَبُها جامِدَةً وهي تَمُرُّ مَرَّ السَّحابِ﴾ [al-Naml: 88], that indicated that it is Allah's creation and making, so He said ﴿صُنْعَ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Naml: 88]. This occurs in the Quran in more than one place, and this is how it is treated by all the grammarians.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن يُرِدْ ثَوابَ الدُّنْيا نُؤْتِهِ مِنها ومَن يُرِدْ ثَوابَ الآخِرَةِ نُؤْتِهِ مِنها﴾, that is: whoever aims with his deed only at this world is given of it — and every blessing the servant is in is a favour from Allah, a giving from Him — and whoever's aim with his deed is the Hereafter, Allah gives him of it. There is no proof in this that He deprives him of the good of this world, because He did not say "and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We give him only of it". And Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is the Possessor of great bounty.

zajjaj:146-146.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَأيِّنْ مِن نَبِيٍّ قاتَلَ مَعَهُ رِبِّيُّونَ﴾ — its explanation is: "how many a prophet" (kam min nabiyy). There are two good, fully eloquent dialectal forms of it, and both are read: it is read "وَكَأيِّنْ" with doubling, and "وَكائِنٍ" on the pattern "فاعِلٍ"; most poetry has come in this latter form. Jarīr said:
؎وَكائِنٍ بِالأباطِحِ مِن صَدِيقٍ ∗∗∗ يَرانِي لَوْ أُصِبْتُ هو المُصابا
(How many a friend in the valleys of al-Abāṭiḥ would, if I were struck down, see himself as the one struck!)
And the poet also said:
؎وَكائِنٍ رَدَدْنا عَنْكُمُ مِن مُدَجَّجٍ ∗∗∗ يَجِيءُ أمامَ الألْفِ يُرْدى مُقَنَّعا
(How many a fully armed warrior we have repelled from you, coming before the thousand, striding along helmeted!)
And an example of the doubled form is his saying:
؎كَأيِّنْ في المَعاشِرِ مِن أُناسٍ ∗∗∗ أخُوهم فَوْقَهم وهُمُ كِرامُ
(How many people among the clans have a brother above them, though they are noble!)
Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, made known that many of the prophets had a company fighting with them who did not weaken, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رِبِّيُّونَ كَثِيرٌ﴾ ﴿فَما وهَنُوا لِما أصابَهم في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وما ضَعُفُوا وما اسْتَكانُوا﴾. The meaning of "فَما وهَنُوا" is: they did not slacken; "وَما ضَعُفُوا": they did not shrink in cowardice from fighting their enemy; and the meaning of "ما اسْتَكانُوا" is: they did not submit to their enemy. It is read — and this is the more common — "رِبِّيُّونَ" with kasra on the rāʾ, and some read "رُبِّيُّونَ" with ḍamma on the rāʾ. It was said in the explanation of "رِبِّيُّونَ كَثِيرٌ" that they are the many multitudes; some said: a "رِبْوَةُ" is ten thousand; and it was said: the ribbiyyūn are the God-fearing scholars, patient in what befalls them for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. Both views are good and fine. It is read "قُتِلَ مَعَهُ" and "قاتَلَ مَعَهُ". Whoever read "قاتَلَ", the meaning is: they fought and did not weaken in their fighting. Whoever read "قُتِلَ", the best is that "قُتِلَ" refers to the prophet, upon him be peace; the meaning is: "How many a prophet was killed while with him were ribbiyyūn, and they did not weaken after his killing" — because those who weakened (at Uḥud) had imagined that the Prophet ﷺ had been killed, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that the godly ones (al-rabbāniyyūn) did not weaken after the killing of their prophet. And it is possible that "قُتِلَ" refers to the godly ones, and "فَما وهَنُوا" means: those of them who remained did not weaken.

zajjaj:147-147.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَما كانَ قَوْلَهم إلا أنْ قالُوا رَبَّنا اغْفِرْ لَنا ذُنُوبَنا﴾ — it is read "قَوْلَهم" in the accusative, and the noun (ism of kāna) is "إلّا أنْ قالُوا", so the meaning is: "Their saying was nothing but their seeking forgiveness", i.e. their saying "Forgive us." Whoever read it in the nominative made the khabar (predicate) of "كانَ" what comes after "إلّا". More common in speech is that the noun (ism) is what comes after "إلّا"; Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَما كانَ جَوابَ قَوْمِهِ إلا أنْ قالُوا﴾ [al-Naml: 56], ﴿ما كانَ حُجَّتَهم إلا أنْ قالُوا﴾ [al-Jāthiya: 25]. The meaning of ﴿وَثَبِّتْ أقْدامَنا﴾ is: make us firm in Your religion; and when He makes them firm in their religion, they stand firm in their battle. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَتَزِلَّ قَدَمٌ بَعْدَ ثُبُوتِها﴾ [al-Naḥl: 94]; the meaning is: "slip from the religion".

zajjaj:148-148.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَآتاهُمُ اللَّهُ ثَوابَ الدُّنْيا﴾, that is: He gave them victory and spoils; ﴿وَحُسْنَ ثَوابِ الآخِرَةِ﴾: forgiveness, and the everlasting bliss He has prepared for them.

zajjaj:150-150.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿بَلِ اللَّهُ مَوْلاكُمْ﴾, that is: He is your protector (walī); and if He is their protector, He is their helper: ﴿ألا إنَّ حِزْبَ اللَّهِ هُمُ المُفْلِحُونَ﴾ [al-Mujādila: 22].

zajjaj:151-151.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿سَنُلْقِي في قُلُوبِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الرُّعْبَ﴾ — it is related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "«I have been given victory through terror»", and he said: "«My enemy is struck with terror of me from a month's journey away»". And Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said in Sūrat al-Ḥashr: ﴿وَقَذَفَ في قُلُوبِهِمُ الرُّعْبَ﴾ [al-Ḥashr: 2].
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بِما أشْرَكُوا بِاللَّهِ ما لَمْ يُنَـزِّلْ بِهِ سُلْطانًا﴾, that is: they associated with Him that for which He sent down no proof. "اَلسُّلْطانُ" in the language is proof. Its like is: ﴿ما أغْنى عَنِّي مالِيَهْ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 28] ﴿هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطانِيَهْ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 29], i.e. "its proof-force (ḥujjiyyatuhu) has gone from me" [Translator's note: so in the printed text ("حُجِّيَّتُهُ"); the sense is "my proof has gone from me".].

zajjaj:152-152.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إذْ تَحُسُّونَهم بِإذْنِهِ﴾ — its meaning is: you were uprooting them by killing. One says: "حَسَّهُمُ القائِدُ، يَحُسُّهم حَسًّا" when the commander kills them. One says: "هَلْ حَسَسْتَ كَذا وكَذا؟", i.e. did you see it or come to know of it? And one says: "ما حَسَسْتَ فُلانًا؟" and "هَلْ حَسَسْتَ لَهُ؟" — and the kasra is more common [Translator's note: i.e. presumably حَسِسْتَ.] — meaning: did you not feel tender toward him or have mercy on him? And one says: "جِيءَ بِهِ مِن حِسِّكَ وبَسِّكَ" ("bring it from your ḥiss and your biss"), i.e. from wherever it may be or may not be — such is the wording of al-Aṣmaʿī; its interpretation is: bring it from wherever one of your senses can perceive it, or one of your efforts can reach it. The meaning of "بِإذْنِهِ" is: by His knowledge.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿حَتّى إذا فَشِلْتُمْ﴾, that is: you lost courage before your enemy; ﴿وَتَنازَعْتُمْ﴾: you disagreed; ﴿مِن بَعْدِ ما أراكم ما تُحِبُّونَ﴾ — because they were given victory and then disobeyed what they were told in their battle, so they were punished by having the turn of fortune go against them.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿مِنكم مَن يُرِيدُ الدُّنْيا﴾, that is: among you is one whose aim in his fighting is the spoils; ﴿وَمِنكم مَن يُرِيدُ الآخِرَةَ﴾, that is: one who aims in his fighting at what is with Allah.

zajjaj:153-153.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَفا عَنْكم واللَّهُ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَلى المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 152] ﴿إذْ تُصْعِدُونَ﴾ — and "تَصْعَدُونَ": both have been read. Whoever said "تُصْعِدُونَ" — it applies to anyone who begins a journey from a place: he has "أصْعَدَ" (set out); whereas ascending (al-ṣuʿūd) is only from below to above. Whoever read "تَصْعَدُونَ", the meaning is: when you were climbing up the mountain, and turning aside for no one.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأثابَكم غَمًّا بِغَمٍّ﴾, that is: He requited you — for your having grieved the Prophet ﷺ — with grief befalling you, through what you were punished with for disobedience. Some said: "غَمًّا بِغَمٍّ" (grief upon grief) is Khālid ibn al-Walīd's appearing over them after what had befallen them.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لِكَيْلا تَحْزَنُوا عَلى ما فاتَكُمْ﴾ — of spoils — ﴿وَلا ما أصابَكُمْ﴾, that is: so that your grief would be only for having disobeyed the Prophet ﷺ.

zajjaj:31-31.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿قُلْ إنْ كُنْتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ اللَّهَ﴾: the reading is with ḍamma on the tāʾ. ”تَحِبُّونَ“ is permissible in the language, but ”تُحِبُّونَ“ is more common, because ”حَبَبْتُ“ is rare in the language; al-Kisāʾī held that it is a dialect that has died out, as far as he reckoned. The meaning of ”تُحِبُّونَ اللَّهَ“ is: you aim at obeying Him and are content with His laws. Love (maḥabba) is of several kinds: love in the sense of pleasures, in food, drink and women; love from Allah for His creation, which is His pardoning them and His bestowing favour on them through His mercy and forgiveness and praising them well; and the love of a human being for Allah and His Messenger, which is his obedience to them both and his contentment with what Allah commanded and what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ brought.

His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿يَغْفِرْ لَكم ذُنُوبَكُمْ﴾ [al-Ṣaff: 12] «[Translator's note: the reference as printed; the phrase discussed in this verse (Āl ʿImrān 31) is ﴿وَيَغْفِرْ لَكم ذُنُوبَكُمْ﴾.]»: the reading is with the rāʾ pronounced distinctly before the lām. One of the grammarians held that the rāʾ may be assimilated into the lām, so that ”وَيَغْفِر لَّكم“ would be permissible. This is a gross error, and I know of no one who read it so except Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ; and I reckon that those who transmitted from Abū ʿAmr the assimilation of rāʾ into lām were mistaken. It is an error in Arabic, because the lām is assimilated into the rāʾ, and the nūn is assimilated into the rāʾ, as in your saying ”هَل رَّأيْتَ؟“ (did you see?) and ”مَن رَّأيْتَ؟“ (whom did you see?); but the rāʾ is not assimilated into the lām when you say ”مُرْ لِي بِشَيْءٍ“ (order something for me), because the rāʾ is a repeated (trilled) letter, and if it were assimilated into the lām the repetition would be lost. This is the consensus of the grammarians whose knowledge is trusted.

zajjaj:32-32.t: His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿قُلْ أطِيعُوا اللَّهَ والرَّسُولَ﴾, i.e. show your love for Allah — if you love Him — by obeying Him and following His Messenger. The meaning of ﴿فَإنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الكافِرِينَ﴾ is: Allah does not love them, because whoever turns away from the Prophet ﷺ has turned away from Allah. The meaning of ”لا يُحِبُّ الكافِرِينَ“ is: He does not forgive them and does not praise them with good.

zajjaj:33-33.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفى آدَمَ ونُوحًا وآلَ إبْراهِيمَ وآلَ عِمْرانَ عَلى العالَمِينَ﴾: the meaning of ”اِصْطَفاهم“ in the language is: He chose them, i.e. made them the pure elite (ṣafwa) of His creation. This is a likening to what is seen, because the Arabs liken what is known to a visible thing, so that when the hearer hears that known thing, it is for him like what he witnesses with his own eyes. We identify the pure (ṣāfī) thing as that which is clear of turbidity; likewise the ṣafwa of Allah from His creation. There are three dialectal forms of it: ”صَفْوَةٌ“, ”صِفْوَةٌ“ and ”صُفْوَةٌ“. They are those in whom there is no stain from any angle, in religion and goodness.

Two views have been given on the meaning of ”اِصْطَفاهم“. Some said: He chose their religion, i.e. preferred it over all other religions, because the religion of this group is Islam, and Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿إنَّ الدِّينَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الإسْلامُ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 19]. Others said: He chose Adam with the mission to the angels and to his offspring, and chose Noah and Abraham and his family with the mission. Do you not see His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿يا آدَمُ أنْبِئْهم بِأسْمائِهِمْ﴾ [al-Baqara: 33]? So Allah the Exalted commanded him to convey [knowledge] from Him to His angels. And ”آلُ عِمْرانَ“ are the family of Abraham.

zajjaj:34-34.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿ذُرِّيَّةً بَعْضُها مِن بَعْضٍ﴾: the meaning is: He chose offspring, some of them from others; so the accusative of ”ذُرِّيَّةً“ is as a badal (substitute). It is also permissible for it to be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the meaning being: ”واصْطَفاهم في حالِ كَوْنِ بَعْضِهِمْ مِن بَعْضٍ“ (and He chose them while some of them were from others).

As for ”ذُرِّيَّةً“, the grammarians said: it is ”فُعْلِيَّةٌ“ from ”اَلذَّرُّ“ (tiny ants/particles), because Allah brought forth creation from the loins of Adam like tiny particles and made them bear witness over themselves: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes". One of the grammarians said: the original of ”ذُرِّيَّةً“ is ”ذُرُّورَةٌ“, on the pattern ”فُعُّولَةٌ“; but when the doubling became excessive, [a yāʾ] was substituted for the last rāʾ, so it became ”ذُرِّوْيَةٌ“; then the wāw was assimilated into the yāʾ, and it became ”ذُرِّيَّةٌ“. The first view is more analogical and better according to the grammarians.

zajjaj:35-35.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿إذْ قالَتِ امْرَأتُ عِمْرانَ رَبِّ إنِّي نَذَرْتُ لَكَ ما في بَطْنِي مُحَرَّرًا﴾: Abū ʿUbayda said: its meaning is ”قالَتِ امْرَأةُ عِمْرانَ“, and ”إذْ“ is redundant (laghw); and likewise ﴿وَإذْ قالَتِ المَلائِكَةُ يا مَرْيَمُ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 42] — he said: its meaning is ”وَقالَتْ“. Abū ʿUbayda achieved nothing in this. All the grammarians said that ”إذْ“ indicates past time; so how can what indicates past time be redundant, when it is a noun together with what follows it? Others besides Abū ʿUbayda — among them Abū l-Ḥasan al-Akhfash and Abū l-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] — said: the meaning is: remember when the wife of ʿImrān said. In my view the meaning — and Allah knows best — is other than what this group held: what governs ”إذْ قالَتْ“ is the sense of choosing (al-iṣṭifāʾ). The meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "And He chose the family of ʿImrān when the wife of ʿImrān said: My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated; and He chose them when the angels said: O Mary, Allah has chosen you". The mention of ”اِصْطَفاكِ“ indicates what we have described, and the meaning of ”نَذَرْتُ“ indicates what we have described.

The meaning of ﴿نَذَرْتُ لَكَ ما في بَطْنِي مُحَرَّرًا﴾ is: I have made it a servant who serves in our places of worship. That was permissible for them, and it was obligatory on their children to obey them in their vow; so a man would vow concerning his child that he be a servant in his place of worship and for their worshippers. That vow was not made concerning females; it was only made concerning males.

zajjaj:36-36.t:
When the wife of ʿImrān gave birth to Mary, she said: ﴿رَبِّ إنِّي وضَعْتُها أُنْثى﴾, and a female was not among what was suitable for the vow. So Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made among the signs in Mary — for what Allah intended concerning the affair of Jesus — that He made her accepted in the vow. He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿فَتَقَبَّلَها رَبُّها بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍ وأنْبَتَها نَباتًا حَسَنًا﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 37]. The original in Arabic would be ”بِتَقَبُّلٍ حَسَنٍ“, but ”قَبُولٍ“ is construed on [the sense of] ”قَبِلَها قَبُولًا حَسَنًا“ (He accepted her with a good acceptance).

One says: ”قَبِلْتُ الشَّيْءَ قَبُولًا حَسَنًا“, and ”قُبُولًا“ is also permissible, when I am pleased with it; ”قَبِلَتِ الرِّيحُ قَبُولًا“ (the wind blew as the east wind, qabūl), and ”هي تَقْبُلُ“; and ”قَبِلْتُ بِالرَّجُلِ أقْبَلُ قِبالَةً“, i.e. I stood surety for him; and ”قَبِلْتُ بِالرَّجُلِ“ has been transmitted in the sense of ”كَفَلْتُ بِهِ“ on the pattern ”فَعِلْتُ“. One says: so-and-so watered his camels qabalan, i.e. poured water into the trough while they were drinking from it, so it reached them. Of everything you see with your own eyes you say: ”أتانِي قُبُلًا“ (it came to me face to face), i.e. visibly. Everything that faces you is ”قَبْلٌ“ with fatḥa. You say: ”لا أُكَلِّمُكَ إلى عَشْرٍ مِن ذِي قِبَلٍ، وقَبَلٍ“ (I will not speak to you for ten [days] henceforth); the meaning [of qabal] is: ten from what we witness of these days, and the meaning of ”قَبِلٍ“ is: ten that we are facing. «[Translator's note: the vowelling of this passage («قَبَلَ إلى عَشَرٍ»، «قَبِلٍ») is uncertain in the printed text; translated as it stands.]» One says: ”قَبِلَتِ العَيْنُ، تَقْبَلُ، قُبَلًا“ (the eye squinted) when the gaze turns towards the nose.

His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿أوْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ العَذابُ قُبُلا﴾ [al-Kahf: 55], and qibalan and qabalan — all are permissible. Whoever reads ”قُبُلًا“, it is the plural of ”قَبِيلٌ“, ”قُبُلٌ“ being like ”رَغِيفَ“ and ”رُغُفٌ“; the meaning is: or the punishment comes to them in various kinds. Whoever reads ”قِبَلًا“ with kasra, the meaning is: or the punishment comes to them visibly. Whoever reads ”قَبَلًا“ with fatḥa, the meaning is: or the punishment comes to them facing [them]. And ”اَلْقَبْلَةُ“ — plural ”قَبْلٌ“ — is something resembling ”اَلْفَلْكَةُ“, i.e. the whorl of the spindle, which is [worn] on a necklace. «[Translator's note: the text says «جَمْعُ قَبْلٌ» ("the plural of qabl"); rendered as "plural qabl", which the sense requires.]»

The meaning of ﴿وَأنْبَتَها نَباتًا حَسَنًا﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 37] is: He made her growing up a good growing up. ”نَباتًا“ comes in a form other than that of ”أنْبَتَ“, on the sense of ”نَبَتَ نَباتًا حَسَنًا“ (she grew a good growth).

zajjaj:91-91.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وماتُوا وهم كُفّارٌ فَلَنْ يُقْبَلَ مِن أحَدِهِمْ مِلْءُ الأرْضِ ذَهَبًا﴾ — because the disbeliever who holds disbelief inwardly and displays faith outwardly is, before Allah, like the one who displays disbelief, since faith is assent (taṣdīq), and assent is only by intention. The meaning of ﴿فَلَنْ يُقْبَلَ مِن أحَدِهِمْ مِلْءُ الأرْضِ ذَهَبًا﴾ is: even if he did good and put forward the earth's fill of gold seeking nearness to Allah by it, that would not benefit him alongside his disbelief. Abū Isḥāq (al-Zajjāj) said: likewise, if he sought to ransom himself from the punishment with the earth's fill of gold, it would not be accepted from him. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that He does not reward them for their good deeds, nor does He accept from them a ransom from the punishment. Some grammarians said that the wāw is dropped (i.e. redundant); he said: the meaning is "the earth's fill of gold will not be accepted from any of them if he offers it as ransom". This is an error, because the benefit of the wāw is clear, and the wāw is not among what is treated as void.
One says ”مَلَأْتُ الشَّيْءَ أمْلَؤُهُ مَلْئًا“ ("I filled the thing"), the maṣdar (verbal noun) being with fatḥa and nothing else. Sībawayh and al-Khalīl said: ”اَلْمَلْءُ“ with fatḥa on the mīm is the act, and you say ”هَذا مَلْءُ هَذا“ [Translator's note: so vowelled in the text; the sense "the amount that fills it" is that of مِلْء with kasra], i.e. the amount that fills it — just as one says ”رَعَيْتُ رَعْيًا“ ("I grazed (the flock), a grazing"), while the property (livestock) is in the riʿy (pasture) [Translator's note: the text vowels the second word as اَلرَّعْيِ; the contrast drawn requires الرِّعْي, "pasture"]. So this is a clear difference. Some grammarians said: one says ”مَلَأْتُ مَلْئًا، ومُلْئًا“; this is a clear error, because what is described here is that if he owned the amount that fills the earth it would not be accepted from him; one does not say "the measure of doing", i.e. of filling the earth — what is offered to seek nearness is the gold which is the fill (milʾ) of the earth, not "that he should fill". One says ”مَلَأْتُ الشَّيْءَ مَلْئًا“, and ”قَدْ مُلِئَ فُلانٌ مَلَأً“ and ”هو مَمْلُوءٌ“ when he has a head cold. ”اَلْمَلَأُ“ are the nobles of a people. You say ”أنْتَ أمْلَأُ بِهَذا“, i.e. wealthier and more reliable; and ”رَجُلٌ مَلِيءٌ بَيِّنُ المَلاءَةِ يا هَذا“ ("a solvent man of evident solvency, O you"). As for what the scribes write, ”أنْتَ المَلِيُّ“ with yāʾ, it is a mistake — and they are unanimous on it; this is an error. ”اَلْمُلاءَةُ“, which is worn (a wrap), is with the long vowel. ”اَلْمُلاوَةُ مِنَ الدَّهْرِ“ is a long stretch of time; and from this is their saying ”أبْلِ جَدِيدًا، وتَمَلَّ حَبِيبًا“ ("wear out a new garment, and enjoy a beloved for long"), i.e. live with your beloved for a long time.
”ذَهَبًا“ is in the accusative as a tamyīz (specification). Sībawayh and all the Basrans said: the noun in the genitive (al-arḍ) has come between "gold" and "fill", preventing (gold) from being genitive. The true explanation of it is that the meaning is: what fills it of gold; and likewise when you say ”عِنْدِي عِشْرُونَ دِرْهَمًا“ ("I have twenty dirhams"), i.e. what equals this amount of dirhams.
It is also possible — and Allah knows best — that His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بَعْدَ إيمانِهِمْ ثُمَّ ازْدادُوا كُفْرًا لَنْ تُقْبَلَ تَوْبَتُهم وأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الضّالُّونَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 90] means the Jews, because they were repentant at the time of their believing in the Prophet ﷺ before he was sent; so Allah made known that that repentance and that faith are not accepted, because they disbelieved after it and increased in disbelief. For their disbelief in what was being sent down to the Prophet ﷺ time after time is an increase in disbelief, and likewise persisting in it is an increase in it.

zajjaj:92-92.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لَنْ تَنالُوا البِرَّ حَتّى تُنْفِقُوا مِمّا تُحِبُّونَ﴾. Some of them said: every good deed by which one seeks nearness to Allah is a spending. It is narrated from Ibn ʿUmar that he bought a slave-girl whom he had loved, and when he came to own her he freed her and did not take her. It was said to him: "You freed her after you had loved her, and did not take her?!" So he recited this verse: ﴿لَنْ تَنالُوا البِرَّ حَتّى تُنْفِقُوا﴾. This action of Ibn ʿUmar is one which people should follow, in not being niggardly with the most precious of what they own in seeking nearness by it to Allah the Exalted.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَما تُنْفِقُوا مِن شَيْءٍ فَإنَّ اللَّهَ بِهِ عَلِيمٌ﴾, that is: Allah will requite it, because He said: ﴿فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُ﴾ [al-Zalzala: 7]; so when he does it, he is requited for it. The interpretation of ”ما“ is that of condition and requital (sharṭ and jazāʾ), and its position is accusative by ”تُنْفِقُوا“ (as its object); the meaning: "And whatever thing you spend, Allah knows it." The fāʾ is the answer to the condition (jawāb al-sharṭ).

zajjaj:93-93.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿كُلُّ الطَّعامِ كانَ حِلا لِبَنِي إسْرائِيلَ إلا ما حَرَّمَ إسْرائِيلُ عَلى نَفْسِهِ﴾. The position of ”ما“ is accusative (as the excepted); the meaning: except the food which Isrāʾīl made unlawful for himself. It is narrated that he suffered a pain — and it has been said in the exegesis that this pain was sciatica — and he vowed that if Allah cured him he would give up the food and drink dearest to him; the food and drink dearest to him were the meat of camels and their milk. Then Allah made that unlawful for them because of their sins, as He said: ﴿فَبِظُلْمٍ مِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا حَرَّمْنا عَلَيْهِمْ طَيِّباتٍ أُحِلَّتْ لَهُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 160]. Allah made known that what Isrāʾīl made unlawful for himself was before the Torah was sent down. In this is the greatest sign for the Prophet ﷺ, because he informed them that they claim that there is in their Book what is not in it, and he called them, moreover, to bring their Book and recite it, so that he might make their lie clear to them; but they refused. Their refusal was evidence of their knowing that the Prophet ﷺ had spoken the truth in what he told them. Had they brought it, they would not have escaped one of two things: either they would add to it what was not in it at that time — and then some of them would know that it had been added to, or Allah would send down upon them a punishment that would expose their affair — or they would bring it in its entirety, and then the falsity of their claim about it would be known. So their story in this verse is like the story of the Christians in the mubāhala (mutual imprecation).

zajjaj:94-94.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَمَنِ افْتَرى عَلى اللَّهِ الكَذِبَ مِن بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ﴾, that is: after what we mentioned of the appearance of the proof concerning his fabrication, ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الظّالِمُونَ﴾.

zajjaj:96-96.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنَّ أوَّلَ بَيْتٍ وُضِعَ لِلنّاسِ لَلَّذِي بِبَكَّةَ مُبارَكًا﴾. It has been said that it is the first mosque established for people; and it has been said that it is the first house established for pilgrimage. It is said that it is the Frequented House (al-bayt al-maʿmūr), that the angels used to make pilgrimage to it before Ādam, and that it is the Ancient House. As for its building, there is no doubt that Ibrāhīm built it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَإذْ يَرْفَعُ إبْراهِيمُ القَواعِدَ مِنَ البَيْتِ وإسْماعِيلُ رَبَّنا تَقَبَّلْ مِنّا﴾ [al-Baqara: 127], i.e. "the two of them saying: Our Lord, accept from us".
As for (the House of) al-Maqdis, Sulaymān built it. The khabar (predicate) of ”إنَّ“ is ”لَلَّذِي بِبَكَّةَ“, and this is the lām of emphasis (lām al-tawkīd). It has been said that ”بَكَّةَ“ is the site of the House, and all that is around it is Makka. The consensus is that ”بَكَّةَ“ and ”مَكَّةَ“ are the place to which people make pilgrimage, and it is the town. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿بِبَطْنِ مَكَّةَ﴾ [al-Fatḥ: 24], and He said: ﴿لَلَّذِي بِبَكَّةَ مُبارَكًا﴾. As for its derivation in the language, the name may be derived from ”اَلْبَكُّ“, which is people's jostling (bakk) one another in circumambulation, i.e. pushing one another. It has also been said that it was called ”بَكَّةَ“ only because it breaks (tabukku) the necks of tyrants. ”مُبارَكًا“ is in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning: the one at Makka in the state of its blessedness. ﴿وَهُدًى لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾: it is possible that ”هُدًى لِلْعالَمِينَ“ is in the position of the nominative, the meaning being: and it is a guidance for the worlds.
As for ”مَكَّةُ“ with mīm, its derivation may be like the derivation of ”بَكَّةَ“, the mīm being substituted for the bāʾ, as one says ”ضَرْبَةٌ لازِبٌ، ولازِمٌ“ ("a binding blow"). The derivation may also be from their saying ”اِمْتَكَّ الفَصِيلُ ما في ضَرْعِ النّاقَةِ“ ("the weaned calf sucked out what was in the camel's udder"), when it sucks hard so as to leave nothing in it; then it would have been so named because of the intensity of crowding in it. The first view — I mean the substitution — is better.
The meaning of ”أوَّلَ“ (first) in the language, in reality, is the beginning of a thing. So it is possible that what is begun has a last, and possible that it has no last: one is the first of numbers, while numbers are unending; and the bliss of Paradise has a first, while it is never cut off. Your saying ”هَذا أوَّلُ مالٍ كَسَبْتُهُ“ ("this is the first wealth I have earned") is possible though there be no earning after it — rather, what you intend is "this is the beginning of my earning". And if someone said ”أوَّلُ عَبْدٍ أمْلِكُهُ فَهو حُرٌّ“ ("the first slave I own is free"), and he came to own a slave, that slave would be freed, because he has begun ownership. So it is possible that "the first house" is the house to which there was no pilgrimage other than it.

zajjaj:154-154.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ثُمَّ أنْـزَلَ عَلَيْكم مِن بَعْدِ الغَمِّ أمَنَةً نُعاسًا﴾, that is: after the terror that befell you, He made you secure with a security in which you could sleep, because one in intense fear can hardly sleep.
﴿أمَنَةً﴾ is a noun; you say "أمِنَ الرَّجُلُ أمْنًا، وأمَنَةً" when no fear reaches him. ﴿نُعاسًا﴾ is accusative as a badal (substitute) for "أمَنَةً". It is read "يَغْشى" and "تَغْشى طائِفَةً مِنكم": whoever read "يَغْشى" with yāʾ made it refer to the drowsiness (al-nuʿās), and whoever read "تَغْشى" with tāʾ made it refer to the security (al-amana), and the security conveys the meaning of drowsiness. If it were read "يُغْشى", it would be permissible. This party is the believers; ﴿وَطائِفَةٌ قَدْ أهَمَّتْهم أنْفُسُهُمْ﴾ — they are the hypocrites.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يَظُنُّونَ بِاللَّهِ غَيْرَ الحَقِّ﴾, that is: the hypocrites think that the cause of the Prophet ﷺ is dwindling away; ﴿ظَنَّ الجاهِلِيَّةِ﴾, that is: in this thought of theirs they are upon their Jāhiliyya. The reading is "وَطائِفَةٌ قَدْ أهَمَّتْهم أنْفُسُهم". Sībawayh said: the meaning is "when a party had become anxious about themselves", and this is the wāw of the ḥāl (circumstantial). Had it been read "وطائِفَةً قَدْ أهَمَّتْهم أنْفُسُهم" (accusative), on the basis of an implied verb "أهَمَّ" whose explanation appears overtly, it would be permissible; the meaning would be: "and their souls made a party anxious". It is also possible for it to be nominative with the khabar (predicate) being "يَظُنُّونَ" and "قَدْ أهَمَّتْهم" a naʿt (adjective) of "طائِفَةٌ"; the meaning: "and a party whom their souls make anxious think …", i.e. a party who think of Allah other than the truth.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ لَوْ كُنْتُمْ في بُيُوتِكُمْ﴾ — it is read "بِيُوتِكم" with ḍamma on the bāʾ and with kasra. Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh related it from ʿĀṣim with kasra on the bāʾ. Abū Isḥāq (al-Zajjāj) said: we read it according to the teaching of Abū ʿAmr from ʿĀṣim as "بُيُوتِكم" with ḍamma on the bāʾ, and the ḍamma is the more common and better. Those who give kasra in "بِيُوتٌ" do so because a yāʾ comes after the bāʾ; but "فِعُولٌ" is not a basic pattern in the language, nor one of the plural patterns, so the preferred form is "بُيُوتٌ", like "قَلْبٌ" / "قُلُوبٌ" and "فَلْسٌ" / "فُلُوسٌ".
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَبَرَزَ الَّذِينَ كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ القَتْلُ إلى مَضاجِعِهِمْ﴾ — the meaning of "بَرَزُوا" is: they went out to a "بِرازٌ", which is open ground; that is: the causes from which killing results would have brought them to their places of lying down (in death).
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلِيَبْتَلِيَ اللَّهُ ما في صُدُورِكُمْ﴾, that is: to test it through your deeds — for He knew it as unseen, so (now) He knows it as witnessed — because recompense falls upon what is known by witnessing, I mean: upon what has actually occurred from those who do it, not upon what is known of them (beforehand).
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ إنَّ الأمْرَ كُلَّهُ لِلَّهِ﴾ — whoever reads (كُلَّهُ) in the accusative does so as tawkīd (emphasis) of "اَلْأمْرَ"; whoever reads it in the nominative does so as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and "لِلَّهِ" is the khabar (predicate). The meaning of "the whole matter belongs to Allah" is: victory, and the terror He casts into hearts, belong to Allah — i.e. all of that belongs to Allah.

zajjaj:155-155.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوْا مِنكم يَوْمَ التَقى الجَمْعانِ﴾ — this is an address to the believers specifically. ﴿إنَّما اسْتَزَلَّهُمُ الشَّيْطانُ بِبَعْضِ ما كَسَبُوا﴾, that is: they did not turn away in their fighting by way of obstinacy, nor in fleeing from the advancing army out of desire for this world specifically; rather Satan reminded them of sins they had, so they disliked meeting Allah except in a state that would please them. For that reason He pardoned them. Otherwise the matter of fleeing and turning away in jihad — when the (enemy's) number is less than double, or the number is double — fleeing is a grave matter. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَمَن يُوَلِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ دُبُرَهُ إلا مُتَحَرِّفًا لِقِتالٍ أوْ مُتَحَيِّزًا إلى فِئَةٍ فَقَدْ باءَ بِغَضَبٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ ومَأْواهُ جَهَنَّمُ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 16]. This shows that the threat (of punishment) for the people of prayer is an established matter, and that turning away in battle is one of the greatest of the major sins.

zajjaj:156-156.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أوْ كانُوا غُزًّى﴾ — the reading, and what is established in the muṣḥaf, is with the short ending (qaṣr). "فُعَّلٌ" is a plural of "فاعِلٌ", e.g. "ضارِبٌ" / "ضُرَّبٌ" and "شاهِدٌ" / "شُهَّدٌ"; and it also comes on "فُعّالٌ", e.g. "حارِبٌ" / "حُرّابٌ" and "ضارِبٌ" / "ضُرّابٌ". "غُزّاءُ" is permissible, except that it does not occur in the reading, because it has the long ending (mamdūd).
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِيَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ ذَلِكَ حَسْرَةً في قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾, that is: so that He may make their supposition — that if they had not been present, and when they are not present at the battle, what was written for them would be averted from them — (a cause of regret), so that their regret over what befalls them is the more intense. ﴿واللَّهُ يُحْيِي ويُمِيتُ﴾, that is: a person's caution does not prevent his appointed term from coming to him according to what has preceded in Allah's knowledge.

zajjaj:159-159.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَبِما رَحْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ لِنْتَ لَهُمْ﴾ — "ما" here, by consensus of the grammarians, is ṣila (an added, connective particle), which does not prevent the bāʾ from governing what it governs. The meaning is: "So by mercy from Allah you were gentle with them", except that "ما", by its entry, has produced emphasis of the meaning. Had it been read "فَبِما رَحْمَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ" (nominative), it would be permissible, the meaning being "by that which is a mercy", just as they permitted "مَثَلًا ما بَعُوضَةٌ". But do not read it so, for reading is a sunna (an established practice), and it is not permissible for a reader to read with what the Companions, the Successors, or the well-known readers of the garrison cities did not read. The meaning is that your gentleness toward them is among what brings about their entry into the religion, because you bring them the proofs and demonstrations together with gentleness and a mighty character. ﴿وَلَوْ كُنْتَ فَظًّا غَلِيظَ القَلْبِ لانْفَضُّوا مِن حَوْلِكَ﴾ — "اَلْفَظُّ" is the rough-mannered one, of bad character. One says: "فَظَظْتَ، تَفِظُّ، فَظاظَةً، وفَظَظًا", except that "فَظاظَةً" is more common, because of the heaviness of the doubling. Nouns on "فَعَلٌ" in doubled roots are not assimilated, e.g. "اَلْمَدَدُ" and "اَلشَّرَرُ"; and what is on "فَعْلٌ" is assimilated in every case, e.g. "رَجُلٌ صَبٌّ" ("a passionate man"), whose origin is "صَبَبٌ", and likewise "فَظٌّ", whose origin is "فَظَظٌ" [Translator's note: the printed text has the pattern "فَعْلٌ" here, while the originals cited (صَبَبٌ، فَظَظٌ) and the non-doubled parallel (فَرِقٌ) point to the pattern فَعِل/فَعَل; the text is translated as printed.]. Its like among non-doubled roots is "قَدْ فَرَقْتَ، تَفْرَقُ، فَرَقًا" and "أنْتَ فَرِقٌ" ("you are fearful"). When a poet is constrained by metre, he restores "فَعْلًا" to its original form in doubled roots; the poet said:
؎مَهْلًا أعاذِلُ قَدْ جَرَّبْتَ مِن خُلُقِي ∗∗∗ أنِّي أجُودُ لِأقْوامٍ وقَدْ ضَنِنُوا
(Gently, O blamer! You have tested my character: I am generous to people even when they have been stingy.)
"اَلْفَظُّ" is also the water of the stomach (of a camel) and the dung, and it was called faẓẓ because of the coarseness of drinking it.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَشاوِرْهم في الأمْرِ﴾, that is: consult them in that in which you have no revelation; as for that in which there is a command from Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, and revelation, sharing opinions about it is ruled out.
