Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, only intended by that to establish the sunna of consultation, and that he honour his Companions by consulting them. Then, after agreement on the opinion, He commanded him ﷺ to rely on Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, saying: ﴿فَإذا عَزَمْتَ فَتَوَكَّلْ عَلى اللَّهِ﴾, that is: do not think that you will attain any attainment you love except through Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He.

zajjaj:161-161.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَما كانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أنْ يَغُلَّ﴾ — and "أنْ يُغَلَّ": both have been read. Whoever read "أنْ يَغُلَّ", the meaning is: "It is not for a prophet to betray his community." Its explanation is that the Prophet ﷺ gathered the spoils on a campaign, and a group of Muslims came to him and said: "Will you not divide our spoils among us?" He ﷺ said: "Even if you had with me the like of Uḥud in gold, I would not withhold a dirham from you. Do you think I would defraud you of your spoils?!" It is related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Let me not find a man coming on the Day of Resurrection with a sheep he took fraudulently, bleating; let me not find a man coming on the Day of Resurrection with a camel he took fraudulently, groaning; let me not find a man coming on the Day of Resurrection with a horse he took fraudulently, neighing." Whoever read "أنْ يُغَلَّ" — it is permissible in two ways [Translator's note: only the first is stated explicitly; the second appears to be the lexicographers' sense "to be accused of betrayal" given below.]: that is, it is not for a prophet that his companions defraud him, i.e. betray him; and it has come from the Prophet ﷺ: "Let none of you withhold a thread or a needle." The lexicographers permitted (for) "أنْ يُغَلَّ" (the sense) "to be charged with betrayal (yukhawwan)". One says: "أغْلَلْتُ الجِلْدَ" when I skinned it and left some fat on it; and "قَدْ غَلَّ الرَّجُلُ، يَغُلُّ" when he betrays, because he took something in secret. Everything of this root goes back to this. Of this is "اَلْغالُ", the valley that grows trees, whose plural is "غُلّانٌ"; of it is "اَلْغِلُّ", which is rancour; and you say "قَدْ أغَلَّتِ الضَّيْعَةُ", so it is "مُغِلَّةٌ", when the estate yields something while its capital remains. Zuhayr said:
؎فَتُغْلِلْ لَكم ما لا تُغِلُّ لِأهْلِها ∗∗∗ قُرًى بِالعِراقِ مِن قَفِيزٍ ودِرْهَمِ
(It will yield for you what villages in Iraq do not yield for their owners, of measures (qafīz) of grain and dirhams.)
"اَلْغِلالَةُ" is the garment worn under the clothes; that which is worn under the coat of mail — the iron mail — is (also) "غِلالَةٌ". "تَغَلَّلْتُ بِالغالِيَةِ" and "تَغَلَّيْتُ" ("I perfumed myself with ghāliya") mean only putting it at the roots of the hair. "اَلْغُلُّ" is the water that runs at the roots of trees. As for the meaning of ﴿وَقالُوا لإخْوانِهِمْ إذا ضَرَبُوا في الأرْضِ أوْ كانُوا غُزًّى﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 156]: the meaning of "إذا" here stands in for both past and future time. The basic function of "إذْ" is to indicate the past; you say "أتَيْتُكَ إذْ قُمْتَ" ("I came to you when you stood") and "آتِيكَ إذا جِئْتَنِي" ("I will come to you when you come to me"). He did not say here "إذْ ضَرَبُوا في الأرْضِ", because He intends that this is always their way. Its like in speech is: "فُلانٌ إذا حَدَّثَ صَدَقَ، وإذا ضُرِبَ صَبَرَ" ("So-and-so, when he speaks, speaks truly, and when he is struck, endures"): "إذا" is for the future, except that this future is judged for him only by what has been experienced of him in the past.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَشاوِرْهم في الأمْرِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 159] — one says "شاوَرْتُ الرَّجُلَ، مُشاوَرَةً، وشَوارًا" ("I consulted the man"), and whatever results from that is called "اَلْمَشُورَةُ"; some say "اَلشُّورَةُ". One says: "فُلانٌ حَسَنُ الصُّورَةِ والشُّورَةِ", i.e. of fine appearance and dress; and "إنَّهُ لَشَيِّرٌ صَيِّرٌ" ("he is handsome of form and appearance"), and "حَسَنُ الشّارَةِ" ("of fine outward look"). "اَلشُّوارُ" is household goods. The meaning of "شاوَرْتُ فُلانًا" is: I brought out in opinion what I had and what he had. "شُرْتُ الدّابَّةَ أشُورُها" is said when I test the riding beast and so learn its form in its gait. One says "شُرْتُ العَسَلَ" and "أشَرْتُ العَسَلَ" when I take honey from the places of the bees; and "عَسَلٌ مَشُورٌ" (gathered honey). Al-Aʿshā said:
؎كَأنَّ القَرَنْفُلَ والزَّنْجَبِي ∗∗∗ لَ باتا بِفِيها وأرْيًا مَشُورا
(As though clove and ginger had spent the night in her mouth, and gathered honey.)
"اَلْأرْيُ" is honey. One also says "عَسَلٌ مُشارٌ"; the poet said:
؎وَغِناءٍ يَأْذَنُ الشَّيْخُ لَهُ ∗∗∗ وحَدِيثٍ مِثْلُ ماذِيٍّ مُشارِ
(And singing to which the old man listens, and talk like pure, gathered honey.)

zajjaj:162-162.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أفَمَنِ اتَّبَعَ رِضْوانَ اللَّهِ﴾ — it is read "رِضْوانَ" with kasra on the rāʾ and "رُضْوانَ" with ḍamma on the rāʾ, and both have been related from ʿĀṣim. ﴿كَمَن باءَ بِسَخَطٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ — it is related that when the Prophet ﷺ commanded the Muslims at Uḥud to follow him, the believers followed him, and a group of the hypocrites stayed behind from him. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, made known that whoever follows the Prophet ﷺ has followed the good pleasure of Allah, and whoever stays behind from him has incurred anger from Allah. The meaning of "باءَ بِذَنْبِهِ" is: he bore it, and the sinner became the abode of the sin; hence "بَوَّأْتُ فُلانًا مَنزِلًا", i.e. I gave him a dwelling.

zajjaj:163-163.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿هم دَرَجاتٌ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾, that is: the believers are of a lofty rank, and the disbelievers are of a lowly rank with Allah. The meaning of "هم دَرَجاتٌ" is: they are possessors of ranks, because a human being is other than the rank — as you say "اَلنّاسُ طَبَقاتٌ" ("people are classes"), i.e. of (various) classes. Sībawayh recited:
؎أنُصْبٌ لِلْمَنِيَّةِ تَعْتَرِيهِمْ ∗∗∗ رِجالٌ أمْ هُمُ دَرَجُ السُّيُولِ
(Are they men set up as a target for death, which comes upon them, or are they (in) the path of the torrents?)
That is: they are of the path (daraj). And "أمْ هُمُ دَرَجَ السُّيُولِ" (accusative) is permissible, as an adverb (ẓarf).

zajjaj:164-164.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لَقَدْ مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلى المُؤْمِنِينَ إذْ بَعَثَ فِيهِمْ رَسُولا مِن أنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ — Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ as a messenger, a man of the unlettered, who did not recite a book nor write one with his right hand; and He sent him among a people who had experience of him and knew him for truthfulness and trustworthiness, and (knew) that he had not read a book nor been taught one. Then he recited to them the stories of the bygone nations and of the past prophets, and no book of the books of his opponents could refute his reports. So Allah made known that He conferred a favour upon the believers by sending one whose affair was already known, so that taking up the proof and demonstration, and accepting the reports and stories, was easy on his account; and in that is the greatest favour. It has come in the exegesis that a messenger from among the Arabs is meant. But if the point of that — and Allah knows best — were that the favour in his affair lay only in his being of the Arabs, then the non-Arabs would have no proof against them in it. Rather the matter — and Allah knows best — is that the favour in it is that his affair and his state had been experienced, his truthfulness was known, and he brought the proofs after they already knew that he was one of them.

zajjaj:165-165.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أوَلَمّا أصابَتْكم مُصِيبَةٌ قَدْ أصَبْتُمْ مِثْلَيْها﴾ — this wāw is the wāw of coordination (nasaq); the alif of interrogation has entered upon it, and it remained with fatḥa as it was before (the alif's) entry. Its like in speech is someone saying "So-and-so said such-and-such", and another says in reply: "أوَهُوَ مِمَّنْ يَقُولُ ذَلِكَ؟!" ("And is he one who would say that?!"). It was said in the exegesis: by this calamity is meant what befell them on the day of Uḥud; and "أصَبْتُمْ مِثْلَيْها": you inflicted on the day of Uḥud its like, and you inflicted on the day of Badr its like, so you inflicted twice what befell you. ﴿قُلْتُمْ أنّى هَذا﴾, that is: from where has this befallen us? ﴿قُلْ هو مِن عِنْدِ أنْفُسِكُمْ﴾, that is: it befell you through your disobeying the Prophet ﷺ. No people ever obeyed their prophet in their battle without being given victory, because when they obey, they are the party of Allah, and the party of Allah are the victorious.

zajjaj:166-166.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَبِإذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾, that is: what befell you was with Allah's knowledge; ﴿وَلِيَعْلَمَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ ﴿وَلِيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ نافَقُوا﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 167], that is: so that the faith of the believers may become manifest through their steadfastness in what befell them, and the hypocrisy of the hypocrites may become manifest through their losing heart and their little patience in what befalls them for the sake of Allah.

zajjaj:169-169.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أمْواتًا بَلْ أحْياءٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ يُرْزَقُونَ﴾ — the reading is with the nominative: "بَلْ أحْياءٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ". Had it been read "بَلْ أحْياءً عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ" (accusative), it would be permissible, the meaning being: "Rather, reckon them alive." More than one view has been given on this. Some said: "Do not reckon them dead in their religion; rather they are alive in their religion", as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿أوَمَن كانَ مَيْتًا فَأحْيَيْناهُ وجَعَلْنا لَهُ نُورًا يَمْشِي بِهِ في النّاسِ كَمَن مَثَلُهُ في الظُّلُماتِ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 122]. Some said: "Do not reckon them as the disbelievers say — that they will not be raised; rather they will be raised": ﴿بَلْ أحْياءٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ يُرْزَقُونَ﴾ ﴿فَرِحِينَ بِما آتاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 170]. And it was said: their spirits roam freely in the Garden and delight in its bliss, so they are alive with their Lord. Some said: their spirits are in the crops of green birds that roam freely in the Garden and then go to lamps beneath the Throne.

zajjaj:170-170.t: His saying, Exalted be His praise: ﴿وَيَسْتَبْشِرُونَ بِالَّذِينَ لَمْ يَلْحَقُوا بِهِمْ مِن خَلْفِهِمْ﴾, that is: who have not caught up with them in merit, except that they have great merit through their affirmation and their faith. ﴿ألا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ ولا هم يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ — the position of "أنْ" is genitive (khafḍ); the meaning is: they rejoice that there is no fear upon them, nor shall they grieve.

zajjaj:171-171.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُضِيعُ أجْرَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — "أنَّ" is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ); the meaning is: "and they rejoice that Allah does not let be lost …". "وَإنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُضِيعُ أجْرَ المُؤْمِنِينَ" (with kasra) is also permissible, in the sense of: "and Allah does not let the reward of the believers be lost". So it is in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh (ibn Masʿūd): "واللَّهُ لا يُضِيعُ", and this strengthens "وَإنَّ" with kasra.

zajjaj:172-172.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿الَّذِينَ اسْتَجابُوا لِلَّهِ والرَّسُولِ مِن بَعْدِ ما أصابَهُمُ القَرْحُ﴾, that is: after the wound had befallen them; whoever reads "اَلْقُرْحُ", its meaning is the pain of the wound. "اَلَّذِينَ" may be in the position of the genitive, as a naʿt (adjective) of "the believers"; but the better is that it be in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ being ﴿لِلَّذِينَ أحْسَنُوا مِنهم واتَّقَوْا أجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾.

zajjaj:173-173.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿الَّذِينَ قالَ لَهُمُ النّاسُ إنَّ النّاسَ قَدْ جَمَعُوا لَكُمْ﴾ — it is said in the exegesis that the one who said this was Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd al-Ashjaʿī; Abū Sufyān and his companions sent him to discourage the Prophet ﷺ and his companions from meeting them. On the day of Uḥud there had been an appointment between the Muslims and the polytheists to meet at "Badr al-Ṣughrā" (the Lesser Badr). The Muslims paid no attention to Nuʿaym's intimidation and resolved to meet the enemy, and they answered him by saying: ﴿حَسْبُنا اللَّهُ ونِعْمَ الوَكِيلُ﴾. The interpretation of "حَسْبُنا اللَّهُ" is: the One who suffices us against them is Allah.
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَزادَهم إيمانًا﴾, that is: that intimidation increased them in firmness in their religion and in perseverance in supporting their Prophet. They went to Badr al-Ṣughrā, and Allah cast terror into the hearts of the polytheists, so they did not take them unawares ("فَلَمْ يُغْفِلُوهم") [Translator's note: so in the printed text; the sense is evidently that the polytheists did not come out to meet them.].
